"Ten thousand years have passed. Cold ashes and withered wood have passed. The incense burner in the ancient temple has passed.
A single white silk ribbon has passed. I ask no more of the rest. What is this 'a single white silk ribbon passing'? Dazhu said, "This merely clarifies matters on the side of a single color.
The Master said, "So you still do not understand the meaning of our former teacher. Dazhu said, "Do you not approve of me? But..."
"Bring incense. "If you cannot leave when the incense smoke has ceased, you have not yet understood the meaning of the former master. Thereupon, he burned incense;
before the smoke had even faded, the Master had already left his seat. The Master patted the back of the seat and said, "To depart while seated or to pass away while standing is certainly possible."
I have not yet even dreamed of the meaning of my former teacher. A monk asked, "I have heard it said in antiquity: 'To succeed by turning outward is the rank of a minister;
to succeed by turning inward is the lineage of the king. Is this so? The Master said, "It is. The monk asked, "What is succeeding by turning outward?

The Master said, "If one does not know the ultimate limit of affairs, but merely manages them, this is called succeeding by turning outward; this constitutes the lineage of a minister. The monk asked, "What is [succeeding by turning inward]?"
“This is the inner succession. The Master said, “To know how to take responsibility and carry the burden within is what constitutes the inner succession.
[The student] asked, “What is the royal lineage? The Master said, “One must see the person who has no one to take responsibility for, the person who has no burden to carry;
only then does one attain the same color. Once the same color is attained, it is therefore metaphorically called ‘birth,’ which is the royal lineage. [The student] said, “If that is so, then...”
"Inner succession must also involve a turning over. The Master said, "It is evident that there is one who can receive and bear this responsibility; how could it not be turned over?
You say that 'inner succession' is the lineage of the human king. But tell me, is there still any principle of succession today?"

Therefore, the ancients said: "Inheriting is a matter of merit; having inherited, it is not a matter of merit. Once one has turned back from merit and entered the position, only then is one called a member of the royal lineage.

[The student] asked: "I do not yet know whether those who 'inherit from outside' also turn back or not? The Master said: "Those who inherit from outside have not yet realized that there even exists [a realm of] existence."
Furthermore, he was taught that there is something "to be known. [The student] asked, "What is this 'knowing that there is'?

The Master said, "At dawn, one does not realize it is light. [The student] asked, "What is external succession? The Master said, "Not borrowing another person's household affairs. [The student] asked, "What is internal succession?"
The Master said, "Pushing the father toward the interior. [The monk] asked, "Between these two phrases, which one is most intimate?

The Master said, "The subject is inside the gate; the king does not go out the gate. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then he who does not go out the gate does not fall into either extreme. The Master said:
He does not sit alone within the world; he succeeds the royal lineage, which is called the "external succession" (wai-shao) royal lineage.

Therefore it is said: succeeding as a minister of renown is "the partial within the correct" (pian-zhongzheng). Having succeeded, turning to become a ruler of renown is "the correct within the partial" (zheng-zhongpian).
Question: Does the one born [of the lineage] still know or hear anything? The Master said: Who else would know or hear? [The questioner] said: If that is so, then...
"Do not simply say 'yes' or 'no. The Master said, "If it were so, why did the ancients say, 'King Birth has a father'?
[The monk asked,] "Since he has a father, why does he not know or hear of him? The Master said, "At that very moment, he does not recognize his own ancestor.
[Another monk] asked, "An ancient said, 'Even one who comes directly without being like this is still a descendant. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The ancients..."
He did not speak falsely. [The monk] asked, "What is it like to be a descendant who has come? The Master said, "One still guards the precious treasure.
[The monk] asked, "What is it like to be the father? The Master said, "There is no house to sit in; there is no world to arise from. [Verse: Everyone asks for instruction;
I do not know what means the Master will use to rescue them. The Master said, "Do you say that even the great mountain has ever lacked a single inch of soil?"
[The student] said, "If that is so, then as one travels throughout the four seas in search [of the Way], what should one do? The Master said, "Yanjiao lost his head and his mind went mad.
[The student] asked, "Is there anyone who is not mad? The Master said, "Yes. [The student] asked, "Who is this one who is not mad?
The Master said, "Suddenly awakening on the road, yet with eyes still closed. [Verse]: Question: What is the student’s own self? Master: Even more...
[The student] asked, "Whom [did he ask]? [The Master] said, "If you respond thus at that moment, how would it be?

The Master said, "Sumeru must further support Sumeru. [Verse: Question: The patriarchs transmit to one another; what exactly do they transmit? The Master said: "Śākyamuni is stingy; Kāśyapa is wealthy. [The student] asked:
"What is Śākyamuni’s stinginess? The Master said: "He has nothing to give to others. [The student] asked: "What is Kāśyapa’s wealth? The Master said: ...
[The student] said, "Within our country there is Lord Mengchang; how would you say he ultimately transmits this matter?
The Master said, "An old man of a hundred years divides his night lamp. [Verse: When the various sages appear from time to time, they are merely people who transmit words.
Is this not the Master’s own words? The Master said, "Yes. [The student] said, "As for when the World-Honored One was born, pointing one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth..."
[The monk said: "The Earth! Above heaven and below heaven, only I am honored alone. For what reason is he called "the man who transmits the words"? The Master said:
"Because he points to heaven and points to earth, he is called 'the man who transmits the words. The monk bowed and withdrew.

[Verse] Questioning an ancient master: "Is it true that delusion is established based on the Real, and the Real is revealed through delusion? The Master said, "Yes. [The student] asked, "What is the True Mind?
The Master said, "That which is not mixed with food is it. [The student] asked, "What is the deluded mind? The Master said, "Grasping at conditions and giving rise to inversion is it.
[The student] asked, "Apart from these two paths, what is the Original Substance? The Master said, "The Original Substance is not separate [from them]. [The student] asked:
"Why do you not leave it? The Master said: "If one does not revere the Goddess of Merit, who would begrudge the Woman of Darkness?
[Verse]: Question: When the entire universe is examined, it is all but this single eye. What is the eye of the universe? The Master said: "The universe is contained within it."
[The questioner] asked, "Where is the Eye of Heaven and Earth? The Master said, "It is precisely this Eye of Heaven and Earth. [The questioner] asked, "Does it still illuminate or not?

The Master said, "It does not borrow the power of the three luminaries. [The questioner] asked, "If it does not rely on the power of the three luminaries, by what means is it called the Eye of Heaven and Earth?"
The Master said, "If it were not so, one would see countless ghosts and spirits before one's skull.

[Verse] He addressed the assembly, saying: "The eternally abiding Dharma-body is neither born nor extinguished. A monk asked, "Since it is neither born nor extinguished, why do beings transmigrate through the six realms?
The Master said, "It is because of the mind. The monk asked, "By what skillful means should one realize the Dharma-body? The Master said, "By means of emptiness..."
[The Master said: "The empty mind accords with the principle of space. [The student] asked, "What is it like after realization? The Master said, "Let it revolve within the three realms;

let it merely listen as the four modes of birth rush by. [The student] asked again, "Do you understand? [The student] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Prostrate yourself! [Added from another collection].
Chan Master Jingxin of Yongquan had been instructed by Shishuang and settled at Yongquan. One day, he ate his meal without wearing his monastic robe.
A monk asked, "Have you not become a layman? The Master said, "Is one not a monk right now?
[Verse] Two Zen practitioners, Qiang and De, saw the Master riding an ox along the road. Not recognizing him, they suddenly remarked, "The hooves and horns are quite distinct!"
Ming: "What can be done? The rider did not perceive. The Master spurred the ox and departed. Qiangde rested under a tree and brewed tea.
When the Master returned, he dismounted from the ox and asked, "Where have you two Chan guests recently come from? Qiang said, "From over there.
The Master asked, "What is the matter over there? Qiang lifted his tea cup. The Master said, "This is still a matter of 'this side.'"
"What is the matter with that side? [The monk] was unable to respond. The Master said, "Do not say that one who rides the ox does not look in the mirror.
[Another day] he ascended the hall and said: "I have been here for forty-nine years, and yet there are still times when I stumble.

You people must not open your mouths too wide. Those with intellectual understanding are many; those with both realization and practice are not one in ten thousand. Intellectual understanding is merely words."

You must know how to penetrate this. If consciousness is not exhausted, I dare say you will continue to transmigrate. Why is this so? It is because the outflows of consciousness have not been eliminated.
You need only exhaust them in the present moment, and only then can you achieve realization. This is also called "establishing merit within" (*li zhong gong*);

when you turn that merit over toward the Other, it is also called "merit within the approach" (*juzhong gong*). This is approaching the Other intimately. Therefore, I say: "Approach people, do not approach things."
He has attained liberation. Yet he does not liberate his own kin. Even such a metaphor you cannot yet comprehend; you fail to grasp the whole thing.
You merely manage to agitate your nature and move your tongue. Have you not seen Dongshan say: "Continuity is also very difficult"?
You must know that there is this matter. If you do not know it exists, there will be days of weeping ahead.
Chan Master Yungai Zhiyuan [Verse]: A monk asked Shishuang, "I do not ask about the time when ten thousand doors are all closed;
what is it like when ten thousand doors are all open? Shishuang said, "What about the matter within the hall? The monk had no reply.
After half a year, he finally offered this turning word: "No one can receive him. Shishuang said, "As for speaking, you speak quite well; however, you have only spoken..."
He attained eighty percent [of the realization]. He asked, "And what about the Master? Shuang said, "No one recognizes him. The Master understood and prostrated himself.
He requested that Shuang provide an illustration [of his realization], but Shuang was unwilling.

The Master then took Shuang by the arm and went up to the abbot’s quarters, saying, "If the Master does not speak, I shall strike the Master! Shuang said, "Go ahead. The Master prostrated repeatedly. Shuang said, "No one recognizes him."
The monk was suddenly enlightened upon hearing these words.
A monk asked Chan Master Nanji Sengyi, "I am fortunate to have gained your personal proximity; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "If I were to give you instruction, that would be a humiliation for you. The monk asked, "How then should a student of the Way proceed? The Master said, "Above all, avoid this."
"No. Question: "We do not ask about those of the same category. What is meant by 'those of a different category'? The Master said:
"If you want your head, they will chop it off and take it away. Chan Master Hongjian of Fushan [Verse]: A monk asked: "I come to the Master bearing my raw jade; will the Master receive me?
The Master struck the incense stand with his hand. The monk bowed. The Master said: "That you bow is not in vain, but as for the matter within it—what is it?"
The monk then struck the incense altar. The Master said, "Your tongue does not leave your mouth.
Chan Master Lüyuan Huī was asked by a monk, "The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another; I wonder what it is they transmit? The Master said, "I ask you; you ask me.
The monk said, "If that is so, then black and white cannot be distinguished. The Master said, "Where would it go?"
Come. Chan Master Shizhu of Fengxiang [Verse]: While traveling, he arrived at Dongshan. At that time, Master Qian uttered a phrase, saying:
"There are four kinds of people. One person speaks beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs, yet cannot take a single step. Another person walks beyond the Buddhas..."
The Patriarch said: "A single phrase cannot be spoken. One person can speak it and practice it; another cannot speak it and cannot practice it. Which of these is the true person?
The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said: "The one who says that even the Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot practice it."
It is simply that one who has no tongue is not permitted to walk; yet there is one who walks beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
It is simply that one who has no feet is not permitted to speak; yet there is one who can both speak and walk. This is simply a case of the box and its lid fitting perfectly.
One who cannot speak and cannot walk is like seeking life by severing one's own breath—this is a stone child wearing a cangue.
Daisō was wearing a lock. Shān asked, “How is it on the level of the *dàolǐ* (the teacher’s portion)? The Master said, "On the level of the *dàolǐ*, everything is encompassed and penetrating;
how could it not be manifest in its own excellence? Shān asked, "As for Minggong Xiù on the sea, how about him? The Master said, "Two illusory people meeting."
Clapping his hands, he laughed heartily.
Chan Master Xuantai of Mount Nanyue was grave and quiet, speaking seldom; he never wore silk, so people of the time called him "Tai the Hemp Robe.
When he first met Deshan, he ascended the Dharma hall. Later, he visited Shishuang and entered his room [as a disciple]. He served as the administrative director for twenty years.
In his later years, he became friends with Guanhui and Qiji. He subsequently resided at a hermitage called Jingangtai (Diamond Terrace), where he vowed never to establish formal disciples.
Those from all quarters who came as junior followers were received by him according to the etiquette of friendship.

Once, observing that Mount Heng was being severely damaged by local mountain dwellers who practiced slash-and-burn agriculture—clearing forests and burning fields—he composed the "Ballad of the Slash-and-Burn Mountain" (*Sheshan Yao*), which begins: "The child of the slash-and-burn mountain..."
The mountain child knows naught; year after year he hews away the green peaks of Mount Mei. Among them, the finest is the hue of Mount Heng;
the sharp axes of the cypress and pine crush their steadfast branches. The numinous birds and wild cranes have no place to rely; the white clouds retreat as the blue smoke flies.

The paths for monkeys and apes are cut off; from the cliffs and precipices, *zhī* fungi emerge. The roots of *yù* rhizomes are lost, yet the *máo* grasses flourish. Year after year, once harvested, they are weeded again;

though a thousand autumns pass, they can never return to their original state. It is further said that this year’s planting was not much, so next year they shall be felled once more on the sunny slopes.
If even the long-lived peaks of the realm are thus, one knows not how this principle may be resolved. This has been propagated far and wide.

The news reached the imperial palace, and an edict was issued to prohibit [the burning]. Consequently, no further fires spread to the monasteries within the mountain ranges; this was due to the Master’s efforts.
As he was about to manifest his passing, he summoned a monk and ordered him to prepare firewood, leaving behind a verse that said: "This year I am sixty-five."
The four great elements are about to depart from their master; his Way is naturally profound and mysterious. Within this state, there are no Buddhas and no patriarchs.

There is no need for tonsure, nor for bathing. A single mass of fierce fire—ten thousand needs satisfied, a hundred thousand needs fulfilled. He passed away sitting upright with one foot hanging down.
His remains were cremated and the relics collected; a stupa was erected beside Yingyun Pavilion.
A monk asked Zen Master Yungai of Tanzhou, "What is it like when one cannot fathom it with the ordinary mind? The Master said, "A tongueless child;
all cleverness and wit are exhausted. Fengxue went to visit him. The Master asked, "When the stone horn pierces the path through the clouds, what is your intention as you carry your staff?
Fengxue said, "Red clouds enshroud the jade elephant; the peaks embrace the streams and sources. The Master said, "You have come along with me. Fengxue—
[The Emperor] said, "The Abbot must also speak in a low voice. The Master said, "Please sit and drink tea.
Chan Master Longhu Pumen was the Crown Prince of Emperor Xizong of the Tang dynasty. From childhood he abstained from meat; as he grew up, he had no intention of governing the world.
Emperor Xizong doted on him, yet despite employing every means to mold and direct him, he could never change his mind. At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, Emperor Xizong...

He fled to Shu. The Master cut off his hair and wandered away, so that no one knew of him. He went to visit Shishuang and asked, "Will you be willing to transmit to me the matter of the Patriarch’s special transmission?
Shishuang said, "Do not slander the Patriarch. The Master said, "The fundamental principle of the world is vast and magnificent."
"Is this not a fabrication? Nanquan said, "This is an actual matter. The Master asked, "What is your own view, Master?
Nanquan said, "Wait until the mountain behind my desk nods its head, and then I shall tell you. At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
The Scholar Zhang Zhuo [Verse]: Because the Great Master Chan Yue directed him to study under Shishuang, Shishuang asked, “Scholar, what is your surname?
He replied, “My surname is Zhang and my name is Zhuo. Shishuang said, “Even seeking for the clever is unattainable; from where does the clumsy come?
The scholar suddenly attained realization and presented this verse: “Luminous, silent illumination pervades the Ganges sands; Ordinary beings, sages, and all sentient creatures share my home. One...”
When mindfulness does not arise, the whole body is fully revealed; as soon as the six sense organs stir, they are obscured by clouds. To sever afflictions is to increase one's illness once more;
to strive toward True Suchness is likewise a deviation. Flowing along with worldly conditions without hindrance, both nirvana and birth-and-death are equal to flowers in the sky.
The Chan Master Feitian Huijue was asked by a monk, "What is the name of this place? The Master said, "Feitian" (Fertile Field). The monk asked, "What should be planted here?
The Master then struck him. The Master had a verse that says: To cultivate many fine phrases is a waste of effort; Returning to the source is itself great folly.
Ancestral Buddhas are not attained through cultivation or realization; Even if one travels the profound path, it remains treacherous.

Chan Master Yuan’an of Luopu Mountain left home to become a monk at the age of eight and received full ordination. He was proficient in the sutras and treatises and went to Linji to inquire about the Way, subsequently serving as his attendant.
Linji once praised him before the assembly, saying, "In the gate of Linji, there is a single arrow; who dares to meet its point?
Having received this seal of approval, the Master considered himself sufficient. One day, while standing in attendance, a presiding lecturer (zuozhu) came to visit Linji.

Ji asked, "Suppose there is one person who clearly understands the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, and another person who does not clearly understand the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
Tell me, are these two people the same or different? The Master said, "If they have clear understanding, they are the same;
if they lack clear understanding, they are different. The Teacher said, "What place is this, where one speaks of 'same' or 'different'?"

Ji looked at the Master and said, "How about you? The Master then gave a shout. When Ji saw the Master off as he was returning the seat-holder, he asked him, "Was it not you who just now shouted at the old monk?
The Master replied, "It was. Ji then struck him. [Verse] Later, the Master took his leave of Ji.
Linji asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am going south. Linji drew a line with his staff and said, "If you can get past this, then go.
The Master then gave a shout. Linji struck him. The Master bowed and departed.
The next day, Linji ascended the hall and said, "In the gate of Linji there is a red carp; shaking its head and wagging its tail, it has gone south."
"I do not know who will be the one drowned in the pickle jar. Having finished his travels, the Master went straight to Jia Shan and established a hermitage there.
For a year he did not visit Jia Shan. Jia Shan then composed a letter and ordered a monk to deliver it. Upon receiving it, the Master sat down immediately;
then, extending his hand again, he asked for it. The monk had no reply. The Master struck him and said, "Go back and report this to the Abbot. The monk returned and related the incident.
"Similar. Shanshan said, "If this monk opens the letter, he will surely come within three days. If he does not open the letter, this man cannot be saved.
The Master indeed arrived after three days; seeing Jia Shan, he did not prostrate but instead stood facing him with his hands folded.
Shanshan said, "A rooster nesting in a phoenix's nest—this is no match for its kind. Get out! The Master said, "I have traveled from afar to pay my respects."
"Please grant me one reception," the Master requested. Yunmen said, "Before my eyes there is no *śrāmaṇera*; here there is no old monk. The Master then gave a shout. Yunmen said, "Wait, wait!
Do not be so hasty and reckless. The clouds and moon are the same; the streams and mountains are each different.
To cut off the tongues of all people under heaven—that is not impossible for you, *śrāmaṇera*. But how can you make a tongueless person speak? The Master stood there lost in thought. Yunmen—
He struck him immediately; from this, [Yunyan] took the teaching to heart. When the Master [Shitou Xiqian] was about to pass away, he spoke these words:
"The branch of Stonehead is coming to an end, look and see! Yunyan said, "Not so. The Master asked, "Why? Yunyan replied, "His family has its own green mountains."

Mount [Zhaozhou] said, "If it is truly so, then our school shall not fall into decline. He ascended the hall and said: "The final phrase at the very end is where one first arrives at the secure barrier;
it locks off the vital passageway, allowing neither ordinary people nor sages to traverse it. I have always told everyone: 'Let the world rejoice as they please, yet I alone do not consent.
If you wish to know those of superior character, they do not take the words and teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and paste them..."

Upon the forehead, like a tortoise bearing the mystic diagram, one brings about the omen of one's own destruction. A phoenix entangled in a golden net—when can it ever hope to soar through the mists and heavens?
You must clarify the source beyond the literal meaning; do not seek patterns within words.

Therefore, if the stone man’s mechanism were like yours, he too would know how to sing the *ba* song. If you were like the stone man, you would surely respond to the *xue* melody. This is the One Guide.

Road. The wise know it to be remote. [Verse] A monk asked: "It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making an offering to a single mindless man of the Way.
I wonder, what fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless man of the Way possess?"
The Master said: "A single sheet of white clouds spans the mouth of the valley; how many returning birds are utterly lost as they seek their nests?

Question: "What is the matter of original nature? The Master said: "A single grain lies in a wasteland; though the seedlings are not weeded, it flourishes of its own accord. Question: "If it is not weeded, will it not be buried by the weeds?
The Master said: "Its flesh and bone differ from those of common grasses and weeds; even the *ti* and *pi* (wild oats) cannot ultimately conceal it."
[Verse] Question: How is it that there is something not contained within the Great Canon? The Master said: "The rain nourishes the three types of grass, which flourish;
a fragment of jade is inherently radiant. [Verse] Question: When a single hair swallows up the vast ocean, what more can be said therein? The Master said:

"If a house possesses the White Zé Map, such monsters and spirits will certainly not exist" (Baofu offered a variant: "If a house lacks the White Zé Map, such monsters and spirits will certainly not exist").

[The Demon]. [Verse]: Question: Are the meaning of the Patriarch and the meaning of the Teaching the same or different? The Master said: "The sun and moon revolve together in their brilliance; whose house has a separate path? He asked:
"If that is so, then light and concealment follow different routes, and matters are not uniform.

The Master said: "As long as you do not forget the sheep yourself, why need you weep at the fork in the road? [Verse]: Question: "When a student intends to return to his hometown, what then? The Master said: "Home."

"The person is destroyed and lost; where will the child return? [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall not return. The Master said, "The remaining snow before the courtyard is melted by the sun; who will sweep away the drifting dust within the room? Thereupon he spoke a verse: "Resolute in my intent, I return to my hometown;

The moon shines upon the withered flowers of the mountain peaks. I have long since abandoned the path of the common world; How could I again enter the gate of the Triple World? The great earth is vast and boundless; The four oceans are deep and immeasurable. I have already cast off the heavy burden of the six paths; Who now would again take up the toil of the three realms?"
Boarding a boat to cross the Five Lakes: the oar is raised and the stars and moon vanish; the rudder is halted and the sun stands solitary.
Unmooring to leave the shore of error, unfurling the sail to enter the path of correctness. Upon arrival, the household is dispersed and scattered; thus one avoids being a fool within the house.

*Admonishing the administrators:* In the Dharma of leaving home, no superfluous possessions are retained. At the time of sowing seeds, one must strictly exercise economy. As for the business of construction—
Everything was consequently suspended. Time flows swiftly, and the Great Way is profound and mysterious; if one merely follows along with negligence, by what means could one realize it?

Although his exhortations were earnest and sincere, the assembly took them as routine and failed to heed them as warnings. [Verse] Manifesting a slight illness, he did not cease receiving visitors for consultation.
One day he addressed the assembly, saying: "It will not be long before I am no more. Today I have a question for you all."
"If you say this is it, you are adding a head atop a head; if you say it is not, you are seeking life by cutting off your own head.
The first seat replied, "The green mountains do not lift their feet; beneath the sun, one does not pick up a lamp.
The Master said, "What kind of time is this to speak such words? At that moment, the seat-holding monk Yancong replied, "Apart from these two paths, I request your verdict."

[Zhao] still did not ask anything further. The Master said, "You have not yet reached it; speak again. [Zhao] said, "Yancong’s Way is not exhaustive. The Master said, "I do not concern myself with whether your Way is exhaustive or not.
[Zhao] said, "Yancong has no attendant to respond for me when addressing the Master. The Master then stopped.
That night, he had an attendant summon Cong and asked him, "The response you gave today was most reasonable. You ought to have realized this."
The Master’s intention: The Master said, “There is no dharma before one’s eyes; the intention is right before one’s eyes. It is not a dharma of the present moment;
it is not something reached by the ears or the eyes. Now tell me, which phrase is the guest? Which phrase is the host?

If you can discern this, I shall entrust you with the patriarchal robe and bowl. Yancong said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “You ought to understand. Yancong said, “I truly do not understand.”
The Master shouted him out and said, "Suffering! Suffering! (Xuánjué remarked: "Now tell me, is it that the Elder truly does not understand, or is he afraid that the alms bowl will stick to him?")
Chan Master Yuantong Yuelun of Huangshan ascended the hall and said: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to proclaim this matter.
It is simply that people do not realize it, but instead seek it outwardly and inwardly—seeking pearls by casting themselves into clear waters, or searching for jade at Mount Jing.
Therefore it is said: 'That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure. To mistake the shadow for the head—is this not a great error?"
Chan Master Shao Shan Huanpu [Verse]: A monk arrived to pay his respects. As he rose from his prostrations, the Master said, "A man of great talent hiding in the door of the humble.
The monk stood to one side. The Master said, "You have lost your timber for a ridgepole. [Verse]: Question: "What is the realm of Shao Shan? The Master said:
"Ancient and modern monkeys and birds cry out; emerald colors are shrouded in thin mist. Question: "What is within the realm?"
The Master said, "Step back and look. [Verse: At the place where right and wrong do not reach, is there still a phrase?
The Master said, "There is. [He asked,] "What phrase is that? The Master said, "A single mass of white clouds does not reveal its ugliness.
[Verse: [He] asked, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "Rootless grass on the peak; without wind, the leaves sway of themselves. [Zun Bunan visited... (Added)
The Master’s questions and answers were most extraordinary (the phrasing is so extensive that it cannot be recorded in full).
Zen Master Lingchao of Shanglan was asked by a monk, “What is the fundamental matter of Shanglan?

The Master said, “It is not borrowed from the thousand sages; how could it be sought among the ten thousand functions? The monk asked, “But what is it like when there is neither borrowing nor seeking? The Master said:
"Can it not be held in your hand? Question: "How does one discern [the truth] before the sharp point? The Master said: "Before the sharp point, no shadow is revealed;
do not seek it on the tip of the tongue. Question: "When two dragons contend for the pearl, who is the one that obtains it?
The Master said: "The pearl covers the ground; though seen with the eyes, it is like mud. Question: "After Sudhana saw Mañjuśrī, why did he [still]..."
"Go south. The Master said, "Learning relies on entering the chamber; knowledge leads to universal penetration. [The monk] asked, "Why did Maitreya instead send him to see Mañjuśrī?
The Master said, "The Way is vast and boundless; it is inexhaustible when encountered by people."
Chan Master Haidu of Taiyuan [Verse]: Once, someone invited Tripitaka Master Guanding for a meal offering.
After the seats had been arranged, the Master took his place upon one of them. At that time, the Dharma Master Yunshe asked, "In what year did you, Reverend, begin your practice?
The Master said, "Dharma Master, come closer. Yunshe approached. The Master said, "As for Kātyāyanaputra, what..."
At what age did he practice the Way? He entered a state of profound obscurity. The Master shouted, "This bed-wetting ghost!
A monk asked Zen Master Youchan of Tiangeshan, "When a student intends to study the sutras, how should they proceed?
The Master said, "Since you are a great merchant, why seek small profits? [Verse: There is a monastery named Wugou Jingguang (Stainless Pure Light). Someone built a bathhouse there. A person...
Question: "Since it is already stainless pure light, why did he instead build a bathhouse? The monk was speechless. Later, he requested the Master to provide an answer on his behalf. The Master said:
"On a night of bright moon in the third autumn month, it is not for the sake of displaying its full orb. [Added by Zeng].
When Chan Master Lingsui of Sanjiao first visited Qingping, Qingping asked, "Why have you come? The Master replied, "I have come to pay my respects. Qingping asked, "To whom do you pay your respects?
The Master said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. Qingping rebuked him, saying, "You dull-witted monk! The Master then prostrated himself.
Qingping struck the Master on the neck once with his hand; from this moment, he attained the essential meaning.
When Chan Master Touzi Gangwen was traveling through the mountains, he saw a cicada’s exuviae. An attendant asked, "The shell is right here;
where has the cicada gone? The Master picked up the shell, shook it three or five times by his ear, and made the sound of a cicada.
The attendant was thereby enlightened. A monk asked, "When the father did not go to Touzi, why did he instead go to Zizhou?
The Master said, "Is this not the business of another's house? The monk asked, "Does the relationship between father and son still belong to 'merit' (karmic function)? The Master said, "It does not."
[The monk] asked, "If they do not belong to the same root, how is it so? The Master said, "Father and son each attain liberation for themselves. [The monk] asked, "Why is it like this?
The Master said, "You and I understand it together."
Chan Master Niutou Wei ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot employ even a single bit of artifice.
The teachers throughout the world have mouths like flat carrying-poles. How do you all fare? It is not easy at all. Unless one knows 'that which is,' no one else can know."
A monk asked the Second Patriarch of Panshan, "How can one escape the three realms? The Master said, "How long has it been since you have been inside them?
The monk asked, "How then can one escape? The Master said, "Green mountains do not obstruct the flying white clouds."
A monk asked Chan Master Jiuzhong Jinghui, "How can one pass over the deep pit of liberation? The Master said, "Do not seek to pass.
The monk asked, "How then can one pass? The Master said, "Seeking to pass is also not it."
Once Chan Master Guanyanyan Jun was passing through a deep valley at Fenglin when he suddenly beheld precious treasures appearing.
His companions looked at one another, intending to take them; the Master said, "When the ancients tilled their gardens, they encountered gold as if it were mere rubble.

Wait until my thatch-roofed hut is complete, and I shall require this to provide for the monks of the four quarters. Having spoken, he left them behind. He then went to visit Touzi, who asked, "Yesterday..."
"Where do you stay overnight? the Master said, "In the immovable site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa). The Master's son said, "If you say it is immovable, how did you come here?
The Master said, "Having arrived here—how could that be movement? The Master's son said, "So, originally you stayed where there is no place to stay. Touzi silently granted him his approval.
A monk asked Chan Master Ximing of Haozhou, "What is the pure Dharma-body?
The Master said, "A maggot in excrement, its head emerging and its head submerging."
Chan Master Guyshan Youyuan [Verse]: A monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?

The Master said: “At midnight, a crow wears snow upon its head; at dawn, a mute man returns home with his head in his arms. [Added later: A monk asked, “What is it like when one is turned around by a single push?
The Master said: “When the wild horse runs, the whip and bridle snap; the stone man claps his hands and laughs heartily.”
A monk asked Chan Master Letan Yanmao, “What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, “I certainly do not say it is earth, wood, tiles, or rubble.
[Another] asked, “Who is the true master, the Abbot? The Master said, “The painted drum resounds as the mallet strikes it repeatedly.”
No sound is heard at the ear’s edge.
Chan Master Changcha of Fengqi Tong’an Temple [Verse]: A monk asked, “What is the家风 (household style/tradition) of Fengqi?
The Master said, “Fengqi has no household style. The monk asked, “Since it is Fengqi, why is there no household style? The Master said, “Not...”
Welcoming guests, he did not wait for them to arrive. A monk asked, "If that is so, then when one travels throughout the four seas in search [of the Way], what should one do?
The Master said, "The food on the platter is provided by others. A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "An iron dog barks at a stone ox; an illusory person gazes at the moonlight. A monk asked, "What is it to be a person with fur and horns? The Master said—
He said: "A straw raincoat and bamboo hat sell for gold; how many who meet them do not know to call out? A monk asked, "I, your disciple, do not yet understand the timing of the occasion;
I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "The pines and bamboos are uneven, shrouded in thin mist; the layered peaks and ridges are slow to receive the rising moon.
The monk prepared to offer a word in response, but the Master said: "Before the armor and weapons are deployed, the thief's body has already been exposed. The monk asked, "Why?"
The Master said: "The refined yang does not prune the bamboo before the frost; ink and water vainly boast of dragons from the sea. The monk circled the meditation seat and departed. The Master said:
"Closing one's eyes to eat a snail—what a bitter and sour experience! [Verse]: Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Master:
A rhinoceros gazes at the moon, patterns forming on its horns; an elephant is startled by thunder, and flowers enter its trunk.
[The Master] said, "Teeth. The Abbot asked, "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.

I do not know, however, what Dharma the Master teaches to people. The Master replied, "I teach the Dharma of the One Vehicle. The Abbot asked, "What is the Dharma of the One Vehicle? The Master replied:
"How many kinds of cloud colors emerge from the mountain peaks? How uniform is the sound of the spring falling before the balustrade?

[The Master] said, "I do not ask about this. What is the Dharma of the One Vehicle? The Master said, "You are remarkably sharp-witted. While enjoying the moon, he said to a monk, "How marvelous, how marvelous!
The stars are bright and the moon is clear; it is truly worthy of contemplation. Is this not the Way? The monk asked, "What is it?"
The Master said, "Try to say something. The monk replied, "He has no wound himself; do not injure him. The Master said, "One who carries a book-satchel to study literature has no leisure for archery.
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Jiangxi. The Master said, "How does the Dharma-way of Jiangxi compare to this place?
The monk replied, "I am fortunate that you asked me; had you asked someone else, trouble would have arisen."
The Master said, "I was a bit hasty just now. [The monk] said, "I am no infant; it is useless to employ yellow leaves merely to stop a child's crying.
The Master said, "To spare the turtle while harming the soft-shelled turtle—killing or giving life is up to me."
Chan Master Wuyin of Heishan went to visit Jiufeng. Jiufeng asked, "You have come from afar; you follow the assembly with such radiance.
What realm do you perceive that allows for cultivation? By what path are you able to transcend? The Master replied, "The heavy darkness has been cleared away;
the blind remain blind. Jiufeng then permitted him to enter his room. Later, he resided at Heishan, where his disciples gathered in great numbers. All...
[The Emperor] then sighed in admiration. ○ The Li clan of Jiangnan summoned him and asked, "Where have you come from, Master? The Master replied, "From Heishan.
[The Emperor] asked, "Where is that mountain? The Master said, "When people come to pay court at the Phoenix Palace, the mountains and peaks do not move."
The ruler of the land held him in high esteem. A monk asked, "What was the meaning of Yangshan’s thrusting in the hoe?
The Master said, "Ask me. The monk said, "Xuansha kicked over the hoe; what about that? The Master said, "I am asking you. The monk said, "I have not yet discerned its fundamental principle."
"How does one fully comprehend this? The Master said, "The head is large, the tail is pointed. [Commentary] [Verse] To study and practice is called "hearing" (learning).
To cease studying is called "neighboring" (the limit). To transcend these two is called "truly transcending. What is true transcendence? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum.
[Question] "What is the True Truth (Paramārtha-satya)? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. [Question] Again he asked, "As for this very mind..."
The Master said, "If it were the Buddha, I would not ask. How is it that it is neither mind nor Buddha? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum.
[The student] asked, "What is the matter beyond [this]? The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. [The student] asked, "When the myriad dharmas arise all at once, what then?
The Master said, "Heshan knows how to beat the drum. (According to the *Wudeng Huiyuan*, this question exists; elsewhere, people speak only of Heshan’s four beatings of the drum.)
A monk asked Chan Master Lètán Mù of Hongzhou, "What is the place where the student exerts effort? The Master said, "This is precisely the place where one exerts effort.
A monk asked Chan Master Shào of Liùtōngyuàn, "How is it with that which does not pass through the throat, lips, or mouth? The Master said, "Wait..."
"You severed Mount Jinsi with a single stroke of your mattock; I will not speak of it to you either.
Chan Master Yungai Zhihan was asked by a monk: "What is the surging tide that floods the heavens atop Mount Sumeru? The Master said:
Wen-shu was creating a commotion. He asked, "What is the matter within the state of directness? The Master said, "I do not display great compassion before the stimulus.
He asked, "What is it like to be a person of that other side? The Master said, "No shadow is revealed before the blade’s edge; after the phrase, no trace can be found."
A monk asked National Teacher Suiyan of Silla, “When both black and white have perished and the Buddha-eye is opened, what is it like?
The Master said, “I fear you will cling to the internal. [The monk] asked, “What is the Prince born at birth? The Master said, “He cannot be led out from the deep palace.
[The monk] asked, “What is the Prince born at dawn? The Master said, “He does not take his place within the palace. [The monk] asked, “What is...”
Master Maseng Wangzi said: "In every place there is no target; the mechanism of the ten thousand men is not deployed.
Chan Master Baeryam of Silla [Verse]: A monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "An ancient tomb is not made into a home. [The monk] asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "Vainly exhausting the tracks of carriages and horses. [The monk] asked, "What is the Teaching? The Master said:
It cannot be fully contained even upon palm leaves.
A monk asked Zen Master Daeryong of Silla Country: "The ancients said, 'Upon reaching Tongguan, one simply stops.

Does one stop because one has understood, or does one stop because one has not yet understood? The Master replied, "It is simply the livelihood within the path of delusion. [The monk] said, "Setting aside delusion..."
"Along the way, have you attained the livelihood within it? The Master said, "In principle one attains it; in practice one does not.
He asked, "Since one attains it in principle, why does one not attain it in practice? The Master said, "Attaining it is a matter for what kind of person?
He asked, "What is the matter within it like? The Master said, "Do not act as if you were noble. [He] asked, "How is it that there is no obstruction within function?"
The Master said: "A single sheet of white clouds flies in disarray. [Verse] Question: What is meant by "purity in all places"? The Master said:
"When jade branches are cut, every inch is treasure; when sandalwood is split, every fragment is fragrant."
A monk asked Master Yin of Heishan: "When the Prince has not yet ascended the throne, who shall govern and transform the realm?
The Master said: "The command of the frontier passes beyond the palace gates; the General himself brings about the years of Great Peace. The monk asked:

"In what way, then, would the merit of governing and transforming still be inappropriate? The Master said: "There is indeed an appropriateness. The monk asked: "What is this appropriateness? The Master said: "The lands of the ten directions."
"The earth belongs entirely to the King. Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "One who accepts [this] is no adept. Chan Master Congshi of Zhexi asked a monk:
"What have you come to do? The monk replied: "I have come to draw near. The Master said:
"Though white clouds may rise to the mountain peaks at dawn, how can the green mountains help but frown?"
A monk asked Chan Master Qingfeng Xuanchu, "The Great Matter has already been clarified; why then is it as if one has lost one's parents?
The Master said, "Without the spring breeze, the flowers do not bloom; once the flowers have bloomed, the breeze blows them away.
A monk asked, "What is the single color? The Master said, "There is not a single drop of water; the surging waves are like silver mountains."
A monk asked Zen Master Wuya Yanbin, "Before one has yet taken human form, what was one doing?
The Master said, "A three-legged stone ox gallops over the hill; a branch of auspicious grass is revealed before one's eyes."
A monk asked Chan Master Yong’an Jing: “When one knows that there is [the Way] yet cannot attain it, what then? The Master said: “What is there to know? The monk said:

“It cannot be that there is nothing. The Master said: “If so, then you ought to be able to speak of it. The monk said: “To speak of it is not impossible; however, the words are biased. The Master said:
“The waters are frozen, so the fish find it hard to leap; the mountains are cold, so the flowers bloom late. [Question: “As for suchness...”
"What is this single color? The Master said: "It is easy to distinguish flour from within the snow; it is difficult to discern soot within ink. Question:
"When it cannot be known by intellect and cannot be recognized by consciousness, what is it like? The Master said: "The crane and the egret stand side-by-side, treading in the snow as they sleep."
The moon’s brightness startles them awake, leaving both hesitant.
A monk asked Chan Master Zhongdu of Dengzhou, “What is the ground of ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), where not a single speck of dust is accepted?

And what is the gate of Buddha-activity, where not a single dharma is discarded? The Master said, “True permanence is unstained by dust; the ocean receives the flow of a hundred rivers. [The monk] said: [“... (The Master replied: “...”.
"Please answer me from beyond sound and form," he requested. The Master said, "The wooden man constantly speaks in response; though he has a nature, he cannot speak.
Chan Master Yong’an Jingwu asked a monk, "When the six gates are blocked, how does one reach the truth? The Master said, "With whom do you, Reverend, associate outside?
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The earthen ox at the bottom of the sea."
"Roar! A wooden horse neighs amidst the clouds.
Chan Master Shiping Shendao’s Verse: When he first visited Luopo, the Master asked, "Before a single bubble has arisen, how does one discern the flow of the water?
Luopo replied, "Shift the boat to learn the currents; raise the oars to distinguish the waves. The Master did not attain realization and thus—
He visited Bānlóng. The dialogue was the same as the previous question. Bānlóng said: "If you move your boat, you do not leave the water; yet as soon as you raise your oars, you lose the source.
From this, the Master attained awakening. [Verse] A monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "Look eastward at the head of the stone ram."
A monk asked Chan Master Chongfu Zhi, “It is said that making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas is not as good as making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way.
I wonder, what fault do the Buddhas have, and what virtue does the mindless man of the Way possess? The Master replied, “When the snow is deep, it is best to stay near the fire;
when the body is warm, one perceives spring to be slow to arrive.”
While Chan Master Shanben of Vulture Peak was bathing, a monk asked, "The Master is a person free from defilement;
why then do you bathe? The Master said, "The water of concentration is full and serene; I bathe this person who is without stain."
A monk asked Zen Master Da’an Xinggu, "What is the meaning of Vimalakīrti’s silence? The Master said, "The dark, black stone oxling;
transcendent, it never leaves its door."
A monk asked Zen Master Wuya Xinglang, "Who is worthy to wear Kāśyapa’s robe of supreme transmission?
The Master said, "The naturally formless child does not don the robe that transcends the mundane."
A monk asked Zen Master Kaishan Huaidou, "What practice must one perform to not contradict the thousand sages?
The Master said, "Sublime conduct is without peer; when the mind is profound, the essence is naturally distinct. [The monk] asked, "What is the teacher amidst the dust?
The Master said, "I arrive wherever I please within the thicket of brambles; I move freely and at will within the grove of sandalwood."
A monk asked Zen Master Qingmian of Mount Qingfeng, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Not a single drop in Lake Nuo; the four seas flow on of their own accord."
Emperor Taizong of the Great Song [Verse]: One day, because a monk came for an audience, the Emperor asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the Woyun Hermitage on Mount Lu.
The Emperor said, "I have heard that where the clouds rest deeply, one does not face the court. Why have you come here? The monk was speechless.
[To this, Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation. (Xuedou’s Verse): When a monk entered for an audience, he reported, "Your Majesty, do you still remember?
The Emperor said, "Where did we meet? The monk replied, "Since our parting at Vulture Peak, it has been until now.

The Emperor asked, "What proof do you have? The monk was speechless. [Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "I, this poor monk, have come specifically for this purpose. [The Emperor once dreamed that a divine being informed him: "Please..."
His Majesty gave rise to the bodhicitta. During an early court audience, he questioned those around him, "How does one give rise to the bodhicitta?

None of those present could answer. (Xuedou provides a substitute response: "Truly, this is rarely heard in all antiquity. [Verse] One day, after the court session had ended, the Emperor held up his alms bowl and asked Prime Minister Wang Sui:
"Since it was something that could not be lifted at the head of Dayu Ridge, why is it now in my hands?"

[The Emperor] asked in accordance with the principle of non-obstruction. Emperor Xiaozong [in a verse] inquired: "When Śākyamuni Buddha entered the mountains to cultivate the Way, he accomplished it in six years.
What was it that he accomplished? I request the Master to explain this clearly. He replied: "I had thought Your Majesty..."
[Lower section omitted due to corruption.

The Dharma heirs of the Master of Tea (Chaling Yushan) are not yet fully known. [Verse]: Having never traveled as a wandering monk, a presiding master arrived from Mount Lu, and they discussed the School.
Regarding the matter of the gate: the Master instructed him to consult the monk Faldeng on the question, "At the top of a hundred-foot pole, how does one take a further step?
Deng replied, "Ugh. This continued for three years. One day, while crossing a bridge on a donkey, he stepped onto a plank and fell; at that moment, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
Thereupon, he spoke in verse: "I possess a divine pearl; for a long time it has been locked away by the dust of worldly toil.
Today, the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, illuminating the myriad peaks of mountains and rivers. Because of this, he no longer traveled to distant lands.
Formerly, Chan Master Jingzhao asked National Teacher Lengyan: "The sutra says that if one can turn things over, one is identical to the Tathāgata;
if one is turned by things, one is called an ordinary person. Now, as for the Shengyuan Pavilion, how would you turn it? Lengyan had no reply.
Chan Master Dongshan Yungding was renowned for his mastery of the Way and its teachings; the monastic community referred to him as "Ding," the Third Teaching.

One day, a Daoist from Jiulongguan, along with three Confucian scholars, invited him to ascend the hall. [The Master said: "In the Confucian gate, they paint the Eight Trigrams and compose contracts, yet these do not save one from the cycle of rebirth in the six realms.
In the Daoist gate, they worship the Nine Sovereigns and refine the true qi, yet this does not lead to an understanding of the kalpas of the three great aeons. I—"
Śākyamuni Bhagavān thoroughly understands the kalpas of the three great aeons and delivers beings from the saṃsāra of the six realms.

With his great vows, he gathers in humans and devas, like the wind-circle supporting the sun and moon; with his great wisdom, he shatters birth and death, as the fire at the end of an aeon consumes even the finest autumn hair.

Those who enter my gate naturally transform heaven and earth and perceive ghosts and spirits in their hidden depths, such that Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, and the great earth [are all transformed].
The great ocean enters into a single pore, yet all sentient beings neither perceive nor know it.
I say that this Dharma-gate is like space, which contains all myriad phenomena; the one becomes the infinite, and the infinite becomes the one.
If a person attains the one, then all matters are complete. Be careful.
Master Yunyou Chongyuan ascended the hall and said: "Yunyou has but a single arrow; space has no front or back.
Shot forth, it pervades the ten directions, yet for all its effort, no one sees it. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the Master’s single arrow?"
The Master said: "If all the people in the great earth had no skulls...
Liuzi the Monk [Verse]: One day, while wandering through the streets and markets, he was adjusting his socks and sash beneath a wine tavern when he heard a song being sung from above:
"Since you have no heart, I shall also cease. At that moment, he suddenly attained great enlightenment; for this reason, he was given the name Liuzi (Liu the Skull).

Lanziyan. The Dharma Master Zhengwu of India once lamented that scholars of his own school were confined by names and forms (*nāma-rūpa*) and bound by written records, even to the point of regarding the transmission of Tiantai as a mere study of texts.
The followers of the Southern School held this in contempt; thus, he went to visit Huguo [Zhixu].
During a conversation at night, Master An Yuan cited the verse by Dongpo on staying overnight at Donglin Temple and remarked, "It is not easy to reach such a state.
An Yuan said, "You have not yet even seen the path; how can you speak of 'reaching' it? Dongpo replied, "As for what he said..."
"The sound of the mountain stream is the broad and long tongue; the color of the mountains—is this not the pure body?

If you do not reach this state, how could there be such news? The Hermit said, "You are merely a man from outside the gate. [The monk] said, "Venerable Sir, do not be stingy; please explain it for me.
The Hermit said, "Instead, right here, apply yourself with intense vigor and look closely. If you look closely..."
When he attained the realization of "the other's breaking," he also came to know where his own *benming yuanchen* (original life-source) was situated. The Master did not sleep throughout the night.
At dawn, as the bell tolled, he removed his secret storehouse and composed a parting verse, saying: "The Layman Dongpo is far too talkative; He wishes to pass through the barrier of sound and form.
If the stream is sound and the mountain is form, Without mountain and without water, what a sorrowful man! [This was] specifically for [him].
He reported this to the Hermitage Master (Baizhang). The Hermitage Master said, "I told you before that he is a man from outside the gate. The Master bowed in thanks.
Not long after, there was one who went to Ma Zu to request the repair of roof tiles for the hall; seeking words to promote the teaching, the Master wrote: "Send word to the old adept of Jiangxi:
Let him be scorched by the sun and fanned by the wind as he pleases. It is not that his descendants lack the means to manage it; One must simply see the moment the ice melts and the walls crumble."
When Chan Master Ci’an saw this, he laughed and said, “It must be this very *śramaṇera* who can do it.
When the Vinaya Master Bensong was questioned by the layman Yang Jie regarding the essential nature of the *vinaya* as expounded by Vinaya Master Xuanchang, the Master replied with a verse:
“How could emotion and wisdom ever differ? The dog barks, while the snake moves on its own. Zhongnan is indeed...”
The meaning is this: "At noon, strike the third watch.
Long ago, there was an elder who [composed a verse] stating: "For an entire summer, I did not speak a word to the monks. A monk sighed and said:
"I have spent this entire summer in vain like this; I do not dare hope that you, Master, will preach the Buddha-dharma, but I would at least wish to hear two characters of the True Cause."
Dede heard this and said, "Acarya, do not speak so hastily. If we speak of the true cause, there is not even a single character.
Having finished speaking, he tapped his teeth and said, "Just now, I spoke without reason; it was improper to say such a thing.

An old practitioner by the neighboring wall heard this and said, "What a fine pot of soup that has been defiled by a single mouse dropping! [Xuedou’s substitute says: "In whose household is there not an ounce or two? ] [Verse] In the past...
There was a monk who did not read the sutras while inside the scripture hall, but sat in meditation every day. The Librarian asked, "Why do you not read the sutras?
The monk replied, "I am illiterate. The Librarian said, "Why do you not ask others? The monk stepped forward, joined his palms, bowed, and asked, "What character is this?
The Librarian had no reply. (The Dàtōng edition reads: "Or again, he said, 'I do not recognize it. )
In the past, two hermits lived in separate huts. [Verse: For ten days they did not see one another; suddenly they met.
The senior hermit asked the junior hermit, "It has been a long time since we last saw each other. Where have you been?
The junior hermit replied, "I have been in my hut constructing a seamless stūpa. The senior hermit said, "I also wish to construct one. May I borrow your stūpa from you?"
[The Master] made a gesture. The abbot below said, "Why did you not say so sooner? It has just been borrowed by someone.
Long ago, an old master said, "This plot of land has been entrusted to you for a long time now; I stand here waiting for you to grasp it.
(Fayan said, "I, this mountain monk, am sitting here now, waiting for you to grasp it. Is there any principle [in this]? Which is intimate and which is distant? Try to judge it. There was...
The monk was studying the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* when he reached the verse: "All dharmas from the very beginning are eternally in the state of quiescent extinction.
Suddenly, doubt arose that he could not resolve. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, he constantly investigated this within himself, yet gained nothing at all.

One spring month, hearing the cry of a heron, he attained sudden enlightenment. He then continued the preceding verse, saying: "All dharmas from the very beginning are eternally in the state of quiescent extinction. Spring has arrived."
A hundred flowers bloom; yellow herons cry atop the willows. A monk finished reciting the sutra with a young boy and ordered him to place the sutra inside the case.
The boy asked, "Where shall I put what I have recited? (Fadeng spoke on his behalf: "What sutra did you recite?")

Formerly, there was an official who wrote a "Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts. One night, while he was wielding his brush, he suddenly saw a ghost appear and say, "You claim there are no ghosts;
what about me? (Wuzu Yan said: "If I had been there at that time, I would have simply made my hand into a magpie's beak and said to him, 'Gu-gua! [The sound of a magpie calling].

Formerly, there was a laywoman who supported a hermit for twenty years, constantly employing a young girl of sixteen or eighteen to serve him. [Verse] A laywoman provided for a hermit for twenty years, Always employing a girl of sixteen or eighteen.
The son served him meals and attended to his needs. One day, the Master ordered the daughter to hold him firmly and asked, "At this very moment, what is it like?
The son replied, "A withered tree leans against a cold cliff; for three winters there is no warmth. The daughter reported this to the Old Lady (the Master’s wife).
The Old Lady said, "For twenty years, I have supported nothing but a worldly fellow. She then sent him away and burned down the hermitage.

The nun Chen Dao once traveled extensively to seek instruction from renowned masters throughout the various regions. Later, at Changlao Mountain, she attained enlightenment through the words of Master Jing.
She composed a verse which says: Upon the level summit of the high ridge, There are only woodcutters.
Everyone harbors the intent of axe and hatchet, Yet they do not see the mountain flowers reflecting red in the water.
Once, there was a woman who entered the monastery to distribute the "money according to age" (suíniánqián) for the assembly of monks. A monk said, "Place one portion before the Holy Monk (Śāstṛ).
The woman asked, "How old is the Holy Monk? The monk had no reply. Fayan spoke on his behalf, saying: "One knows it when the heart's aspiration is fulfilled.
(End of Volume Six of the *Huìyuán*).

The Fourth Volume of the True Lineage of the Chan School.
Emperor Qingyuan first visited Chan Master Guoyi of Mount Jing, where he received the mind-to-mind transmission of the Dharma and served him diligently for five years.

Later, he studied under Mazu, which served as a further seal of his prior understanding; the Dharma has no divergent teachings. He remained in attendance for two summers and then went to visit Shitou.
He asked, "Setting aside concentration and wisdom, by what dharma do you instruct people? Deshan said, "In my place, there are no servants; what is there to set aside?
The monk asked, "How then can one attain clarity? Deshan said, "Can you grasp empty space?
The monk said, "If that is so, then from this day forward, I shall not follow [your path]. Deshan said, "I wonder, when did you come from 'that side'? The monk said, [silently].
Dowu said, "I am not a man from that place. Baizhang said, "I have long known where you come from. Dowu asked, "Why do you falsely accuse me with stolen goods?
Baizhang said, "Your own body is right here. Dowu said, "Even though it is so, how ultimately will you show this to future generations?
Baizhang said, "Who do you say is a 'future generation'? At this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and fully exhausted the two preceding [stages].
The words of the master artisan contain that which is grasped by the mind. A monk asked, "What is the profound and wondrous teaching?
The Master said, "Do not say that I understand the Buddha-dharma. The monk said, "How can I avoid my own lingering doubts?
The Master said, "Why do you not ask the old monk? The monk said, "I have already asked. The Master said, "Go! This is not where you should settle."
Chan Master Chongxin of Longtan [Verse]: His family sold cakes. The Master was extraordinary from his youth.
Initially, he studied under Master Wugou, who was secretly invited by Lingjian to reside at Tiantai Temple; no one could fathom this.

The Master lived in the lane adjacent to the temple and would daily provide him with ten cakes. Whenever the Abbot finished eating, he would always leave one cake behind, saying, "I give this to you."
[The Emperor] used [the merit] to provide for his descendants. One day the Master thought to himself, "I brought these cakes away;

why has he returned them to me? Is there some other hidden meaning? He went to see him and asked about it. The Emperor said, "These were yours to bring; returning them to you—what fault is there in that?

Upon hearing this, the Master was deeply enlightened by the profound principle and consequently entered the monastic life. [Verse: The Emperor said, "In the past, you honored and cultivated blessings and goodness."
"Now you believe my words; you may be named Chongxin (Venerable Faith). From then on, he served diligently at the Master’s side.

One day, the Master asked him, "Since you arrived, I have not received instruction on the essentials of the mind. Huang said, "Ever since you arrived, I have never failed to point out the essentials of your mind.
The Master asked, "Where did you point it out? Huang replied, "When you brought me tea, I accepted it from you; when you walked..."
"When you come to eat, I will receive it for you; when you bow, I shall lower my head. Where else would I not point out the essential heart-mind?
The Master lowered his head for a long while. The Emperor said, "If you see, see directly; if you deliberate, you have already missed it.

At these words, the Master attained immediate understanding. He asked again, "How does one maintain this? The Emperor said, "Roam freely according to your nature and remain relaxed and open in accordance with conditions. Simply—"
Exhausting the ordinary mind, there is no separate "sage's understanding.
Chan Master Deshan Xuanjian [Verse]: A native of the Zhou clan from Jianzhou; while in Shu, he frequently lectured on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
At that time, he was known as Zhou Jingang. Carrying his commentaries on the *Qinglong* [Sutra], he departed from Shu.
While traveling on the road to Liyang, he saw an old woman selling cakes. He set down his pack and bought some cakes for a snack.

The woman pointed to his pack and asked, "Regarding the three minds in the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, I wonder, Elder, which mind do you point to? The Master was speechless. He then proceeded to Longtan and arrived at the Dharma [Hall].
The Hall Master said: "For a long time I have heard of Dragon Pond (Longtan). But when I actually arrived, the pond was not to be seen and the dragon did not appear.

The Pond drew himself up and said, 'You have truly arrived at Dragon Pond. The Master was speechless, and so he took up residence there. [Verse] One night, while standing in attendance, the Pond said, "It is deep in the night;
why do you not leave? The Master said, "I take my leave," and then departed. Returning, he said, "It is dark outside."
Tongan held up a paper candle and passed it to the Master. As the Master reached out to receive it, Tongan blew it out.

At this, the Master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself. Tongan asked, "What have you seen? The Master replied, "From now on, I shall no longer doubt the tongues of all the old monks under heaven.
On the following day, Longtan ascended the seat and said to the assembly, "Among you there is one..."
Han: His tusks are like sword-trees; his mouth is like a blood-basin. Struck once with a staff, he will not turn back.
In time, he shall stand upon the summit of a solitary peak and establish my Way. The Master then piled his commentaries and sub-commentaries before the Dharma Hall, raised a torch, and said:
"To exhaust all profound dialectics is like placing a single hair in the great void; to exhaust all worldly mechanisms is like casting a single drop into the vast ocean."
He then burned them. [Commentary] [Verse] He paid his respects at Longtan and went straight to Mt. Mui. Clinging to the double-roofed building, he ascended to the Dharma Hall;
he went from west to east, and from east to west. Looking toward the abbot’s quarters, he said, "Is there anything?

Is there anything? Master Mui sat there without so much as a glance. The Master said, "There is nothing, there is nothing," and then departed. Upon reaching the gate, he said, "Even though it is thus, nevertheless..."

He thought, "I must not treat this lightly," and so he prepared his full ceremonial regalia and entered again for an audience. As soon as he stepped across the threshold, he held up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*) and said, "Venerable Teacher!
As Shanshan reached for his whisk, the Master gave a shout; the monk then shook out his sleeves and departed.

That evening, Guishan asked the head seat, "Is the newcomer from today still here? The head seat replied, "At that moment, he turned his back on the Dharma Hall and went out wearing his straw sandals."
Yunmen said, "In the future, this man will build a thatched hut atop a solitary peak and go about scolding the Buddhas and reviling the Patriarchs.
Ascending the hall, he said: "If you have no affairs within yourself, do not seek them falsely. Even if you were to obtain something through false seeking, it would still not be attainment.
You need only be without affairs in your mind and without mind toward affairs; then you will be empty yet spiritually aware, vacant yet wondrous."
If one speaks of the beginning and end of things even to the extent of a hair-tip, it is entirely self-deception.

Why? A single thought tied to a hair’s breadth is the karmic cause for the three miserable realms; a fleeting stir of emotion results in shackles for ten thousand kalpas. Holy names and mundane titles are all but empty sounds;
extraordinary features and inferior forms are all but illusory colors. If you seek them, will you not be burdened? And when you grow weary of them, yet again...
It results in great calamity; in the end, it is of no benefit. [Verse] He gave a small-scale sermon (*xiao can*) to the assembly, saying:
"Tonight, I will not answer questions. Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows of the staff. At that time, a monk came forward and bowed. The Master struck him immediately.
The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; for what reason does the Master strike me? The Master asked, "Where are you from? He replied, "Silla (Korea)."
A man approached. The Master said, "If you had not yet stepped onto the boat's railing, I would have given you thirty blows. (Fayan said, "The Great Deshan has split his discourse into two pieces.
Yuanming said, "The Great Deshan has a dragon’s head but a snake’s tail. Ascending the hall, he said: "To ask is already a fault; not to ask is still a deviation. A monk came forward and bowed.
The Master struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have only just bowed; why did you strike me? The Master said, "I was waiting for you to open your mouth."
"What can be done? Xuefeng asked, "What was the meaning behind Nanquan’s act of beheading the cat?

The Master then drove him away, but called out again, "Do you understand? Xuefeng said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Even with such a grandmotherly heart of mine, you still do not understand.
[Verse] Addressing the assembly, he said: "If you can speak it, thirty blows; if you cannot speak it, thirty blows."—Linji.
Having heard this, he said to Luopu, "Go and ask him why [he says], 'Thirty blows for being able to speak. Wait until he strikes you;
catch hold of the staff and give it a shove. See what he does then. Luopu asked according to these instructions.
The Master struck him. Luopu caught the staff and gave it a shove. The Master then returned to his quarters. Luopu returned and reported this to Linji. Linji—
Linji said, "I have always suspected this fellow. Even so, do you recognize Deshan?
As Pufu hesitated, Linji struck him.
The Venerable Lestam Baofeng asked a monk, "The ancients had a single path to receive those of later generations and beginners;
do you know it? The monk said, "I ask the Master to point out that single path of the ancients. The Master said, "What then? Have you already understood it, Lay Brother?
The monk said, "To place a head atop a head. The Master said, "It is not fitting for Baofeng to question you, worthy one. The monk said, "Why then did you ask?"
[The Master] interrupted him. The Master said, "No one here has ever been allowed to prattle on about principles.
Get out! Chan Master Yantou Quanhuo [Verse]: One day he went to visit Deshan. As soon as he stepped across the threshold, he asked, "Is this ordinary or is it sacred?
Deshan gave a shout. The Master bowed. Someone reported this to Dongshan, who said, "Had it not been for Master Huo, [the matter would have been different]."
"A great responsibility to undertake. The Master said, "The old man Dongshan did not recognize good from bad; he wrongly applied these names and phrases.
At that time, I was holding one hand up and the other down. [Verse]: Xuefeng served as the head cook at Deshan. One day, the meal was late.
When Deshan was carrying his bowl down from the Dharma Hall, Xuefeng happened to see him as he was drying his rice-cloth. Xuefeng said, "The bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded;
where are you going with your bowl? Deshan then returned directly to his quarters. Xuefeng reported this incident to his teacher.

The Master said, "Great as De Shan may be, he has not yet realized the final word. Upon hearing this, De Shan ordered his attendant to summon the Master and ask him, "Do you not approve of me, old monk?
The Master secretly revealed his intention, whereupon De Shan desisted. The next day, when De Shan ascended the hall, it was indeed different from his usual manner.
The Master went before the Sangha Hall, clapped his hands, and laughed loudly, saying, "I am glad that the old man at the head of the hall [has finally changed]."
Han: He grasped the final word at the end of his life; thereafter, no one in the world could do anything with him.

Nevertheless, he was only able to live for three years (he passed away three years later). [Verse] The Master resided at Yantou in Ezhou. During the period of the Buddhist purge, he served as a ferryman by a lake.
He hung a board on each bank; whenever someone crossed the ferry, he would strike the board once. The Master would ask, "Who is it?"
Someone said, "I must go over to that side. The Master then raised his oars and welcomed him.
One day, a woman came carrying a child in her arms and said, "I will not ask about raising the oars and dancing with them; tell me, from where did this child in the old woman’s hands come?
The Master struck her. The woman said, "The old woman has given birth to seven sons; six have not met with one who understands their worth. Only this—"

At that time, a monk came forward and bowed, requesting the Master to provide an illustration. The Master said: 'The intent of my teaching is like the three dots of the character for "three" (*三*). The first [dot]..."*
Drop one dot toward the east; this dot opens the eyes of all Bodhisattvas. Drop a second dot toward the west;
this dot sustains the life-faculty of all Bodhisattvas. Drop a third dot upward; this dot marks the crowns of the heads of all Bodhisattvas.
This is the meaning of the first section. It is further said: "The intent of my teaching is like that of Maheśvara, who splits open his face and raises it upright."
"One eye. This is the second meaning. [Verse] It is also said: "The intent of my teaching is like a drum smeared with lethal poison;
when struck once, all who hear it, whether far or near, perish. This is the third meaning.
At that time, the Venerable Xiaoyan asked, "What is the 'poison-smearing drum'? The Master pressed both hands upon his knees, leaned forward, and said, "Han Xin facing the throne."

Xuefeng asked, "What words did Yantou say? The monk recounted the previous dialogue. Xuefeng then struck him thirty blows and drove him out.

Whether asked about the Buddha, the Dharma, the Path, or Meditation, the Master would always only emit a sigh (the verse on this ancient case differs slightly).
Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun [Verse]: Initially, while traveling with Yantou to Aoshan Town in Lizhou, they were detained by snow.
Yantou spent his days doing nothing but sleeping, while the Master sat in meditation all the time. One day, [Yantou] called out, "Brother, Brother! For now..."
[The Master] got up. Daowu asked, "What are you doing? The Master said, "This life does not go smoothly.
I have been traveling with this fellow Wensui; everywhere we go, I am brought to ruin by him. Today, having arrived here, he simply keeps on sleeping. Daowu shouted, "Go eat and sleep!
Sitting on your bed every day, you are just like a local deity in a village of seven hamlets. In the future, you will become a demonic spirit!"
"The men and women of the world have already departed," the Master said, pointing to his own chest. "I am not yet settled here; I do not dare deceive myself.
Baizhang Tou said, "I took you for someone who would one day, atop a solitary peak, build a grass hut and propagate the Great Teaching, yet you still speak these words.
The Master replied, "I truly am not yet settled. Tou said, "If it is indeed so..."

where you are not, I shall cut it away for you. The Master said, "When I first arrived at Yanguan, I saw him ascend the hall and expound upon the meaning of form and emptiness, and I attained a point of entry.
