He instructed a monk to ask, "What is the environment of Kaixian? The Master replied, "The very best is this single boundary that breaks the color of the green mountains.
The ruler asked, "Who is the person within the environment? The Master replied, "Gathering withered wood and boiling spring water. The ruler was greatly pleased.
He was treated with even greater reverence.
One day, a monk asked Zen Master Fatao, "What is the person who does not pay court to the Son of Heaven and does not envy princes and lords?
The Master said, "Every day, three lines; for years on end, a single robe. The monk asked, "I wonder, does this person still succeed to the lineage?"
[The Master] said, "There is no such thing as 'founder's style' (zongfeng). The Master said, "A magpie comes and speaks upon my head; clouds fly before my eyes.
When Master Hongyan of Shuilu ascended the hall, the assembly had gathered in silence.
The Master descended from his seat, took up the incense burner, and walked before the assembly, saying, "I offer this to the Buddhas of the ten directions," and then returned to his quarters.
A monk asked Chan Master Guangyan Xianze, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion?
The Master said, "The Green History Tower within the city; the High Peak Pagoda beyond the clouds. [Another] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?"
The Master said: "The spring water in the secluded ravine is clear; the moon atop the high peak is white.
Chan Master Baoci Huilang ascended the hall and said: "The successive sages of the past appeared in the world for the sake of the one great cause and condition.
They have transmitted this message to one another. Do you all understand? If you do not understand, it is truly intolerable."
Easy. A monk asked, "What is this one great matter? The Master said, "Do not mistake my words as a report. The monk said, "If that is so, then I have no doubts.
The Master said, "Alas, how can you avoid having a speck before your eye?"
Master Jingchan Shifo ascended the hall and said: "If you say that the natural face is being presented, you are still adding rouge and powder;
even if you transcend this addition, you still have a transgression. How, then, do you all realize it?"
Chan Master Qinghuan Guanyin ascended the hall and said: "Virtuous Chan practitioners, if you wish to discuss Chan, speak of the Way, or proclaim the ancestral style, consider this:
within the very sphere of each person, upon a single tip of a hair there are immeasurable Buddhas turning the Great Dharma Wheel;
within a single speck of dust, the Jewel-King Lands appear. The Buddha speaks, sentient beings speak, and the mountains, rivers, and great earth all speak at once."
He spoke without ever ceasing. Like King Vaiśravaṇa, from beginning to end he never sought external treasures. Since each already possesses such a family tradition, who is lacking?
One must not seek further from others for its distribution. A monk asked, "What is the nature of the Dharma-realm?
The Master said, "Within your own body are the ten thousand phenomena. The monk asked, "How can one realize this? The Master said, "The void..."
Tang Xunsheng further sought out the origins and details.
Chan Master Kelong of Dongchan addressed the assembly: "This is truly a matter of great essential realization; yet you yourselves have not attained it.
If you are merely those who listen for echoes, it would be better for you to return to the hall and sit by the fire. Take care."
A monk asked National Teacher Suibian: "Does the person who is always present throughout the twelve hours of the day deserve the offerings of devas and humans?
The Master said, "He does not. The monk asked, "Why does he not deserve them?
The Master said, "Because you are always present. The monk asked, "As for the person who is not always present, does he deserve them? The Master said, "In a donkey’s year."
Chan Master Huai Lie of Yong’an ascended the hall. Looking around at those present, he said, “Why do you suffer from stammering? Then he returned to his quarters.
Ascending the hall again, after a long silence, he said, “Fortunately, they were naturally pitiable; yet they have been defiled once more.”
Master Guishan [Verse]: Someone cited the story of Prime Minister Pei, who convened a Dharma assembly and asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying?
The monk replied, "The Sutra of the Silent Child. The official asked, "How many fascicles does it have? The monk said, "Two fascicles.
The official said, "Since it is 'the silent one,' why are there two fascicles? The monk was speechless. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "If we discuss the 'silent one,' it is not only..."
In the two-fascicle [version] (the verses are found in Pei Xiu), Master Baoci Conghuan was asked by a monk:
"I have heard it said of old: 'If people today study the ancient teachings, they cannot avoid mental turmoil;
yet if they wish to avoid mental turmoil, they must study the ancient teachings. What, then, are the ancient teachings? The Master replied: "It is like..."

This is what I have heard. [A questioner] asked, "What is it that causes turmoil within the mind? The Master said, "The sound of sparrows over there. The Grand Councilor, Layman Wang Yanbin, visited Zhaoqing Temple for tea.
As he was there, the Senior Monk Lang and Mingzhao were holding the tea kettle. Suddenly, the kettle overturned. The Grand Councilor asked, "What is that under the tea stove?

Lang replied, "It is the Spirit Who Supports the Stove. The Grand Councilor said: [Commentary: When the Grand Councilor arrived at Zhaoqing for tea, Senior Monk Lang and Mingzhao were holding the kettle. Suddenly, the tea kettle overturned. The Master asked, "What is that beneath the tea stove? Lang said, "The Spirit Who Supports the Stove. The Master said:
"Since you are the incense-bearer deity, why did you overturn the tea? Lang said, "To serve an official for a thousand days, yet to lose him in a single morning.
Gong shook his sleeves and departed. Mingzhao said, "Venerable Lang, having eaten the rice of Zhaoqing, you have gone out to gather wild chestnuts.
Lang asked, "How about you, Venerable One? Mingzhao said, "A non-person has taken advantage of the situation."
A monk asked Chan Master Yanshou Huilun, "What is 'one color'? The Master said, "Blue, yellow, red, and white.
The monk said, "Excellent! One color! The Master said, "I thought there was no one; yet here is one, or perhaps half one."
When a monk asked Chan Master Wenqin Baoci, “What is the realm of all Buddhas?
the Master said, “When rain falls, clouds and mist darken; when it is clear and dry, the sun and moon shine bright. A monk asked, “What is the wondrously enlightened mind of clarity?
the Master said, “This winter’s fine late rice grows from the autumn rains. A monk asked, “What is the wondrous function that is as vast as the sands of the Ganges? the Master said, “Clouds arise.”
Emerald Peaks. Rain falls upon the blue heavens. Question: "What is the ordinary mind in accord with the Way? The Master said:
"Drink tea and eat rice, passing the time as it comes; gazing at the water and looking at the mountains truly delights the spirit."
A monk asked Chan Master Congchen of Fenghuang Mountain, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "If one's own gate-style is similar, there will be no obstruction;
however, you are not that person. The monk asked, "What would it be like if one were to suddenly encounter that person?"
The Master said, "One must not shake [the tree] beforehand while waiting for the itch. A student asked, "My faculties and thoughts are slow and hesitant;

within the gates of expedient means, I beg the Master for a side-glance. The Master said, "A side-glance. The student said, "I have deeply grasped the Master's intent; how would I dare speak further? The Master said, "That is too much."
A monk asked Chan Master Yonglong Huiying, "Why is it that for one who is unconditioned and without affairs, a golden lock is difficult to break?

The Master said, "Because the coarse and the subtle have been severed; being precious, it is difficult to retain. The monk asked, "Why do you say that for one who is unconditioned and without affairs, there is true joy in carefree wandering?
The Master said, "Because amidst the clamor and confusion, one must bring things to an end."
A monk asked the Abbot of Mount Yue-lu, "What is the phrase beyond sound and form? The Master said, "The howling of monkeys and the singing of birds.
A monk asked, "Please, Master, proclaim the phrase regarding the severing of the tongue. The Master said, "The sun can make it hot; the moon can make it cool."
Later, a monk asked Master Zhaoqing, "What is the house style of the Master? The Master said, "A single pitcher along with a single bowl;
everywhere is one's livelihood. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "In a state of bustling and haste:
the cock at dawn and the bell at dusk."
A monk asked Zen Master Jianshan Cheng, "The temporal teachings of a single era guide and lead beings of the present. I wonder, how do the ancestral masters instruct people?
The Master said, "Regarding the temporal teachings of a single era, someone has already asked about them. The monk asked, "How then does the Master instruct people?
The Master said, "I lament that the red amaranth tree before my courtyard produces leaves year after year, yet never bears flowers."
Chan Master Shaotong of Zhaoqing ascended the seat for the opening of the hall. A monk asked, "My fellow students do not understand at all;
I ask the Master to provide instruction. The Master said, "Do you even know how to laugh? He then said, "Those who are senior figures in the monastic community, I dare not offend or provoke.
But as for those who are beginners or junior students, if you have not yet believed, you must believe; if you have not yet realized, you must realize."
Do not engage in empty verbiage. The fundamental destination of all people has never for a single moment failed to be manifest;
there is not a single thing capable of covering it over. If you wish to know it, there is no need to shift even a hair’s breadth, nor is there need for the slightest effort.
Simply take it up within the state of an ordinary person of common ground. Would this not save you mental energy? Since you are already able to...
Enough said. You will then stand shoulder to shoulder with all Buddhas. Practice according to this; for this matter is a place of pure clarity.
Today, you must purify your body and mind to accord with it; only then will you naturally harmonize with the past and the present, and transcend birth and death. As the ancients said:
"One who recognizes the mind, realizes the fundamental, and understands the unconditioned dharma is alone entitled to be called a śramaṇa. Now...
All you officials and the great assembly must each understand this well; do not cast the entire burden onto the shoulders of the master-monks.
The Buddha-dharma is equal across all levels: from the Buddhas above down to all beings below, we share in this same matter.
This being so, who has it and who lacks it? Beyond your official duties, you must also exert yourselves. That I have spoken as much as I have just now was simply because there was no other way.
That is all. Do not say that such discourse is appropriate for the ancestral school of our tradition.
But as for this ancestral school—how should it be? Do you understand? If there is anyone who understands, I shall clear my debt to the tradition today.
I have stood for a long time before this great assembly. Take care. A Verse on the Expedient Means of Seated Meditation:

Among the four modes of deportment, sitting is primary; Purifying body and mind, they gradually become tranquil. If, in a fleeting moment, conditions arise that follow the turbid world, One must not allow them to continue—this is the way of the sages.
In practice, one simply learns by following the path of effort; How could the ultimate principle be discussed as being "over there"? At all times...

Constantly maintaining [this state], when causes and conditions converge, one suddenly penetrates the profound mystery. He said to those who cling to sitting meditation: "The Great Way is clearly manifest, utterly free from a speck of dust;

why must you sit for long periods to become intimate with it? If you can understand that whatever you encounter is without exception the Way, how could there be 'old' or 'new' amidst the clamor of the world?
Would you be willing to join the company of Zhi Dun in his carefree ease? How could you possibly dwell as a neighbor to Huiyou? Or...
Whether wandering among springs and rocks or amidst the bustling marketplace, he may truly be called one who dwells beyond the world of smoke and clouds.
A monk asked Chan Master Ziyi of India, "What was the underlying meaning when Danxia burned the wooden Buddha?

The Master said, "When cold, one surrounds a brazier and turns toward the fierce fire. The monk asked, "Is there still any fault in this? The Master said, "When hot, one goes to the banks of the bamboo grove stream."
He sat. [The student] asked, "How should one practice so as to immediately attain accord with the Way? The Master said, "Roll up the bamboo blinds high while chanting;
brew a strong cup of tea after sleep."

One day, Chan Master Baibun Zhi was ascending the hall at Mount Gu. He called out to the assembly; when the assembly all turned their heads, the Master threw open his robe to reveal his chest to them.
The assembly was at a loss, but only Master Zhi clearly awakened to its meaning. He entered the room to seek certification, and later, while attending the assembly, he continued his practice.
Mount Shàn called out, “Come forward! The Master stepped forward. Shàn said, “Nanquan called for the head of the monastery; what was his intention?

The Master folded his hands, maintained a solemn countenance, and withdrew to stand aside. Shàn smiled broadly, marveling at him. Later, when he resided [at a monastery], he ascended the hall and said:
“Is there anyone who can pose a question regarding the lineage of the Patriarchs? I shall wait for you to do so, and I will answer from within that very lineage.”
At that time, a monk came out to pay his respects. The Master then returned to his quarters. A monk asked, "What is the dragon’s cry within the withered tree?
The Master said, "A lotus blooming in fire. The monk asked, "What are the eyes within the skull? The Master said, "A clay ox entering the sea."
Chan Master Wenyi of Longshan ascended the hall and said: "If I were to bring up the essence of the school, the monastery would fall silent and the surroundings would become desolate.
If I were to leave it to your questions, what more would you wait for? Is there anyone here who understands thoroughly? Come forward and let us test you.
If no one understands, do not attempt to deceive with empty words. He then descended from his seat.
When Chan Master Zhizhe of Gushan first traveled to Huanglong in Ezhou, he asked, "I have long heard of Huanglong;
now that I have arrived, I see nothing but a striped red snake. The Dragon said, "You see only a striped red snake, yet you do not recognize Huanglong.
The Master asked, "What is Huanglong? The Dragon said, "Flowing and surging. The Master asked, "What if one encounters a golden-winged bird?"
"Come," [the Master] said. "And how is it? Long said, "Life and nature are difficult to preserve. The Master said, "In that case, you have been swallowed by him.
Long said, "I thank the Kalyāṇamitra for his sustenance. The Master then bowed.
On the day Chan Master Ba’en Qinghu ascended the hall, a monk asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, heavenly flowers fall in profusion.
When you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there? The Master replied, "Yesterday the new thunder rolled; this morning the fine rain falls."
A monk asked Master Jin of Ruiyan, “What is the realm of Ruiyan? The Master said, “Layer upon layer of overlapping peaks stretch far from the south;
toward the imperial capital, it is but a few inches away. The monk asked, “Who is the person within that realm?
The Master said, “Ten thousand miles of white clouds approach the Rui Peak; a fine drizzle sprinkles before the eaves. The monk asked, “How should one draw near to it?”
Regarding this person, the Master said: "I thought you, O *jiaoli*, had personally entered the inner chamber; it turns out you are still separated by ten thousand layers of barriers.
Chan Master Baoguo Zhao ascended the hall and said: "If I were to manifest my total capacity (*quanjī*), where would you go to grope for it?
It is simply because capacities are not equal that one becomes devoid of shame and remorse. Do you understand this far-reaching point? Now, for all of you gentlemen..."
To create a gateway for entry, he struck the meditation seat twice and said: "Do you see? Do you hear?
If you see, then see; if you hear, then hear. Do not attempt to speculate within the realm of consciousness, for that merely results in deluded thoughts and inverted views."
"There will be no time of emergence. Take care.
A monk asked Zen Master Longce Zixing, "Within the state of the absolute position (zhengwei), is there anyone who attains Buddhahood?
The Master said, "Who is a sentient being? The monk said, "If that is so, then everyone has already attained Buddhahood. The Master said, "Bring me back to the absolute position."
[The monk] asked, "What is the position of correctness? The Master said, "You are a sentient being.
A monk asked Chan Master Fuyao, "What is the house style of Fuyao? The Master said, "When seeing off guests, one does not go more than three paces;
when inviting guests, it is done only before the thatched hall. Ascending the hall, the Master said: "I, this mountain monk, now see..."
All you elders travel on foot in this manner, enduring hardship and suffering, crossing mountains and wading through ravines;
you never do so merely to sightsee at prefectures and counties or to seek out famous mountains and sacred sites—it is surely for the sake of this one great matter.
Now, I simply wish for you all to bring forth a message from within your own fundamental inquiry. If you do, I, Yunshan, dare to provide witness for it; not only that—
Yunshan testified to this, saying, "It is indeed a Buddha-land within the Zen grove; it also bears witness. [The Master asked,] "Is there anything further to be born?
The assembly all dispersed, and he then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Nanchan Yuyuan ascended the hall for the formal discourse. "How can this matter be treated? At that time, a monk came forward and said, "I ask the Master to speak.
The Master replied, "The moss on the streams of Muzhou; the stone pavilions of Jincheng."
A monk asked Chan Master Zifú Yuǎn, "Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral style do you inherit? The Master said, "The moon before the peaks of Snow Ridge;
its clarity shines within the waves of Mirror Lake. [Another] asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, the heavens rain down the four flowers."
The earth shook in six ways. "Venerable Master, what auspicious signs are there today? The Master replied, "When not a single thing arises, the whole body is revealed;
who knows the radiance before one's eyes?"
Once, Chan Master Wugu Yiyan was entering meditative absorption among a thicket of bamboo. Ants were gnawing at his robes, and withered leaves covered the steps.
Chan Master Zihu Nan did not yet know the depth of the Master’s realization and asked, "The concentration you dwell in is merely that of the Lesser Vehicle.
At that time, the Master was just drinking tea; he held up his tea bag and said, "Is this great or small? Zihu was struck with awe.
A monk asked Master Baiku Gui: "When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, the hundred birds brought flowers as offerings;
why did they no longer come after he saw him? The Master said: "Before the light of dawn has parted, all gaze expectantly;
once daybreak comes, it is just as usual."
Chan Master Changqing Zangyong ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, he threw his fan onto the ground and said, "The foolish person says gold is earth;
how does the wise person act? The younger generation is to be feared; you must not all simply remain in ignorance."
"Is there anyone who can speak? Come forward and speak! At that time, a monk came out, prostrated, and stood back.
The Master said, "What else could you say? The monk replied, "I beg the Master to look into this with clear discernment. The Master said, "A peach pit from a thousand years ago."
When Chan Master Shuifeng Zhidu first visited Anguo, he saw a monk ask, "What is the body alone revealed amidst the myriad phenomena?
Anguo held up a finger. The monk did not realize it, but the Master was thereby in profound accord with the mysterious principle.
He then entered the room and said, "Just now, seeing that monk’s question, I have reached a point of realization. Anguo asked, "What do you see?"
"What is the principle here? The Master also raised a finger and said, "What is this? Guo nodded in agreement, and the Master thanked him.
Later, after taking up residence, he ascended the hall and held up his whisk, saying: "This is what Caoxi never exhausted; people of the time call it 'the emergence of horns.
When I, this mountain monk, take it up to swat a mosquito, those who can realize it will find heaven and earth collapsing. A monk was there one night...
"Enter! The Master said, "Who is it? [The monk] replied, "I, so-and-so. The Master said, "Quanzhou sugar; betel nuts on the ship. The monk remained silent for a long while.

The Master asked, "Do you understand? [The monk] replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you understood, you would have cleared away the five aggregates and swallowed up the ten directions.
[Another monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "A wooden horse gallops like smoke; a stone man pursues it."
It was not yet sufficient. Master Ming of the Immortal School ascended the hall and said: "Fortunately, there is such a tradition of our school; why do you not propagate it with brilliant splendor?
If you can propagate it, you will not be within the three realms. If you were to leave the three realms, you would destroy the three realms. If you remain..."
The three realms are precisely the obstruction of the three realms; that which is unobstructed and indestructible is both exiting the three realms and not exiting the three realms.
To penetrate thus thoroughly is fit to be the seed of the Buddha-dharma; humanity and the heavens shall have cause for reliance. At that time, a monk asked:
"If grasping the clouds does not depend on wind and thunder, how can one pass through the body amidst the surging waves? The Master said: "How can you abandon the root to pursue the branches?"
A monk asked Chan Master Anguo Xiang, "When responding to things and manifesting form, it is like the moon in water. What is the moon?
The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "Why did the ancients say that the moon in water has no form? The Master replied, "What do you see?"
Chan Master Baofu Qinghuo visited Shuilong. Shuilong asked him, "Master Huo, which venerable elder have you come to see?

Have you attained realization yet? He replied, "I once visited Dazhang and gained a point of conviction. Thereupon, Shuilong ascended the hall, gathered the assembly, and called out, "Master Huo, come forward!
Burn incense before the assembly and speak of your realization; I shall grant you [the seal of approval]."

To provide proof: The Master came forth from the assembly and held up the incense, saying, "The incense has already been offered; whether you have awakened or not. Long Da Yue was greatly pleased and granted him permission.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a poor family suffers a robbery? The Master said, "He could not take everything."
[The student] asked, "Why is it that one cannot go to the very bottom? The Master said, "The thief is a member of the family.
[The student] asked, "If he is a member of the family, why does he instead become a family thief? The Master said, "Since there is no response within, he cannot act without.
[The student] asked, "What happens when he is suddenly caught? The Master said, "Within and without, all news is cut off. [The student] asked, "After he is caught, where does the merit reside?"
The Master said, "I have never heard of such a thing being rewarded. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then one toils but achieves no merit.

The Master said, "Merit is indeed not lacking; it is simply that once accomplished, one does not dwell within it. [The monk] asked, "Since you have achieved success, why do you not dwell within it? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said:
'Peace was originally brought about by the generals, yet they are not permitted to witness that peace'? The Master then suddenly left the assembly.
Desiring to enter the mountains to await his passing, he left behind this verse: "Let the people of the world cease speaking of the hardships of the road;
The path of birds and the sheep’s gut are but a few inches apart. Take care, O waters of the Nüxi stream; You shall return to the vast ocean, while I shall return to the mountains.
He then went to Guihu to establish a hermitage. Not long after, he said to his disciples: "After my passing, you shall offer my remains to the insects and ants. Do not..."
The construction of stupas and pagodas.
A monk asked Zen Master Zhihong of Dulong Mountain, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "It is you yourself.
The monk asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "Do you still find fault with a bowl that has no handle? [Question: What is the subtle and wondrous?
The Master said: "The wind carries the sound of water to the side of my pillow; the moon shifts the shadow of the mountains onto my bed. [Commentary] [Verse]: Question:

When the physical body (rūpakāya) decays and perishes, what is the indestructible Dharma-body (dharmakāya)? The Master said: "Mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the stream water is as deep blue as indigo."
Chan Master Xing’ai of Baima Mountain [Verse]: A monk asked, “What is the pure *dharmakāya*?
The Master said, “A frog at the bottom of the well swallows the moon. [Verse] A monk asked, “What is the true eye of Baima? The Master said, “Facing south, look at the Big Dipper.”
A monk asked Master Xingjiao Puchan: "The profound teachings fill the dragon palaces and overflow the ocean treasuries.
I do not ask about the true exposition; what is the Dharma of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, "In the eyes, in the ears, in the nose.
The monk said, "Is this it right here? The Master said, "What is it? The monk gave a shout. The Master also shouted.
The Monk Dazhu (the Second Patriarch) asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "How clever!
The monk said, "I thank the Master for his instruction. The Master said, "How pitiable! The monk bowed. The Master said, "When I speak thus, where does it fall?
The monk was speechless. The Master said, "He has no wound himself; do not inflict one upon him."
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Zhiyong, "What is the fundamental source of all Buddhas?
The Master said, "This very question—what is its source? The monk said, "If that is so, then all Buddhas must be without distinction.
The Master said, "The sword of Yanping has already become a dragon; yet there are still those who seek it by marking the boat."
A monk asked Chan Master Cheng of Xuandu, "I am delighted to have come to the abbot’s quarters; what is the style of your house?

The Master said, "The western wind opens the morning dew; the bright moon is exactly in the sky. The monk asked, "How do you provide salvation? The Master said, "One stroke of the drum atop the Golden Cock Tower."

The Realized One Lü Yán, whose courtesy name was Dōngbīn, first studied under Huánglóng. Upon hearing the Master’s words, he attained immediate realization. Lü composed a verse, saying: "I cast away my gourd-bag and smashed my lute;
Now I no longer crave gold within the mercury. Since the moment I first beheld Huánglóng, [All delusions have been severed at their root]."
Initial awakening arises from previous errors in the application of the mind. The Dragon (Nāga) entrusted him with the charge to provide protection.
Chan Master Puzhao Yu ascended the hall and said: "Thirty years hence, there will be many who, at this very point, will lose their wits and be left speechless.
After a long silence, he asked: "Do you understand? Truly, were it not for a true lion cub, how could one recognize [this]?"
He attained the opportunity for the Supreme Vehicle (*agrayāna*). At that time, a monk asked: "What is it like when the lion has not yet emerged from its cave?
The Master said: "The other beasts are in vain. The monk asked: "What is it like after he has emerged? The Master said: "Solitary and absolute for ten thousand miles. The monk asked:

"What is it like when he intends to emerge but does not? The Master said: "Those who go to the court perish. The monk asked: "As for what lies ahead, what is it like? The Master said: "It is decided at the moment of facing it."
Feng. The monk prostrated. The Master spoke in verse: "Decisive at the moment of the edge, The natural mechanism of the lion.
A single snarl sends one beyond the three realms; None but the Patriarchs can know it."
When Chan Master Hongjin of Qingxi was serving as the First Seat under Dizang, one day Dizang ascended the hall.
Two monks came forward and prostrated; Dizang said, "Both are wrong. The two monks were speechless. After the assembly left the hall, they requested instruction from Master Xiu.
Xiu said, "You yourself are towering and majestic, yet you pay homage and intend to question others; is this not a mistake? When the Master heard this, he did not approve.
Xiu then asked, "I wonder, Senior, what about you? The Master replied, "You are yourself deluded and ignorant; how can you act as a teacher for others?
Xiu was incensed and went to the Abbot’s quarters to seek instruction. Baizhang pointed toward the corridor and said, "The Head Cook."
He entered the storehouse and departed. Xiu then realized his error. [Verse: One day the Master asked Master Xiu, "You clearly understand the principle that birth is non-birth;
why then are you carried away by birth and death? Xiu replied, "A bamboo shoot will inevitably become a bamboo stalk.
Now, could it still be used as a strip of bamboo? The Master said, "You shall realize this for yourself in the future."
Xiu said, "My own understanding is only this much. What is your intention, Venerable Sir? The Master pointed and said, "This is the Director's quarters;
that is the Steward's quarters. Xiu then prostrated in thanks. While the Master was walking in meditation, the assembly of monks followed him.
He then said to the assembly, "What sayings from the ancients are there for us all to deliberate upon? At that time, there was...
When the Venerable Yī stepped forward from the assembly intending to pose a question, the Master said, "This hairless donkey! At these words, Yī attained sudden and radiant enlightenment.
Zen Master Qingliang Xiufu once said of himself: "If I rely on verbal expression, I am stuck with the raft;

if I seek to advance toward profound stillness, I again fear falling into emptiness. Since I could not resolve this dilemma of advancing or retreating, I abandoned both extremes and went to seek out a master of the school."
Relying on Dizang, for years they were not in accord, until [Dongshan] fell ill and entered the Nirvana Hall. One night, Dizang went to see him and asked, "Is the Senior Monk well?
The Master replied, "I am at odds with the Master's karmic conditions. Dizang pointed to the lantern and said, "Do you see this?
The Master said, "I see it. Dizang said, "Even this very thing is not at odds. At these words, the Master attained realization.
[The Master] said, "I have attained realization. A monk asked, "What did the ancients attain that they were able to rest immediately? The Master said, "What have you attained that you do not rest?
He asked the Dharma Master Zhong, "Which sutra are you lecturing on? [Zhong] replied, "The Lotus Sutra.
The Master said, "Wherever the Lotus Sutra is being preached, I manifest a jeweled stupa to serve as a witness. Great Virtue," [the Master continued].
"What person can testify to this? Zhong had no reply. (Fadeng said: "I thank the Master for the lamp-light.
Chan Master Longji Xiu [Verse]: Initially, he studied together with Fayan under Dizang. What he attained, he considered to have reached the ultimate.
When Yan and Tong arrived at Jianyang together, during their conversation on the way, Yan suddenly asked, "The ancients said, 'Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.
Does this negate the myriad phenomena, or does it not negate them? The Master replied, "It does not negate them. Yan said, "What do you mean by 'negate' or 'not negate'?
The Master was utterly bewildered and did not know how to respond. He returned to Dizang. Before long, Dizang asked him, "You have been gone for no great length of time; why [is it that...]"?
He returned, and the Master said, "I have a matter that remains unresolved; do you not fear the long journey across mountains and rivers?

Zang replied, "The many mountains and rivers you have traversed are not insignificant either. The Master did not understand his meaning and asked, "An ancient said, 'Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed.
What is the intent of this? Zang replied, "Tell me, does the ancient negate the myriad phenomena, or does he not negate them?"

The Master said, "I do not strike them away. Zang said, "There are two. The Master was startled; he reflected deeply and then asked, "I wonder, did the ancients strike away the myriad phenomena, or did they not strike them away?
Zang said, "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'? Only then did the Master achieve awakening.
He took his leave of Dizang once more to visit Fayan. Fayan’s words and meaning were identical to those with which Dizang had previously instructed him.
1. [Verse] Entering the Hall: "The ordinary person possesses the dharmas of an ordinary person, yet the ordinary person does not know them.
The sage possesses the dharmas of a sage, yet the sage does not realize them. If the sage were to realize them, he would be an ordinary person;

if the ordinary person were to know them, he would be a sage. These two phrases have one principle and two meanings. If a person can discern them, there will be a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma. If...
"I cannot discern it. Do not say you do not doubt this; take care. A monk asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Cuiyan.
The Master said, "What words or phrases did Cuiyan use to instruct his disciples? He replied, "He usually says: 'When you go out the door, you meet Maitreya;
when you enter the gate, you see Śākyamuni. The Master said, "How can one speak in such a way? He asked, "And how about you, Master? The Master said, "Go out!"

"Who have you encountered at the gate? Upon entering the gate, what do you see? At these words, the monk attained realization. Ascending the hall, he said: "Where sound and form do not reach, the illness lies in seeing and hearing. Where verbal explanations fall short, the fault lies in the lips. A monk asked, "Setting aside sound and form, please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Bring your question forward from within sound and form. [Verse]: When the kalpa-fire blazes forth, asking—what is it that does not burn? When the great wind blows, asking—what is it that does not move? If you can discern this, you will know the place where the Buddha-way is revealed. If you cannot discern it, you will remain lost in the dark. If you wish to avoid the pitfall of the two extremes, you must first understand the meaning of the Middle Way. If you can understand it, you will see the moon; if you cannot understand it, you will see the stars. If you can see the moon, you will transcend the world; if you can see the stars, you will sink into the abyss. If you can transcend the world, you will be free from birth and death; if you sink into the abyss, you will wander through the three realms. Therefore, I urge you all: do not be negligent. If you are negligent, you will surely fall into the pit of the two extremes. If you do not fall into the pit of the two extremes, you will naturally enter the gate of the Middle Way. If you enter the gate of the Middle Way, you will attain the fruit of Buddhahood. If you attain the fruit of Buddhahood, you will benefit yourself and others. If you benefit yourself and others, you will repay the four debts of gratitude. If you repay the four debts of gratitude, you will be called a true disciple of the Buddha. If you are a true disciple of the Buddha, you will never again be subject to the cycle of birth and death. This is truly a matter of great importance. Do not take it lightly. Be careful! Be careful! [Verse]: When the kalpa-fire blazes forth, asking—what is it that does not burn? When the great wind blows, asking—what is it that does not move? If you can discern this, you will know the place where the Buddha-way is revealed. If you cannot discern it, you will remain lost in the dark. If you wish to avoid the pitfall of the two extremes, you must first understand the meaning of the Middle Way. If you can understand it, you will see the moon; if you cannot understand it, you will see the stars. If you can see the moon, you will transcend the world; if you can see the stars, you will sink into the abyss. If you can transcend the world, you will be free from birth and death; if you sink into the abyss, you will wander through the three realms. Therefore, I urge you all: do not be negligent. If you are negligent, you will surely fall into the pit of the two extremes. If you do not fall into the pit of the two extremes, you will naturally enter the gate of the Middle Way. If you enter the gate of the Middle Way, you will attain the fruit of Buddhahood. If you attain the fruit of Buddhahood, you will benefit yourself and others. If you benefit yourself and others, you will repay the four debts of gratitude. If you repay the four debts of gratitude, you will be called a true disciple of the Buddha. If you are a true disciple of the Buddha, you will never again be subject to the cycle of birth and death. This is truly a matter of great importance. Do not take it lightly. Be careful! Be careful!
"When the great trichiliocosm is destroyed, I do not know whether this [reality] is also destroyed. The Master said, "It is not destroyed. [The monk] asked, "Why is it not destroyed?

The Master said, "Because it is identical to the great trichiliocosm. [Another time,] he ascended the hall and said: "Rolling up the curtain removes obstructions; closing the door creates impediments.
As for these very obstructions and impediments, no one from ancient times to the present has understood them. To understand them is to be obstructed; not to understand them is likewise obstructed."

[The Master was] sovereign. A monk asked, "What is it like when the ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "It shines through heaven and earth. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has been polished?
The Master said, "It is pitch black. The Master had a verse that said: "When the wind moves, the mind shakes the tree; When clouds arise, nature gives birth to dust.
If you understand today's affairs, You have obscured the person of original nature. All phenomena are the radiance of the mind.
All conditions are merely phenomena; fundamentally, there is no person who is deluded or awakened.
It simply requires realization this very day. A monk asked Chan Master Yanyue Chuan of Yanqing: "When one sees form, one sees the mind. The lantern is form;
which one is the mind? The Master said: "You do not understand the meaning of the ancients. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the ancients? The Master said: "The lantern."
"This mind. [Verse] Question: "If one can transform things, one is identical to the Tathāgata. I do not yet understand what kind of thing is transformed. The Master said: "Speak!
The monk was about to offer a reply when the Master said: "This lacquer bucket! (This case is recorded in the first fascicle of the *Songgu*, within the chapter on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*).
A monk asked Zen Master Shouan of Nantai, "What is it like when all is silent and there is nothing to rely upon?

The Master said, "As for that which is silent, listen! He then presented this verse: Sitting in stillness at Nantai, a single burner of incense; All day long, composed and unmoving, ten thousand anxieties vanish.
This is not merely quelling the mind to eliminate delusive thoughts; It is simply because there is nothing whatsoever to be pondered.
Chan Master Guangping Xuanzhi ascended the hall and said: "Is there anyone here who can provide verification?

If there were someone who could verify this, it would spare us from failing our ancestors and neglecting those who come after. If you are merely seeking words and phrases, they are clearly present throughout the Great Canon.
But as for the Gate of the Ancestors, what is so strange about speaking thus? These too are but words cast aside."

[Commentary] [Verse] The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Mount Lu. The Master said, "Have you ever been to the Five Elders Peak? He replied, "I have not."
The Master said, "Ācārya, you have never traveled the mountains" (Yunmen said: These words were all spoken out of compassion; they are talk that descends into the weeds). Ascending the hall, he said:

"All of you, each turn the light inward and reflect back upon yourselves. Do not merely memorize my words. Since beginningless kalpas, you have turned your backs on the light and cast yourselves into darkness;
the roots of your deluded thoughts are deep and cannot be uprooted suddenly. Therefore, I provisionally employ skillful means to seize your coarse consciousness."
It is like using yellow leaves to stop a child’s crying—what validity is there in such a thing?
It is also like a person who takes a hundred kinds of goods and sells them together with gold and jewels in one shop, intending only to gauge the customer's capacity for value. Therefore it is said:
"Shitou’s place is a shop of pure gold; my place here is a general merchandise shop. If someone comes seeking mouse droppings, I likewise pick some up and give it to them."
"Come seeking true gold; I shall also pick some up and give it to you. At that time, a monk asked, "I do not want the mouse droppings;

I ask for the Master’s true gold. The Master said, "To bite the arrowhead and attempt to open one's mouth—even in a donkey’s year, one will still not understand. The monk had no reply. The Master said:
If one calls out for it, there is a transaction; if one does not call out for it, there is none.

If I were to speak of the Chan school, I would not even have a single person to accompany me by my side, let alone a multitude of five hundred or seven hundred followers. If I were to speak of this or that, [it would be like that].
Then you will scramble forward with your heads to pick them up, like using an empty fist to deceive a small child; there is no substance in it at all.
I shall now clearly explain to you the matters on the side of the Holy One. Do not attempt to fix your mind upon them; simply turn toward the ocean of your own nature.
Practice according to reality. There is no need for the three knowledges (*vidyā*) or the six supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). Why? Because these are merely the peripheral matters of the noble ones.
For now, you must simply recognize the mind and penetrate the root. Once you have attained the root, you need not worry about the branches;
at some point in the future, they will naturally be complete. If you have not attained the root, even if you exert your emotions and imitate others, you will not succeed. Have you not seen this?
Master Guishan said: "When the sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted, the essence reveals the true permanence;
when phenomena and principle are non-dual, one is the Buddha of Suchness. The Master returned to Mount Gui to pay his respects. Guishan asked:

"Since you call yourself a good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), how do you distinguish those who come from various quarters—those who know [the Way] and those who do not, those with a teacher and those without, those who study the doctrines (yìxué) and those who pursue the profound (xuán)?"
"Disciple, try to explain it. The Master said, "Huiji has a point of verification. Whenever a monk comes, I simply hold up my whisk and ask him:
'Do the elders of all quarters speak of this or not? He further said, 'Setting this aside for a moment, what is the intention of the elder masters of all quarters?
Guishan sighed and said, 'This is the very fang-tooth and claw of the ancestral school. [Verse] Guishan asked.
"The sentient beings of the great earth have their karmic consciousnesses wandering in a vast blur, with no foundation to rely upon. How do you know whether they exist or not?
The Master said, "Huiji has a way to verify it. At that moment, a monk passed by in front of him, and the Master called out to him:
"Ācārya," the monk replied. "Monk," the Master said, "this is precisely what is called 'vague karmic consciousness,' having no fundamental basis to rely upon.
Baizhang said, "This is a single drop of a lion’s milk that scatters six bushels of donkey’s milk. The Master asked a monk:

"Where does the fault lie? [The monk] replied, "It is not fitting for you, Master, to show people such a scene. The Master then struck him. [Verse]: A Brahman monk arrived from the air.

He replied, “It is early. The Master said, “Why are you so late? He replied, “I was wandering the mountains and enjoying the waters.

If you can speak [the truth], I shall keep it; if you cannot, I shall smash it. The assembly remained silent.

Having sat down and put on his robe, he turned back to look at himself. [The disciples] bowed in prostration and expressed their gratitude. As the Master was about to pass into *parinirvāṇa*, several monks stood in attendance.

"Fundamentally, before your parents were even born, try to utter a single word. When the Master was thus questioned, he was left utterly bewildered.

If one discusses this matter, it is like a person climbing a tree who has a branch in his mouth, yet neither his feet nor his hands touch the branches.

The Master said: "When the grain is ripe, one does not wait for the field. A questioner asked: "What is it like when it is like frost and like snow?
The Master said: "It is still a defilement. The questioner asked: "What is it like when there is no defilement? The Master said: "It is of a different color."

The Master let out a thunderous shout. The leader did not awaken; he struck the Master with his blade.

The Master said, "Where have you seen the Buddhas of the three periods of time? A monk asked, "One flower opens and five petals emerge;
the fruiting occurs naturally. What is 'one flower opening and five petals emerging'? The Master said, "The sun rises and the moon is bright. [The monk] asked, "What about..."
"This is the fruition that is spontaneously accomplished. The Master said, "Heaven and earth are bright and clear. Ascending the hall, he said:
"In general, when speaking words, one must ensure they are free from leakage before they are acceptable. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the sentence that is free from leakage? The Master said:
"Your mouth resembles your nostrils. [The monk] asked, "What is not realizing a single dharma? The Master said, "Wait for the words to finish.
[The monk] asked, "What is realizing all dharmas? The Master said, "Why are you drunk?
He then said, "Just as when this mountain monk answers him in this way, how do you all, venerable seniors, understand it? Is it being truly helpful? Is it being exactly so..."
At such a time, is there not a single dharma to be realized? Is it perhaps recognizing his place of origin? Is it perhaps the total manifestation of one’s entire being? Do not misunderstand!
Such an understanding is called "clinging to grass and leaning on wood"; it is worlds apart from the Buddha-dharma.
Even if one’s ability to respond and discern were like a cascading river, one would still only attain a perverted view.
If you merely value repartee and the art of discerning debate, what difficulty could there be? I only fear that it will be of no benefit to others and, on the contrary, lead to deception and error.
As for the various forms of discerning debate, questioning and answering, memorization, and the exposition of principles that you have studied in the past—why does your state of doubt not cease?
Why is it that when you hear the expedient means of the ancient sages, you specifically fail to understand them? It is simply because [your practice] is full of emptiness and lacks substance.
"Venerable Elder, it is not like this. You should look right from beneath your heels and see through it all at once. What principle is there?
How many Dharma gates could there possibly be to provide you with doubts and a quest for understanding?

Only then will you know that all those things you have studied until now are merely the root-source of birth and death, the livelihood within the realms of the aggregates. Therefore, the ancients said: 'If seeing and hearing are not shed, it is like...'"
The moon in the water. No need for anything; take care. [Verse] Addressing the assembly, he said: "At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this world. Outside the mind there is no dharma;
before one's eyes are green mountains. (Fayan heard this and said: "By this single verse alone, my school may be established. ○ Entering the hall, a monk asked: "I have heard an ancient saying:
'If a person sees Prajñā, they are bound by Prajñā. If a person does not see Prajñā, they are likewise bound...'"
"Bondage by Prajñā. [The student asked: "Since one has already seen Prajñā, why is one instead bound by it? The Master said: "Tell me, what does Prajñā see?
[The student] said: "It does not see Prajñā. [The Master asked: "Why, then, is one still bound? The Master said: "Tell me, where does Prajñā not see? He then said:
"If you see Prajñā, it is no longer called Prajñā; if you do not see Prajñā, it is likewise not [Prajñā]."
It is named Prajñā. For now, how can one speak of seeing or not seeing? Therefore, the ancients said: "If there is even one dharma lacking, it does not constitute the Dharmakāya;
if there is even one dharma remaining, it does not constitute the Dharmakāya; if there is even one dharma present, it does not constitute the Dharmakāya."
"If there were not even a single dharma, the Dharmakāya would not be established; this is the true essence of Prajñā. (And so forth. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Buddha-dharma is already perfected; all is complete. Have you not heard it said: 'Perfectly identical to the great void, lacking nothing and having no excess'?"
If it is thus, then who is lacking and who is in surplus? Who is right and who is wrong? Who is the one who understands and who is the one who does not understand?
Therefore it is said: "Going east is also the Seat-Holder; going west is also the Seat-Holder; going south is also the Seat-Holder; going north is also the Seat-Holder.
For what reason do these directions—east, west, south, and north—come to be established? If you understand this...
It is attained. Spontaneously, the paths of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are cut off, and all dharmas manifest before one.
Why is this so? Because the Dharmakāya is formless, yet whatever meets the eye takes on form; Prajñā is without cognition, yet it illuminates in response to conditions.
You must grasp this thoroughly and completely all at once. Venerable Elders, how should those who have left the household life act? This is the principle of original existence. It has not yet...

This is beyond the ordinary. To recognize the mind and penetrate the source is what is called being a śramaṇa. If you recognize the mind as luminously clear, there is truly not even a hair’s breadth of obstruction.
The Elder has stood for a long time; take care. [He] ascended the hall. A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say..."
