Like hooks and like chains; like gold and gold. At every stage they are perfectly equal, without the slightest discrepancy, and without mutual confusion.
They are neither one nor different, neither identical nor distinct. If one returns to the ground of reality, every phenomenon reaches its ultimate depth.
It is not that it is so when one asks "how" or "what," nor is it otherwise when one does not ask. This is while residing upon the long benches of the monastic hall.
When one is seated, it exists; when one is not seated, it does not exist. Yet, the teachings of the venerable elders throughout all quarters remain in the world like the sands of the Ganges River.
Every scroll of the Tathāgata’s Great Canon speaks of the Buddha’s principle; every sentence expresses the Buddha’s mind.
Why, then, is there failure to understand? If one were to exclusively weave together these teachings and seek understanding through the conscious intellect—
Even if the Venerable Rāhula were to pass through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, he would still be unable to penetrate it thoroughly. This is called inverted knowledge and views;
it is merely the calculating mind’s livelihood, and there is no place where it gains power. This is because one has not clarified what lies beneath the heels of one’s feet.

If one exhaustively investigates the source of all Buddhas' Dharma, the great treasuries as numerous as the sands of the Ganges will all at once manifest before one—neither lacking even a hair’s breadth, nor exceeding it by a hair’s breadth. All...
The Buddha constantly appears in the world and constantly preaches the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, never ceasing for a moment.

Even down to the cries of monkeys and the calls of birds, and the grasses, trees, and thickets, they always assist the Elder in triggering his realization. There has not been a single moment when these things have not served the Elder.
Such extraordinary wonders are truly to be cherished; all you Elders, investigate this thoroughly so that the Dharma may long abide in the world.
[Interval. May the lifespans of humans and devas increase; may the King enjoy peace and happiness; may all be free from trouble. Take care.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited an ancient saying: "I have a single word that reaches both heaven and earth. If people do not understand it, there are only green waters and blue mountains.
But what is the principle of this "single word"? One must truly comprehend the words of the ancients before one can grasp them. If one were to...

To speak and give names to what is spoken—there has not yet been a point of realization here. It is precisely because one has thoroughly investigated the root and stem of all phenomena that one finally understands this single word.
This is not a matter of intellectualizing or conceptualizing a single word or half-sentence and calling it "one word.

If you understand that words are cut off and the sphere of mental activity is extinguished, only then do you reach the realm of the ancients. Nor is it a matter of closing your eyes and hiding your sight in the dark.
Within this, there is nothing to be seen. To call it "the cutting off of the path of words" is merely a way to prevent misunderstanding;

the Buddha-dharma is not such a principle. Do you wish to understand? Even if one were to speak for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, not even half a phrase would ever reach you, venerable ones.
Yet, even if one did not speak for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, not even half a phrase would ever be lacking. You must understand this thoroughly to the very bottom.
Only then can one attain it. If you scrutinize names and words in this manner, you will merely exhaust your mind and strength to no avail.

Let this be a mutual testimony for all the senior monks; those of later generations and beginners must quickly investigate and realize this. I shall remain standing for a long time; take care. Ascending the hall, he said briefly:
"One must attain thorough, bottom-to-top clarity and penetration before one can succeed. This is not a matter of asking about a single phrase or memorizing a single..."
They twist words and craftily construct rationalizations; using metaphors of wind, clouds, water, and moon, they pair four, six, and eight characters, treating these as the Buddha-dharma.
Do not deceive yourselves, O venerable elders! In the end, it is of no benefit.
Chan Master Qingliang Taichin was born with an innate understanding of the Way. His eloquence was unimpeded, and he entered the chamber of the Dharma-eye;

the assembly gathered around him like the sea, all of whom declared him a "skilled craftsman. Initially, he resided at Shuanglin Monastery in Hongzhou. On the day he ascended the hall, he pointed to the Dharma seat and said:
"Venerable predecessors of this mountain have once before preached the Dharma here. This seat is lofty and vast; how could one of such meager talent ascend it? Ancient...
Formerly it was said: "One must pay obeisance to the Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja before one can sit.
But tell me, where is the Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja now? Does the assembly wish to see him? [The Master] prostrated himself all at once and then ascended the seat.
After a long silence, he said: "The assembly is just like this. Is there anyone who understands? A monk asked: "What is the Double Grove (Śāla Grove)?"
“Scene,” he said. “Even a painting cannot capture it. The monk asked, “What is one within the scene? The Master said, “Go away for now.
You have not even recognized the scene; first seek out the person.”
When Chan Master Lingyin Qingsong first visited Fayan, Fayan pointed to the falling rain and said to him, "Every drop falls into the eyes of the Venerable.
At first, the Master did not understand the meaning; later, upon reading the *Avatamsaka Sūtra*, he attained realization and received Fayan’s seal of approval.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Buddhas of the ten directions are always before you; do you see them?
If you say you see them, do you see them with your mind or with your eyes? Therefore it is said: 'All phenomena are neither born nor extinguished.
If one can understand in this way, the Buddhas are ever manifest. It is also said: 'When seeing form, one sees the mind. But what do you call 'mind'? He then pointed to the mountain.
The great earth and rivers, the myriad phenomena arrayed before us—blue, yellow, red, white, male, female, and all such forms—are they the mind or not the mind?
If they are the mind, why do they instead become external objects? If they are not the mind, yet it is said that "upon seeing form, one sees the mind.
Do you understand? It is simply because of delusion regarding this that inversion arises, resulting in all manner of differences within what is fundamentally non-different.

Among differences, one forcibly creates similarities and differences. Suppose for a moment that you directly accept this right now; suddenly your original mind is revealed, and it is so luminously clear that not a single thing exists that can be seen or heard.
If you seek liberation apart from the mind, the ancients called this "searching for the source in the waves"—it will be difficult to achieve awakening.
A monk asked: "When both the sense faculties and their objects have vanished, why is it that phenomena and principle are not yet clear? The Master said: [The text here is incomplete].
He said, "Setting aside matters and principles for a moment, what do you call the sense organs and their objects when both are utterly extinguished?
A monk asked, "It is said that the true nature of ignorance is itself Buddha-nature. What is Buddha-nature? The Master said, "What do you call ignorance?
A monk asked, "What is Mahāprajñā? The Master said, "The snow falls vast and boundless. The monk was speechless. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "No."
[The assembly] gathered. The Master presented a verse, saying: "Mahāprajñāpāramitā is neither grasped nor abandoned; if people do not realize this, there will be wind, cold, and falling snow.
When Chan Master Guizong Yirou ascended the seat for the opening of the hall, the Rector struck the gavel and said: "In this Dharma assembly, there is a multitude of dragons and elephants."
"One should contemplate the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*). The Master said, "If it is the ultimate truth, then how do you contemplate it?
When you speak thus, where does it fall? Is it contemplation, or is it that one is not permitted to contemplate? Elder Xiande, may you all provide mutual testimony.
You students who have recently begun your studies, do not call this a "reversal question" or a "leaning-back" statement. If you have doubts, please ask.

A monk asked, "When the Buddhas appear in the world, they preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings, moving both heaven and earth. When you, Master, appear in the world, what auspicious signs are there?
The Master said, "Before the great assembly of humans and devas, why do you prattle like a child? He asked another monk, "What sutra are you reading?"
[The monk] said, "The *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*. The Master said, "Since you are a śramaṇa, why are you reading the *Ratnakūṭa Sūtra*? The monk was speechless.
The Master spoke on his behalf, saying: "Its application throughout antiquity and the present is inexhaustible."

Chan Master Baizhang Daoheng went to study under Fayan. He requested instruction on the story of the outsider’s question to the Buddha: "I do not ask about having words; I do not ask about having no words.
Before he had finished speaking, Fayan said, "Stop! Stop! Do you intend to understand this at the point where the World-Honored One remained silent for a long while?
From this, the Master attained awakening. A monk asked, "An ancient said: 'Śākyamuni and I have studied together.'"
“I do not know for certain whom you have visited. The Master said, “Only those of like training will know. [The monk] asked, “I do not know for certain how one should approach such a person.
The Master said, “If that were so, then you do not understand how to practice Zen.

[The monk] asked, “What is the single phrase by which Bai Zhang saves people? The Master said, “If you go to other places, you must ask about this everywhere. He then added, “In truth, there is nothing at all.”
Each and every person here is a Buddha; what further doubt could there be? Having reached this point, an ancient said: "The ten directions gather together as one;
each and every one studies non-action. This is the field for selecting Buddhas; with an empty mind, they return having passed the imperial examination.
But what is this "empty mind"? It is not merely sitting there with eyes closed in cold stillness—that is precisely the functioning of the conscious intellect.
Consider this: does the Elder wish to realize the emptiness of the mind? Simply recognize the mind, and you will see that the mind is empty.
Therefore it is said: "The past has already passed; do not calculate the future. Sit upright and without concern; who has ever called out to you?"
If someone calls out to you, Elder, you should respond; it is not right not to respond. If you respond, who would call out to the Elder?
If you do not respond, yet you are not deaf either. The substance of the three periods of time is empty, yet you are certainly not a block of wood.
Therefore, the ancients said: "When the mind is empty, one may see the Dharma King. But do you see the Dharma King? It is none other than this old, sick monk.
Do not say that he merely praises himself; take care! A monk cited a person asking Xuansha: "I do not ask about the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings;
what is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Xuansha replied: "The Three Vehicles and the twelve..."
"The teaching of the two divisions is unnecessary. I do not understand it; I beg the Master to explain it for me. The Master said, "You truly do not understand.
[The monk] said, "I truly do not understand. The Master showed him this verse: "Do not seek the Three Vehicles; seek the ancestral source. That the Three Vehicles are unnecessary is shared with you.
If you now wish to comprehend the fundamental principle, Listen to the night-owl’s cry on the chaotic peaks after midnight. [He] ascended the hall. To all the monks above...
"Take your seat. Just now, as you came out from the Sangha Hall, before your feet had even crossed the threshold, you turned back;
that was already a repetition of the verse. To come here again would be an excessive redundancy. As the ancients said:"
It is better to investigate for oneself than to rely on another. Therefore it is said: "The myriad phenomena of the universe are the master of Sudhana;
karmic delusions and worldly toil are the realm of Samantabhadra. If you can investigate in this way, you will be investigating alongside Sudhana.
If you are unwilling to investigate in this manner, then return to the hall and warm yourself by the fire, and investigate the Brahmin Jvalamukha. Be careful. *Oṃ.*
He ascended the hall. As soon as the assembly had gathered, he said, "Go drink tea. At other times when the assembly had gathered, he would say, "Take care" (zhēnzhòng).
Or at other times when the assembly had gathered, he would simply say, "Rest. Later, he provided a verse on this: "Bai Zhang has three secrets: Drink tea, take care, and rest."
To accept it directly and immediately—dare I say you have not yet reached the bottom.
Chan Master Daoyan of Yongming in Hangzhou [Verse]: When he first visited Fayan, Fayan asked him, "Aside from your formal inquiries and requests for instruction, what sutra are you studying?
The Master replied, "The Avataṃsaka Sūtra. Fayan said, "Regarding the six aspects of totality, particularity, sameness, difference, formation, and disintegration—"
"To which section does this belong? The Master said, "The text is within the *Daśabhūmika* chapter.
According to the principle, all phenomena, both mundane and supramundane, possess the six aspects. Huayan said, "Does emptiness itself also possess the six aspects?
The Master was bewildered and had no reply. Huayan said, "You ask me; I shall tell you. The Master then asked, "Does emptiness also possess the six aspects?"
Wu said, "The eye is empty. At these words, the Master attained enlightenment; he leaped for joy and prostrated in gratitude. Wu asked, "How do you understand this?

The Master replied, "Empty. Wu approved of this. Later, when a great assembly of men and women entered the monastery, Wu asked the Master, "The Vinaya states that if one hears the sound of hairpins and bracelets from across a wall, it is called breaking the precepts.
Now we see gold and silver intermingled, and crimson and purple robes crowded together."
"Chen, is this breaking the precepts or not? The Master said, "A fine way in. Yuanian said, "In the future, you shall have five hundred disciples;
you will be held in high esteem by kings and lords. The Master then took his leave and stayed at an ancient temple in Quzhou, where he read the Tripitaka.
King Zhongyi summoned him to the palace, conferred upon him the Bodhisattva Precepts, and appointed him as the Abbot of Cihua Dinghui Temple.
The Chan Master established a great monastery where the sun of wisdom shone eternally; he was invited to reside there. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The Buddha-dharma is manifest before you. Why is it that you do not understand? All you venerable monks, if you wish to understand the Buddha-dharma, simply ask Zhang San or Li Si.

If you wish to understand worldly dharmas, then seek them in the groves of the ancient Buddhas. There is nothing more to do; I shall not stand long. A monk asked: "When Bodhidharma came from the West..."
"Come," [the Master said]. "What shall I transmit? The teacher replied, "I shall transmit a manual. [The Master] asked, "If that is so, then there must be dharmas outside the mind.
The teacher replied, "There are no dharmas within the mind."
Chan Master Huilang of Ba’en in Hangzhou was refined in the three studies and resolved to explore the profound essence [of the Dharma].
While he was dwelling in a hermitage at White Sand on Mount Tiantai, the senior monk Pengyan—learned and possessing a powerful memory—came to visit him to debate the fundamental tenets of the school.

The Master said, "Excessive words distance one further from the Way. Now I shall ask you a question: regarding all the sages of antiquity and the former worthies, were there any among them who did not attain awakening?
Yan replied, "As for the sages and former worthies, how could there be any who did not attain awakening?
The Master said, "When one person gives rise to the truth and returns to the source, the voids of the ten directions are entirely dissolved."
"Today Mount Tiantai stands towering and majestic; how can it be made to vanish? Yan was at a loss for what to do.
From then on, students from other schools came to study extensively, and all who arrived took his teachings to heart. Ascending the hall, he said: "Do you all understand?
Do not say that speech and silence, movement and stillness, are nothing but Buddha-work. But do not misunderstand. Tianlong Chan Master asked: "..."
"All Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra; yet I do not know from where this sutra emerges.
The Master said, "Speak! As the Deva and Dragon were about to offer a reply, the Master said, "It is already past."
Master Xingyan of Baoci Monastery in Jinling ascended the hall and said: "Whenever a traveling monk visits a spiritual teacher and arrives at a monastic community, he sets down his flask and bowl;
this may be called practicing the bodhisattva path, and his essential task is complete. Why then would he come here again?
To raise discourses on *tathatā* (suchness) and *nirvāṇa* is a teaching for the wrong time. Nevertheless, there is an ancient saying that serves as a metaphor:"
It is like sifting through sand to recognize a treasure: once the grit and pebbles are removed, the pure gold naturally appears;
it is then called the "Eternal, Abiding Sangha Jewel" complete within the world.

It is also like a rain of a single flavor falling upon a uniform ground, where all things grow, yet they differ in size and vary in taste—sweet or bitter—but one cannot say that the earth or the rain possesses names of "large" or "small. Therefore:
The Way: when square, it appears as square; when round, it appears as round. Why is this so? Because phenomena have neither partiality nor correctness; they appear in accordance with conditions.
This is called the "manifestation of the physical body in response. Do you see it yet? If you do not see it, do not sit idly by.
The Master heard the cry of a pigeon and asked a monk, "What sound is that? The monk replied, "The sound of a pigeon. The Master said, "If you wish not to incur the retribution of..."
Do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma. Ascending the hall: On this day, the worthy and sages have gathered together; the ocean-like assembly has arrived in unison.
Truly, the essence of the Buddha-Dharma is fully present here. For those with such brilliant discernment, there is no need to wait for words.
Yet, since speech itself is fundamentally non-existent, why remain silent? Therefore, the myriad phenomena of the phenomenal world and all the Buddhas—
The Great Source: when manifest, the light of the Sea-Seal is clear and serene; when obscure, the emotions are deluded and self-bewildered.
Were it not for the superior person of universal mind and the transcendent man of extraordinary rank, how could one, amidst the various sensory objects, manifest the ultimate subtlety?

How could one roll up or unfurl phenomena, grant or withhold the myriad forms, and demonstrate that birth is not birth and cessation is not cessation? Only when birth and cessation are thoroughly penetrated can one speak of the "True."
Regarding the conventional, when one speaks of the provisional, shadows disperse across a thousand paths; regarding the ultimate, when one discusses the real, the single emptiness leaves no trace.
How could one possibly calculate this in terms of existence and non-existence, or arising and ceasing?
Chan Master Chongshou Qichou ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The fourfold assembly observes the primary principle with earnest attention.

What is this primary principle? The Master said, "Why trouble yourself to ask further? He then continued, "Great assembly, if you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should observe the conditions of time and season.
What are these conditions of time and season? You, venerable ones, may disperse right now. And so he did.
"Does the Way exist or not? If it does not exist, for what reason do people disperse upon hearing of it? If it does exist, what is the primary meaning (paramārtha)?

Elder, the primary meaning is already manifest; why trouble yourself to contemplate it further? If you can realize it with such clarity, the Buddha-nature is constantly illuminating and all phenomena are eternally abiding.
Yet, if you perceive that there is a phenomenon which eternally abides, you have still not reached the true source of the Dharma."

"What is the true source of the Dharma? "Elder," have you not heard the ancients say: "When one person awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions all vanishes"?
Is there still even a single dharma for intellectual understanding? The ancients had such a great matter of cause and condition;
simply act in accordance with it, and that is it. Why trouble yourself, Elder, with so much talk? Among the assembly...
If there is something you do not yet understand, please ask for instruction. A question was asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master replied: "What is the Buddha? The questioner asked:
"How should one understand this? The Master said: "To understand it is not [the Buddha]."
Chan Master Ba’en Fa’an first resided at Caoshan. He ascended the hall and said: "To know illusion is to leave it;
no expedient means are required. To leave illusion is awakening; there is also no gradual progression. Venerable elders, how do you understand 'no expedient means'?"
Furthermore, there is no gradual progression. Where does the intent of the ancients lie? If you can understand this, the Buddhas are constantly manifest before you;
if you have not yet understood it, do not seek it within the *Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment*. Truly, the Buddha-dharma has been manifest at all times from antiquity to the present.
All you venerable seniors, at every moment, you inherit this majestic radiance; you must possess the great faculty of faith to bear this burden.
One must attain it by starting from the very beginning. One does not see the Buddha praising those who are merely fierce and sharp;

nor does he commend others for long-cultivated pure karma directed toward goodness. Rather, one must be like that broad-foreheaded, fierce butcher who, upon throwing down his cleaver, immediately realized the fruit of Arhatship.
It must be exactly like this to succeed. Therefore, the Elder said: "It is as if taking the rank of Brahmā... and so forth.
[This teaching was] bestowed upon the ordinary.
Zen Master Qingxi of Yunju was asked by a monk, "What is the realm of Yunju? The Master said, "What do you call 'the realm'?
The monk asked, "What is the person within the realm? The Master said, "What did I just tell you?"
Zhengqin Xihong addressed the assembly upon ascending the hall: "The ancient sages said that the perfection [of reality] is identical to the great void; it is neither deficient nor redundant.

They also said that each and every dharma is a distinct school, and that the many dharmas constitute a single school of principle. Furthermore, they said that when arising, it is only dharmas that arise; when ceasing, it is only dharmas that cease.
Moreover, at the time of arising, it does not say 'I am arising,' and at the time of ceasing, it does not say 'I am ceasing. Based on these teachings..."
[The Master] said: "O senior monks who have long remained in the monastic groves, if you are brothers who are beginners, you must first realize the Way.
A human body is difficult to obtain; the True Dharma is difficult to hear. Do not treat it as something ordinary. The food and clothing provided by donors are not easily digested.
If you do not clarify the Way, each of you will ultimately have to repay them. Senior monks, do you wish to understand the Way? Be careful. A monk asked: [Question]
An ancient said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are your true spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
How can one take mountains, rivers, and the great earth as spiritual friends? The Master said, "What do you call 'mountains, rivers, and the great earth'?"

Luo Han Zhiyi Chan Master ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the entire world of the ten directions, there is not so much as a single speck of dust of a dharma that can serve as an object for your seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing.
Do you believe this? Even so, you must still attain awakening; do not treat it as something trivial. Have you not heard it said:
'To clarify the self alone, yet fail to awaken to what is before one's eyes—such a person possesses only a single eye'?"
"The eye. Do you understand yet? A monk asked, "If not even a speck of dust is established, why do beauty and ugliness appear before one?
The Master said, "Take this clearly to heart and ask someone else elsewhere."
When Chan Master Zhangyidao Qin first resided at Qixian, he ascended the hall and said: "Is the Way far? It is true in every encounter.
Is the Sage far? If you embody it, you are divine. I have been showing this to you constantly; why do you not sit beneath my robe and bowl and investigate it directly right here?
What is it that you must seek by coming up here? Now that you have come up, I shall not deal with you through phenomena."
Having attained this, I shall now cite a small measure of the ancients' expedient means to shake off a bit of "tortoise hair" and "hare's horns," and deliver them to you.
All you venerable elders, if you wish for something concise and essential, you should investigate it within the Sangha hall, at the triple gate, or in your own quarters.
Is there anyone who understands? If there is, please speak of it so that I may bear witness for you, O Monks.
Question: "What is the realm of Qixian? The Master said: "What realm does Qixian have?
The Ruler of Jiangnan invited him to reside at the Changyi Monastery. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "Why have you all come here to stand?
Good friends as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are constantly your companions; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they never depart from you. It is simply this continuous bed."
Seated firmly above, the spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) of the ten directions come of their own accord to visit you, the Elder.
Why do you not believe and accept this? You have been able to create so many difficulties and ease. The ancient sages lamented seeing people of the present age at a loss;
they said, "Alas! Human sentiments have long been deluded. Facing the truth with one's own eyes, one does not perceive it. This was a lament for all of you; look back!
"I do not know. But tell me, regarding what do you say you do not know? Why do you not examine the expedient means of the ancients?

It is simply because you lack sufficient faith that you have come to this state. All you, venerable seniors, need only set your minds upon the Buddha-dharma, and there will be nothing you cannot attain.
Go and embody the Way in your daily affairs. Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Ba’en Kuangyi was invited by the Prince of Jiangnan to reside in the Upper Hall. Ascending the hall, he looked over the assembly and said:
"If you rely upon this and put it into practice, there will be no entanglements. Do you believe me? It is like the blazing, radiant clarity of the sun."
Do not engage in further deliberation; it cannot be reached through deliberation. Even if one were to reach it through deliberation, it would be called "limited wisdom.
As the former masters said: "When the person has no mind, they accord with the Way; when the Way has no mind, it accords with the person.

When the person and the Way have thus accorded, this is called being a person of no affairs. Furthermore, what makes one an ordinary person? What makes one a sage? If you have not yet realized this, it may be said:
Enveloped by deluded emotions, one departs from it yet cannot leave it; in the state of delusion, there are immediate obstructions, appearing as various opposites and dependencies.
Suddenly, when these are discarded, there is nothing to be gained. It is like the case of Yajñadatta, who mistook his reflection for a demon and thought his head had vanished;
did he not carry his own head while searching for it? Yet, at the very moment of his delusion, his head was not lost. When he finally awakens—
Departing is also not for the sake of attainment. Why is this? When people are deluded, they say there is loss; when people awaken, they say there is attainment.
Attainment and loss reside in the person; what concern do they have with movement or stillness?

He then produced a commentary with topical headings and sub-sections, interweaving the textual passages with annotations.

Once this work was completed, he went to see Fayan to present his own scholarship; it deeply accorded with the intent of the sutra. Fayan said, "Does the *Śūraṅgama* not contain the principle of the 'eight returns'? The Master replied: [He then proceeded to explain it].

"You ask me; I shall tell you. The Master asked, "What is the student’s own self? Guishan replied, "The child Bingding comes seeking fire.
At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. On the day of the opening of the hall, King Li and Fayan were both present in the assembly.
A monk asked, "The dragon roars and the mist rises; the tiger roars and the wind arises. I know this to be the realm of transcending the world."

When the matter reached this point, why did he not understand? The Master said, "Understand it well. The monk raised his head to look at the Master, and then, looking at Fayan, he withdrew and joined the assembly.
At that moment, Fayan and King Li both turned pale with alarm. Fayan returned to his quarters.

He ordered his attendant to summon the monk who had engaged him in dialogue. Yunyan said, "Elder, you were granted the title 'one with eyes' just now when you answered that question before the assembly of devas and humans.
Why did you not bow to cover it over? He struck the monk once with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*).
Three days later, the monk passed away emitting light from his mouth. [Later,] he ascended the hall and said, "All you elders possess the ever-perfect moon; each harbors..."
A treasure of true value: thus, when the moon is amidst the clouds, though it is bright, it does not shine; when wisdom is hidden within delusion, though it is true, it does not penetrate.
When there is no matter, one stands for a long time. A monk asked, "What is the Venerable Immovable? The Master said, "Flying and flying, soaring and soaring."
Chan Master Jingde Zhiyun ascended the hall and said: "The expedient means of all the sages of the past have been numerous;
in essence, they simply desire that you, honorable ones, possess a point of realization. Although you have not yet seen it, there is nevertheless not even a hair’s breadth of discrepancy."
Good sirs, you have never deviated from this by even a hair’s breadth. Why is this? It is brilliantly manifest and revealed;
you may understand it right now without expending even a fraction of effort. Do you understand the essential point?

To say that Vairocana has a teacher and the Dharma-body has a master is merely a matter of emphasizing and suppressing [the truth] for the sake of responding to specific capacities. Good sirs, what do you say to this?
One must understand this fundamental principle. If you do understand it, do not disparage the words of the Buddhas, nor overvalue the patriarchs;
you must simply attain clarity of your own eyes right here and now. Ascending the hall, he said: "Those who wish to aspire to the Way must possess the highest capacity;

otherwise, those of inferior or middling faculties will find it difficult to take up the burden even in moments of haste. Why is this? Because the Buddha-dharma is not within the realm of mind, intellect, or consciousness."
"Venerable Elder, do not treat the ground with such contempt. The ancients said that the 'eye of the śramaṇa' secures the world;
it encompasses heaven and earth, remaining continuous without leaking so much as a hair's breadth. For this reason, all Buddhas praise it, yet their praise can never suffice."
Metaphors cannot reach it. The venerable elder’s majestic radiance is brilliant and pervasive, spanning from antiquity to the present.
Fortunately, such is your family tradition; why do you not continue it? Why do you instead give rise to self-deprecation and undergo toil in vain, failing to attain awakening?
It is precisely because of this that the Buddhas appear in the world; it is precisely for this reason.
It is precisely for this reason that all Buddhas proclaim their entry into *nirvāṇa*. This is why the Patriarch came from the West specifically for this purpose.
One day, National Preceptor Hye-gu of Goryeo was invited by the King into the royal palace. Upon ascending the hall, the Master pointed to the Weifeng Pavilion and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Weifeng Pavilion has already proclaimed the Dharma for you, venerable elders. Do you understand? If you do not..."
"If you understand, how do you understand? If you say you do not understand, why do you not understand at Weifenglou?
Take care.
Master Shao Yan of the Precious Pagoda was commanded by the King of Wuyue to open the Dharma. He ascended the hall and said: "This mountain monk has always been of little knowledge."
I see that you originally intended to live in leisure and seclusion, reciting sutras while awaiting death.

Yet today, the Great King has shown such earnestness and weightiness, laboriously urging this mountain monk to emulate the venerable masters of various quarters by arranging this Dharma assembly. However, the purpose of the Great King’s invitation is solely to enable you, honorable ones, to clarify your own minds;
beyond this, there is no other principle. Have you, honorable ones, clarified your minds yet? Is it not so?
When speaking and laughing; when sitting in solemn silence; when seeking out spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*);

when discussing the Way with companions; when observing mountains and enjoying waters; and when the ears and eyes are utterly transcended—is this your mind? All such understandings as described above are entirely possessed by demons;
how can they be called "clarifying the mind"? Furthermore, there is another class of people who, apart from the delusive thoughts within the body, seek elsewhere...

To identify that which pervades the worlds of the ten directions, containing the sun and moon and encompassing the great void, as being the original true mind—this too is the calculation of the non-Buddhists;
it is not the realization of the Mind. O worthy ones, do you wish to understand? The Mind has nothing that is "is," nor is there anything that is "is not.
How could you hope to grasp or identify it through conceptual attachment?
A monk asked Chan Master Jingzun of Prajñā: “When Niutou had not yet seen the Fourth Patriarch, why did the hundred birds bring him flowers?
The Master said, “Where did you see that? The monk asked, “After he saw him, why did they no longer bring flowers? The Master said: [“... (The Master remained silent.)
"Furthermore, understand this well. The Master himself composed a true eulogy, saying: "The Truth is vast and empty; it is like a master carver from Ying applying lacquer to wood.
Mountains rise into the clouds and sky; the moon leaps into the azure depths."
Chan Master Guizong Cezhen was originally named Huichao. He went to visit Fayan and asked, "I, Huichao, inquire of the Master:
what is the Buddha? Fayan replied, "You are Huichao. From this, the Master attained awakening and entered [the Way]. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Venerable elders, seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing can only occur once. As for that which is understood, is it seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing? It is not."
Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing—do you understand? I have already explained it thoroughly for all of you, Venerable Elders. You must wait until you attain realization before it will be of use.
I have stood here for a long time; take care.
Chan Master Xiqian Yuan ascended the hall and said: "Upon leaving the Sangha Hall gate, one sees Mount Wulao. This is the lifelong study of a monk."
"The business is finished. Why have you come here again? Nevertheless, you have taken the trouble to visit this seat once more. Take care.
Zen Master Xin Xingqi was asked by a monk, "How can one escape from the three realms? The Master said, "Do you believe it yet?"
[The monk] said, "I have deep faith. I beg the Master’s compassion. The Master said, "This very mind of faith has spanned from antiquity to the present.
You must investigate it with urgency; why linger in hesitation? If you wish to transcend the three realms, know that the three realms are nothing but mind.
Because of the snow, the Master said to the assembly, "Venerable elders, do you see the snow? To see it is to have eyes; not to see it is to be without eyes. To have eyes..."

"If one realizes that the constant absence of the eye is itself cessation, then the Buddha-body is all-pervading. The monk took his leave and went to Letan, requesting the Master to show him a way of entry.
The Master said, "A fine way of entry! With a firm resolve for the Way, follow the assembly in your inquiries."
He followed the communal labors; when he wished to go, he went, and when he wished to stay, he stayed. His going and staying were for no other reason than this.
When he arrived at Letan, he did not inquire after Mazu.
Once, while the ancient worthy Jinchan Chanshi was attending Dharma Eye, Dharma Eye asked a monk, "Where have you come from since leaving this place?
The monk replied, "I have come from entering the mountain ranges. Dharma Eye said, "Not easy. The monk said, "I have traveled across all those mountains and waters for nothing.
Dharma Eye said, "Those many mountains and waters are not bad either. At these words, the monk was without speech, and the Master attained realization thereupon.
Chan Master Xingfu Kexun was asked by a monk, "Why do you say that dharmas are empty? The Master said, "They are not empty. He presented a verse to the assembly, saying:
The autumn river, misty islands, and clear skies; Gulls and egrets stand in rows. If one does not call upon Avalokiteśvara, How can one know the entry into the Universal Gate?
When Chan Master Yongming Yanshou first resided at Xuedou, he ascended the hall and said: "At this place, Xuedou, a torrential waterfall plunges for a thousand fathoms without ceasing;
wondrous cliffs rise ten thousand cubits high, leaving no place to set foot. You people of the assembly, where will you take your next step?
A monk asked, "How does one tread upon the single path of Xuedou? The Master said, "Step by step, frosty flowers form. (He spoke these words.)
He spoke of "thoroughly freezing. The Master had a verse that said: "The lone ape’s cry falls upon the moon in the central crag; The wild guest’s chant remains unfinished by the midnight lamp.
Who can grasp the meaning in this realm at this moment? Only the meditation monk sitting deep within the white clouds.
King Zhongyi invited him to open the new temple of Lingyin. The following year, he moved to the Great Seat of Yongming, where the assembly numbered over two thousand. [Verse] Monk.
The monk asked, "What is the wondrous purport of Yongming? The Master said, "Add more incense. The monk said, "Thank you for the instruction.
The Master said, "Be glad that there is no connection at all. The monk bowed; the Master said, "Listen to this verse: 'If you wish to know the purport of Yongming...'"
Before the gate is a lake. When the sun shines, light arises; when the wind comes, waves stir. A student asked, "I have been at Yongming for a long time.
Why do I not understand the house style of Yongming? The Master said, "Understand it where you do not understand.
The student asked, "How can one understand where one does not understand? The Master said, "An elephant calf is born from within a cow's womb; red dust rises from the azure sea. [Question] Asked:
"One cannot escape becoming a Buddha or a patriarch; one cannot escape the cycle of the six realms of existence. I do not yet understand from where one cannot escape.
The Master said, "One cannot escape from the very place you ask. Question: "What is the Great Perfect Mirror?"
The Master said, "A broken sand pot. The Master resided at Yongming for fifteen years, ordaining one thousand seven hundred disciples.

In the seventh year of the Kaibao era, he entered Mount Tiantai to confer the *upasampadā* precepts, with approximately ten thousand people participating. He constantly conferred the Bodhisattva precepts upon the seven classes of followers.
At night, he offered food to ghosts and spirits; in the morning, he released various living creatures in numbers beyond counting. Six times a day, he distributed alms.
He practiced the Flower Garland Way (Avatamsaka). With his remaining strength, he recited the Lotus Sūtra approximately thirteen thousand times.

He composed the *Zongjing lu* (Record of the Mirror of the Source) in one hundred fascicles, as well as poems, gāthās, and rhapsodies totaling several million words, which were disseminated beyond the seas.
Chan Master Wuyun Zhifeng was thoroughly versed in the three studies and had a complete understanding of both nature (xing) and characteristics (xiang).
He once dreamed that he ascended Mount Sumeru and beheld three Buddhas seated in a row: first Śākyamuni, then Maitreya;

he prostrated at their feet in both cases, yet he did not recognize the third honored one, merely gazing up at him. Śākyamuni Buddha said to him, "This is the one who will succeed Maitreya: Siṃhacandra."
The Master of the Buddha was about to prostrate himself when, upon waking, he read the *Tripitaka* and found it corresponded exactly with his dream.

While traveling, he arrived at Yunju on Mount Tiantai and visited National Teacher [Huizhao]. Through the karmic conditions of their master-disciple relationship, the profound mysteries were suddenly revealed.
One day, as the Master sat in meditative absorption within the Hall of Samantabhadra, a divine being suddenly knelt before him. The Master asked, "Who are you? The being replied:

[The deity] was a guardian of the precepts. The Master said, "I have a latent transgression from past lives that has not yet been extinguished; do you know of it? [The deity] replied, "What sin does the Master have?
It is merely a minor oversight. The Master asked, "What is it? [The deity] said, "Whenever you pour out water from your bowl, that too is the property of a donor."
The Master always discarded [the water from his bowl], which was inappropriate. Having finished speaking, he vanished. From that time on, the Master drank all the water used for washing his bowl;

after doing so for a long period, he consequently developed a spleen ailment, which only recovered after ten years. (In general, when discarding food, drink, saliva, mucus, or excrement, one should snap the fingers, silently recite the mantra, and discard them with a mind of giving.
The King of Wuyue, admiring the Master’s spiritual influence, summoned him and bestowed upon him purple robes, appointing him as Chan Master Pujue.
The Master was appointed to reside at Gongchen Monastery in Lin’an. Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly:
"All you venerable seniors, you abandon one teacher to seek out another teacher, following entirely the example of Sudhana’s journey to the south. Now I ask you, venerable seniors:
when Sudhana took his leave of Mañjuśrī and intended to ascend Mount Miaofeng to visit the Bhikṣu Meghashiri, why was it that when he arrived at that place, Meghashiri—"
Yet we shall meet again on another peak. The intent of the Teachings and the intent of the Patriarchs are one and the same expedient means;
ultimately, there is no separate principle. If he understands that clearly, this too will be manifest. You venerable elders are now gathered around this old monk—is this meeting or not meeting?
Is this place the Wondrous Peak or a different peak? Should you depart from here, it may be said that you have not [truly left].
"You have brought shame upon this old monk. You have also seen the Bhikṣu De-yun, yet you have never been separated from him for even a single moment.
Do you still believe this? Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "The ancients traveled for the sake of the Dharma, undaunted by toil and hardship.
Take Xuefeng, for instance, who went to Touzi three times and ascended Dongshan nine times; though he lingered and traveled back and forth, he still could not find a way in. Look at you!"
These days, as soon as students of the Way step through the gate, they demand that this old monk guide them and instruct them in Zen.
But tell me, you who wish to realize the path of the ultimate mystery—how can it be treated as something ordinary? Moreover, this matter has its own proper timing;
how can it be attained through restless seeking? Do you wish to know the moment of awakening? For now, each of you go down to the hall and sit in stillness.

"I shall explain it for you only when Mount Yangjia nods its head. At that time, a monk came forward and said, "Mount Yangjia has nodded its head; please, Master, speak. The Master said, "Tell me, does this monk understand my words, or does he not? The monk bowed. The Master said, "Today, by chance, I have failed in my discernment. "A person of non-action and non-activity—why is there nevertheless the difficulty of the golden chain? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf:

"Precisely because of non-action and non-activity. A monk asked: "The scriptures say that when Mañjuśrī suddenly gave rise to the view of Buddha and the view of Dharma, he was seized by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and cast into the two Iron Ring Mountains.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Where are the two [Iron Ring Mountains]?"
At Mount Cakravāḍa, the monk remained silent. The Master said, "Do you understand? If anyone nowadays gives rise to a view regarding the Buddha-dharma, I shall brew two cups of tea for them.
Now tell me: is this rewarding them or punishing them? Is it in accord with the intent of the teaching or not?"
Master Ba’en Yong’an was asked by a monk, “What is the meaning of the West? The Master said, “Stand over here.
As soon as the monk took a step, the Master called out, “Do you understand? The monk replied, “I do not understand. The Master said, “Listen to this verse:
‘You ask for the meaning of the West, Yet stand over here. Last night at the third watch, The rain soaked the void. [The Master added: “A flash of lightning!”
Suddenly it was bright; it was not like the hurried movement of a centipede.
Zen Master Zining Zhiquan was asked by a monk, "What is it to hold a hoe in one's empty hands? The Master said, "Simply believe with such earnestness.
The monk asked, "What is it to walk while riding a water buffalo? The Master said, "From where have you come?"
Chan Master Pumen Xibian ascended the hall and said: "I, this mountain monk, have always lacked insight and am further deficient in learning and retention.
Although I recently stood in attendance upon the National Teacher, I did not receive a single word of instruction.

Consequently, as I gather here today with you virtuous ones, there is not a single dharma by which I can assist or inspire you; how much less could I possibly distinguish between the black and the white for you?"
Discussing matters of past and present, do you still find fault with this mountain monk? If there is one who finds fault, tell me: does this person possess the eye, or not?
Does he maintain the principle of host and guest, or not? Those who are late learners and beginners must examine this most carefully.
A monk asked, "What is the manifestation of supernatural powers through the Universal Gate? The Master said, "If it were so, then you, O *kalyāṇamitra*, would have cause for resentment."
The old monk departs. A monk asked, "If one does not err, what then? The Master said, "First, go down to the hall and reflect upon it.
Guangqing asked Cuiyan An, "I beg the Master to bestow the priceless jewel. The Master said, "You are well able to reveal it.
The monk said, "In that case, every person is fully endowed with it. The Master said, "Where is the jewel? The monk— [remained silent].

[The student] prostrated. The Master said, "This too is empty talk. [The student] asked, "When the main points are grasped and the essential principles are raised, the roles of host and guest are fully established.
What is the host? The Master said, "I understand this question deeply. [The student] asked, "What is the guest? The Master said, "What did I just say to you?
[The student] asked, "When the host and guest reach accord, what then? The Master said, "His orders will not be carried out. [The Master] ascended the hall. He wished—
"Understand the purport of Caoxi: clouds fly before the mountain ahead. This is clearly and truly it; there is no need for further pursuit. A monk asked, "An ancient worthy once said:
'Red dust arises from the bottom of the well; waves surge upon the mountain peak. I do not know what the meaning of this is.
The Master said, "If you go to other places, simply ask whatever you wish. The monk asked, "What is your own intention, Reverend? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"What did I just say to you? He then said: "The tradition handed down from ancient times to the present all says:
'Dust arises from the bottom of the well; waves rise upon the mountain peak. Fruit forms on empty flowers; children are born to a stone woman. Now, how do you understand this?

Is it that you send forth affairs with harmonious sounds, manifesting the mind through objects, concealing the blade within the phrase, or being fully revealed before the sound? Or is it that there is the name but no substance?"
As for the essence: do you sing of the profound discourse in a different way? If you, Elder, understand it yourself, you will grasp the intent of the ancients.
But if that is not so, and you cannot understand it in such a manner, then how should you understand it? Elder, do you wish to understand? Simply observe where the clay ox walks:
the mirage turns into waves. When the wooden horse neighs: the empty flowers cast their shadows. Such is the principle of the holy and the ordinary.
It is perfectly clear; why need you stand here long? Take care.
A monk asked Zen Master Huidá of Huayan, “What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, “Mountains, rivers, and the great earth.”
Question: What is the realm of Avataṃsaka? The Master said: "Filling the eyes, yet without form or shadow.
Chan Master Jiǔqū Qìngxiáng [Verse]: A monk asked: "In the midst of perilous and evil paths, what serves as the bridge?
[The Master] said: "This very thing serves as the bridge. The monk asked: "What is this? The Master said: "It strikes right through your nostrils."
A monk asked Chan Master Kaohua Xingming, "What is the skillful means that flows forth from the gate of Kaohua?
The Master said, "The sound of the tide is heard twice every day."
Shuilu Meets Master Xuan’an [Verse] He received the Dharma from Tiantai. Furthermore, he frequently studied the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*.

Upon reaching the passage, "When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, this is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and vision are without seeing, this is nirvāṇa," the Master read it by breaking the phrasing as follows:
"Knowledge and vision establish—knowledge is the root of ignorance. Knowledge and vision are without—seeing, this is nirvāṇa."
At this, Anpan had an awakening. Someone said to the Master, "You have broken the phrasing. The Master replied, "This is my point of realization;
I shall not change it for the rest of my life. At that time, he was called An Lengyan.
Chan Master Longhua Huiju addressed the assembly upon opening the hall, saying: "When it comes to the ancestral vehicle of our predecessors, how can one proclaim it here?

Even as Śākyamuni Buddha taught the Dharma of his entire lifetime like pouring water from one vessel into another, the ancient worthies have already said that it is 'like the matters of a dream or the prattle of sleep. Now tell me, by what principle does one say this?"

Do you understand? The Great Gate of Giving is open; when has it ever been obstructed? It nurtures both the ordinary and the sage, without leaking even a speck of dust. To speak of the ordinary is to be entirely ordinary;
to cite the sage is to be entirely sage. Ordinary and sage do not wait for one another; each and every one is uniquely honored. Therefore it is said:
"The mountains, rivers, and the great earth constantly preach the Dharma and constantly emit light. Earth, water, fire, and wind—each and every one..."
Thus it was. At that time, a monk came forward to pay his respects. The Master said, "What an excellent question! Ask according to the Dharma.

As the monk prepared to step forward, the Master said, "Again, there is no connection. [He] ascended the hall for formal instruction. "At Longhua, here as well, we do nothing more than gather firewood and pick vegetables;
coming up and going down; a single bowl of gruel in the morning; a single meal at noon; and drinking tea after sleep. Simply this."
Investigate it thus. Take care.
Chan Master Qiyun Yuzhen was asked by a monk: "The perfectly clear awareness—why does it not arise from mental activity?
The Master said: "The perfectly clear awareness. The monk asked: "How is it different from mental activity? The Master said: "What do you call 'mental activity'?"

Sitting idly on an autumn evening, I spontaneously composed this verse: The autumn courtyard is solemn, the wind whistles through the trees; Cold stars are arrayed across the sky as the moon’s orb rises high.
Leaning my chin upon my hand, I sit in stillness, my spirit unwearied; From the bird’s nest, without cause, a tuft of cloth-hair is blown forth.
Master Shuilu Benxian ascended the hall and said: "Do you all see the Zhulin Hermitage, the mountains, the waters, the monastic quarters, and the assembly?
If you say you see them, then there are dharmas outside the mind.

If you say you do not see them, how can you deny that the Zhulin Hermitage, the mountains, the waters, the monastic quarters, and the assembly are all vividly present right here? Do you understand this instruction?"
If you meet [the truth], it will not hinder your spiritual acuity. Do not stand idly when there is nothing to do. Ascending the hall, he said:

"In general, regarding the study of the Way, it is not necessarily the case that studying 'talking about the matter' (huà) constitutes studying the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying 'discerning the matter' constitutes studying the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying 'substituting words' constitutes studying the Way;

it is not necessarily the case that studying 'alternative words' constitutes studying the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying how to 'pierce through' the extraordinary statements found within the sutras and treatises constitutes studying the Way."
To engage in study through mere words is not necessarily the study of the patriarchs’ extraordinary speech.

If you engage in such study, no matter how thoroughly you may master it—reaching the seventh or eighth level—if you still lack any insight into the Buddha-dharma, you are called a person of "dry wisdom.
Have you not heard the ancient masters say: "Cleverness cannot withstand birth and death; how can dry wisdom escape it?"
The Wheel of Suffering: If you people would study, you must study with true sincerity before you can succeed.
When walking, take it up while walking; when standing, take it up while standing; when sitting, take it up while sitting; when sleeping, take it up while sleeping.
"When speaking, speak; when silent, take up [the inquiry] during silence. During all activities, take up [the inquiry] during all activities.
Since you are taking it up during such times as these, tell me: what person are you taking up? What words are you taking up?
At this point, you must have a place of personal clarity before you can succeed. If it is not like this, it is called...
Those of a fickle and superficial disposition lack the principle of ultimate realization. [Ascending the hall: In the secluded forest, birds cry out; in the azure ravine, fish leap.
Cloud fragments unfurl, and the sound of the waterfall is plaintive. Do you recognize such manifold scenes? Shall I show you a point of entry?
If you can recognize it, you may proceed with your practice without hindrance. [Ascending the hall: You all—
O people, when you sleep soundly at night, you are unaware of anything. Since you are unaware of anything, let me ask you this:
at that time, does the original nature exist, or does it not exist? If you say that the original nature exists at that time, yet you are unaware of anything, you are no different from being dead.
If you say that the original nature does not exist at that time, then upon suddenly awakening from sleep, you will realize it.
It is as before. Do you understand? Not knowing anything at all is no different from death; when one suddenly awakens from sleep, awareness is as it was before. At such times as these, what is this?
If you do not understand, each of you must investigate it for yourselves. Do not stand idly by when there is nothing to do. Ascending the hall, he said:
"The arising of all phenomena is manifested only by the mind. Such words are an excellent point of entry."
"Regarding these gateways, let me ask you all: when the eyes see all forms, the ears hear all sounds,
the nose smells all fragrances, the tongue discerns all tastes, the body touches all that is soft and smooth, and the mind discriminates all phenomena—
just as it is with these objects confronted by the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, are they merely your own minds?"
Is it, moreover, not your own mind? If you say it is solely your own mind, why does it not merge entirely with your bodies into a single mass and come to an end?
Why, then, do the objects encountered by you remain outside your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind?
If you say that the objects encountered by the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind are not [your own mind]...
"Focus your minds. Furthermore, how can you deny that all phenomena arise from the mind and are manifested by the mind?
These words remain in the world; who does not recite them? When you see these words, do you understand them? If you do not, let us all apply our minds together to deliberate and master them.
May you find joy within this, and do not grow weary of study. For now, there is nothing more to be done, so please withdraw."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "In the teachings of Tiantai, there are explained three gates: those of Mañjuśrī, Avalokiteśvara, and Samantabhadra.
The gate of Mañjuśrī refers to all forms; the gate of Avalokiteśvara refers to all sounds; the gate of Samantabhadra refers to arriving without moving a step.
My teaching, however, holds that the gate of Mañjuśrī is not all forms, the gate of Avalokiteśvara is not all sounds, and the gate of Samantabhadra..."
"What is this 'Gate of the Sages'? Do not say you have set aside the teachings of Tiantai;
there is nothing to do, so withdraw for now. [Ascending the hall, he gave this discourse: He cited a monk who asked Changsha, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing?

Changsha said, "He became a donkey at the eastern neighbor's house and a horse at the western neighbor's house. The monk said, "I do not understand. Changsha said, "If you want to ride him, then ride him. If you...
"Down, down! The Master said, "If one is a person practicing to seek liberation from the three realms, hearing these words will inevitably cause doubt and inevitably cause alarm.
Where has Nanquan gone after his passing? He has become a donkey for the eastern neighbor."
The western neighbor acts as a horse. Some understand this by saying: "A thousand transformations and ten thousand changes do not go beyond the true and constant. Others understand it by saying:
"One must understand 'acting among those of different species' before one can truly grasp these words. Still others understand it by saying:
"The eastern neighbor is Nanquan; the western neighbor is Nanquan. Yet others understand it by saying: "The master of the eastern house; the master of the western house."
Disciple: Some have said, "What is the eastern neighbor? What is the western neighbor?
Others have said, "Then he brays like a donkey and neighs like a horse. Still others have said, "What do you call the eastern neighbor’s donkey?
What do you call the western neighbor’s horse? Yet others have said, "Since you ask about passing away, the answer lies within the question itself. Some have also said...

[The Master] said: "He has gone to where the pillar stands exposed. Some have interpreted this by saying: "He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor; what harm did this do to Nanquan?
Such interpretations by various masters all find a place of peace within the Buddha-dharma. But where did Nanquan go when he passed away?
He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor. I, this student, do not understand; I wish to ride him.
He immediately mounts; he dismounts whenever he wishes to dismount. This matter does not require many principles to understand.

If you see the nature of the Dharma-realm, there is nothing more to it. Take care. [The Master] ascends the hall and says: "The form and shadow in a mirror depend solely upon the light of the mirror for their manifestation.
You people here—tell me, upon what do all the things you do depend for their manifestation?"
Do you understand yet? If you do understand, you will find yourself fully satisfied in your study of the Way; there is nothing more to do, so do not stand idly by.

When Chan Master Xingjiao Hongshou was working together with National Teacher Huizhong, he attained realization upon hearing a piece of firewood fall and composed a verse, saying: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
What falls is not another thing; whether horizontal or vertical, it is not dust. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—these fully reveal the body of the Dharma King.
Chan Master Daoyuan of Yong’an in Suzhou was asked by a monk, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Shoo! You outcaste! The monk said, “I am a beginner;
I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, “What are you asking? The monk said, “I am asking about the Buddha. The Master said—
He said, "Tut! This candāla" (from the *Jingde Chuandeng Lu*).
Master Yunju Daoqi traveled extensively through various Chan assemblies, yet his desire for learning did not cease. [Verse] Later, at Shanglan Monastery...
The Abbot of the Sūtra Repository was once asked by Fadingeng: "If someone asks me the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, I answer them, 'Neither east nor west.
How do you understand this, Master? The Master replied, "Neither east nor west. Fadingeng said, "Even if you understand it in that way, how can you be right?
The Master said, "Daoqi simply understands it as such. I wonder, however, what your own honorable intention is, Reverend Sir? Fadingeng... [replied].
[The Master] said, "That family already has its own descendants. Thereupon, the Master suddenly understood the essential meaning.

He offered this verse: "Receiving beings and benefiting life—how exquisite! An outsider is ultimately unworthy. That family already has its own descendants; When brought forth, they will serve perfectly.
(From the *Gonggu* [Verses on Ancient Cases], Chapter on Qingliang Taiqin Fadeng.)
Chan Master Yuanzhao of Luohan Monastery in Xiuzhou ascended the hall. "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth are true spiritual friends," he said.
"They constantly preach the Dharma and perpetually deliver sentient beings. It does not hinder you, venerable monks; you should investigate this for yourselves.

A monk asked, "What is the家风 (monastic style) of Luohan? I request a single phrase from the Master. The Master replied, "The grain ears of Jiahe grow together; the fragrance is transmitted to the Central Kingdom. The monk said, "This is still merely 'Jia' (excellent)."
The House Style of the He Family. What is the house style of the Arhats? The Master said: "If you travel to various regions, explain it clearly to others.
Zen Master Zhitian Bianlong addressed the assembly, saying: "The majestic true reality (dharmatā) fills the void; it is the adamantine essence."

There is no destruction. Does the great assembly see it or not? If you say they see it, yet the essence of the true mark (dharmatā) fundamentally lacks blue, yellow, red, white, long, short, square, or round; nor is it a phenomenon that can be seen, heard, sensed, or known.
So, how do you establish the principle of "seeing"? If you say they do not see it, yet it is further said that the majestic true mark fills the void.
"Empty. "Why do you not see it? A monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "That which is beneath your feet.
The monk said, "In that case, I am constantly treading upon it. The Master said, "Do not mistake it."
A monk asked Chan Master Chêng-tsì of Hsi-hsien: "When the Seer Vimala took Sudhana by the hand, he saw as many Buddhas as there are motes of dust.
But when he had not yet taken his hand, what did he see? The Master said: "What do you see now?
(Lian-shu composed a verse on this).

Chan Master Qian Guanghuan of Xiangzhou Province had thoroughly studied the Vinaya texts and listened to the *Wenju* (Textual Explanations) of Tiantai. He settled his mind in the Perfect and Sudden *Zhi Guan* (Calming and Contemplation).

Later, while reading the *Śūraṃgama-sūtra*, he found its literary style and principles so vast and profound that he could not yet penetrate their full meaning. One night, after having recited the sutra for a long time, he fell asleep.
He leaned over his desk and dozed off. In his dream, he saw the solar disc descending from the sky; he opened his mouth and swallowed it.

From that moment on, he suddenly attained awakening. The various categories of meaning became clear and flowed without obstruction. Later, he visited Yongming, who merely confirmed his prior understanding and offered no further instructions or metaphors.
Chan Master Chongfu Qingxiang ascended the hall and said: "Virtuous Chan practitioners, the nature of seeing is all-pervasive; the nature of hearing is likewise so.
It penetrates the ten directions, being neither internal nor external. Therefore, the ancients said: 'Following conditions without fabrication, movement and stillness are eternally true.'"
Such is this practice, which fully embodies the function of true wisdom.
Master Yunju Yene ascended the hall and said: "There is no need to come up here.
In the hall, the Elder Kauṇḍinya shall turn the Dharma-wheel of the primary meaning for all you elders. Can you do it? If you can believe it, each of you return to your quarters."
"Take this up for contemplation. After descending from his seat, he asked a monk, "Just as I have just instructed you, 'Take up the contemplation of the Holy Monk,' what did the Holy Monk say?
The monk replied, "I am especially grateful to the Master for raising this again.
[Another] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "This very mind is the Buddha. [The monk] said, "I do not understand; I beg the Master for an expedient means. The Master said:
Conveniently, they call this "Buddha. Turn the light back upon yourself and reflect: what are body and mind?
Master Guizong Huicheng was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "I do not know. He then added, "Stop your questioning for a moment.
Even if you were to question until the end of kalpas, the question would not apply; even if one were to answer until the end of kalpas, [the answer would not reach it]."
Answer: It does not reach it. Why? Because each person has their own fundamental matter, which is perfect throughout the ten directions and spans from antiquity to the present.
Even the Buddhas dare not err regarding this matter for people; thus, it is called the "Summit Lineage" (Dingzu).

This is merely to assist the Venerable Fashang. Therefore he said: "All sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm realize the fruit of the Sugata in every thought-moment.
Since they are great men, so am I; how can I disparage myself and succumb to despondency? O Venerable Ones!
Do not be discouraged; believe and accept this, and rest here. When the Patriarch came from the West, he spoke only of seeing one's nature to achieve Buddhahood.
All other teachings do not equal this teaching.
A monk asked Zen Master Uisang of Sŏgyeong-san, "Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha; Vimalakīrti remained silent in Vaiśālī. I wonder how you would instruct the assembly?
The Master said, "You do not wish for me to speak. The monk said, "I do not understand your intent.
The Master said, "Withdraw for now. Question: "What is the true person of no station? The Master said, "There is no place here to set him down."
[The Master] set him aside.
When Chan Master Xuanben of Lingyin saw a monk reading a sutra, he asked, "What sutra are you reading? The monk was speechless.
Thereupon, [the Master] presented this verse: Reading the sutra, yet not knowing the sutra, In vain you labor to damage your eyes. If you wish not to damage your eyes, Be clearly discerning.
Record of the *Jing*:
Zen Master Haoyuan Xian of Yao Peak was asked by a monk, "The teachings state that 'this Dharma is equal, with no high or low.
What is this equal Dharma? The Master said, "Yao Peak is high; Baofeng is low. The monk said, "If so, does it not become high?"
[The Master] went down [from the seat]. The Master said, "I knew you would understand it in this way. Upon hearing the sound of thunder, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Do you hear the sound of thunder? Do you know its place of origin? If you know its place of origin, you will know where body and life fall.
If you do not even know this, then as the ancients said: 'Those who do not know heaven and earth yet insist there is a Qian and Kun—better that they eat.'"
"Tea, go. A monk asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
He then remarked, "As for that monk who finally asked, 'When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?'—I told him, 'Heaven!
Heaven! Now tell me, where does the meaning of this lie? Is it in grief?"
Do you still painfully remember the Way-man who has passed away? If you discuss it in such a manner, you truly have no knowledge of where he has gone.
Do you wish to know where he has gone? There is no need to stand for long; simply rest. Ascending the hall:
Winter passes and spring arrives; the gates of the pavilion open. If you can enter, there is no need to linger. Monks, can you enter here?
It is not yet like being able to enter. Therefore, the ancients said: "Every place is Maitreya; there is no gate and no Sudhana.
If you have not yet been able to enter, you are merely wandering aimlessly, O venerable elders. I shall say no more; take care and do not stand for long. Respectfully.
Chan Master Shengshou ascended the hall and said: "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, what further matter is there?
Therefore it is said: the mountains and rivers of antiquity and today; the sun and moon of antiquity and today; human relations of antiquity and today;

the cities and towers of antiquity and today—these are called the Dharma-gate of Equality, which is devoid of past and future limits. Do you all believe this? If you can believe it, then rely upon it and put it into practice."
I have stood for a long time; take care.
Zen Master Xingjiao Weiyi was asked by a monk: "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said: "Several layers of white clouds. The monk asked:
"How was it after he appeared in the world? The Master said: "A single peak of green mountain."
Chan Master Xi Yu Tiyou ascended the hall and said: "One person holds a torch, burning his own body; another person embraces ice, lying lifeless across the road.
To advance is to encounter obstructions at every turn; to retreat is to have one's breath choked and fill the chest.
Truly, there is no way to ascend to heaven and no door to enter the earth. Even now, it is beyond remedy. After a long silence, he said: "Wait until..."
The snow has melted away; naturally, spring has arrived.

Dingshan Weisu, the abbot of the mountain, asked about the Heart-Seal of Bodhidharma. The Master had already understood it; he was now tested to see if he could demonstrate his house style before the assembly.
The Master said: "Before the gate stands a tall pine tree; at midnight, the cuckoo comes and cries upon it. [Question]
"What is the realm of Mount Ding? The Master said, "A pure breeze fills the courtyard. [The monk] asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, how do you receive them?
The Master said, "Do not disdain its simplicity and coolness. He then remarked, "As for discussing one's family style and the realm, it is not easy to respond to.
I have often seen people point to specific locations, which fails to allow others to attain freedom. Once, a monk asked Daguī: 'What is...'"
Regarding the "house style" of our Master, Suí said, "Painting a winnowing fan with red earth," and he also said, "There is no placard pasted upon his belly. Now, let me ask you all:
how do you understand this? Furthermore, Jia Shan, Yun Men, Lin Ji, and Feng Xue all had this same saying.
Spread throughout all directions, each established in different ways. Furthermore, how do you understand this? The Dharma has no divergent tracks;

though the paths differ, they lead to the same destination. If you wish to exert little effort and achieve easy understanding, simply recognize your own native roots, and you will be able to inherit the family legacy.
Everywhere you are liberated, and its application manifests before you. Heaven and earth share the same root; the myriad things are one body. This is called...
The eyes of a patch-robed monk (nanseng) are continuous and do not leak even a hair’s breadth. If one is not clear regarding this, one will merely wander about in vain hardship.
Master Zheng of Jingtu once asked: "You are titled 'Chan Master,' yet you do not speak of Chan; why is that?"
The Master said: "It is a waste of words; I am weary of them. Why resort to such convoluted turns? Let the myriad phenomena simply perform the exposition for you day and night.
While speech has its limits, this Dharma is inexhaustible—what is called the 'Inexhaustible Treasury of Creation'."
Chan Master Yan Shan of Lingyin ascended the hall and said: "I offer you, the assembly, a single thread of the Way.
But how do you discuss the Buddha-dharma? If it were as impenetrable as water-tight sealing, there would be no place for you, venerable ones, to establish yourselves or find your livelihood.
At such a time, even if the Patriarchs and Buddhas were to appear, they would each receive twenty blows from me. Having spoken thus, does this mountain monk still have [anything left]?"

"It was a mistake; it did not happen. [The Master said: "I have never seen the World-Honored One, upon being born, walk seven steps, gaze in the four directions, point one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, and declare:
'Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am the Honored One. Yunmen said:
'If I had seen him at that moment, I would have struck him with a single blow of my staff and fed him to a dog. Why is this so? It is because he sought to be the most honored under heaven."
"Ordinary. Now tell me: when Yunmen speaks in this manner, does he possess the principles of the Buddha-dharma or not?
Even so, Yunmen possesses only one eye. I have stood here for a long time; take care. (The end of Volume Ten of the *Canyuan*).
*Zhengmai of the Chan School*, Volume Five.

Phonetic Explanations: *Qǐngkài* (qīng, upper tone; kǎi, lower tone): To cough. *Sùì*: Grain spikelets. *Guǐ*: A dial on a sundial. *Niè* (pronounced *shì*): To bite. *Cù*: An arrowhead. *Shān*: To mow.

*Chēng* (pronounced *chēng*, as in *yóuchēng*): To scout; also, to inquire. *Lú*: A type of dog (*Hánxū*). *Hù*: A gourd. *Bó*: A large sea-going vessel. *Zhèn*: A sound of loud laughter. *Mòu*: The name of a place.
