All things are unified and merged; good and evil are both forgotten. Sitting and cutting off the heads of the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas, one severs the paths of the holy and the ordinary.
Only upon reaching this point does one have a slight degree of resonance. Even if it were so, from the perspective of a patch-robed monk, it would not be considered extraordinary.
Why is this? As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost. *Tu!* (A shout)
Chan Master Qingshan Long ascended the hall and said: "Flowers cluster thickly; brocade clusters thickly. For years, every necessity has been fully provided—salt and sauce.
We have preserved Nanquan’s broken cauldron and entrusted it to a novice to cook the morning gruel.
The morning gruel is at your disposal for all to eat, but as for the phrase 'washing the alms bowl'—how do you understand it? How many people remain in doubt?"
Chan Master Jingyin Tan’an Jicheng ascended the hall and said: “Vast and boundless, all are but people seeking the Buddha; throughout the world, it is difficult to find a true man of the Way.
When staff and shouts are hurled back and forth, they become medicinal taboos; yet even when these taboos are forgotten, one has not yet attained the True Heaven.

[He] ascended the hall and said: “In the nose there is sound, and in the ear there is fragrance; in the eye there is salty and bland, and on the tongue there is black and yellow. The mind can perceive touch, and the body [perceives]...”
Discrimination. An ice chamber is like spring; even in the ninth month of summer it is cool.

If you can see it thus, only then will you know that one enters meditative concentration within a male body and emerges from concentration within a female body. The sunflower turns following the sun; the rhinoceros-patterned horn reflects the moon.
Fragrant maples transform into old men; caterpillars become gall wasps. If you do not know this, how bitter it is, O Buddha! I grant you [this].

Possessing the single eye. ○ The Master, together with Yuanwu, Fazhen, Cishou, and ten great Dharma masters—along with a thousand monks from both the Chan and Lecture schools—attended a vegetarian feast at the residence of Grand Marshal Chen Gong Liangbi.
At that time, Emperor Huizong went there in private to observe the proceedings.
The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Lu, was also present among them. There was a master of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra who was a "tiger of meaning" within the Xianshou school.
Addressing the assembly, he questioned the Chan practitioners, saying: "Our Buddha established his teachings ranging from the Small Vehicle up to the Perfect and Sudden.
He swept away both emptiness and existence to realize alone the true and eternal; only after being adorned with the myriad virtues can one be called a Buddha. I have heard that the Chan school..."
"A single shout can transform the ordinary into the holy; this seems to contradict various sutras and treatises.
Now, if a single shout can enter the five teachings of our school, it is a correct teaching; if it cannot so enter, it is a false teaching. The various Chan masters looked toward their teacher.
The teacher said, "As for what the Dharma Master has asked, it is not sufficient to be answered by the three great Chan masters. Jingyin [is small...]"
"Venerable One, you may cause the Dharma Master to be free from delusion. The Master summoned Shan, and Shan responded with an assent. The Master said:

"What the Dharma Master calls the 'Teaching of the Lesser Vehicle of Ignorant Dharmas' possesses the meaning of existence (*asti*). The 'Initial Teaching of the Mahāyāna' possesses the meaning of emptiness (*śūnyatā*).
The 'Final Teaching of the Mahāyāna' possesses the meaning of neither existence nor emptiness. The 'Sudden Teaching of the Mahāyāna' possesses the meaning of..."

"Existence" is precisely the meaning of emptiness. The Perfect Teaching of the One Vehicle is the principle that there is existence without being existent, and emptiness without being empty (alternatively:

"empty yet not non-existent, existent yet not non-empty"). For example, my single shout is able to penetrate not only the five teachings, but even reaches into the arts and crafts, as well as all the various schools of thought and the hundred masters.
The Master let out a thunderous shout and asked Shan: "Did you hear it?"
[Zhaozhou] asked, "Did you hear it? He replied, "I heard it. The Master said, "Since you heard it, this one shout is 'existence'; it can lead one into the Hinayana teachings.

A short while later, he asked Shan again, "Did you hear it? He replied, "I did not hear it. The Master said, "Since you did not hear it, that previous shout was 'non-existence'; it can lead one into the Initial Teaching (Shijiao).
Then, turning to Shan, the Master said, "When I first gave the shout, you said there was sound; yet after the shout had long since ceased, the sound..."
"Extinguished. You further say 'non-existent. If you say it is non-existent, then originally it was truly existent; if you say it is existent, then now it is truly non-existent.
Neither existent nor non-existent, one can enter the Final Teaching (Zhongjiao). When I utter a single shout, existence is not existence, for existence exists because of non-existence.
When there is no shout, non-existence is not non-existence, for non-existence exists because of non-existence. Being both existent and non-existent, one can enter [the Perfect Teaching]."
Regarding the Sudden Teaching: You must understand that this single shout of mine does not function as a mere shout.

It transcends existence and non-existence; intellectual understanding and conceptualization are both forgotten. When the Way is present, not even a speck of dust can stand; when the Way is absent, it pervades the void horizontally.
This very single shout enters into hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts, and hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts enter into this single shout. Therefore, it is able to penetrate all.
In the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao), Shan rose and bowed twice again. The Master spoke to him once more, saying: "It is not only the case with a single shout;

it extends even to a single word or a single silence, a single movement or a single stillness. From antiquity to the present, throughout the ten directions of empty space, the myriad phenomena of the forest-like universe, the six realms and four modes of birth, the Buddhas of the three periods, all the sages and worthies, the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates, and the hundreds of thousands of [samādhis]..."
It is the realization of immeasurable, wondrous meanings that accord with principle and respond to capacity, being one body with heaven, earth, and the myriad things—this is called the *dharmakāya*.
That the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only, and that the four seasons and eight nodes of time are of one essence with the Yin and Yang—this is called *dharmatā*.
Therefore, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* states: "The Dharma-nature pervades all places—whether with form or without form, whether a single sound or a single color.
It is entirely contained within a single speck of dust, encompassing four meanings. Phenomena and principle are boundless, pervasive without exception;
they interpenetrate without being confused, and are blended yet not one. All these are fully present within this single shout; it is thus the gateway for establishing transformation."
"Teaching through spontaneous expedients is called a 'minor resting place. One has not yet reached the Treasure Place;

one simply does not realize that within our ancestral lineage, mind is transmitted to mind and Dharma is sealed by Dharma. Without relying on words and letters, one realizes Buddhahood by seeing one's nature.
There is a path that transcends all, which not even a thousand sages have transmitted—the upward path. Shan asked again, "What is this upward path? The Master said:
The Master said, "You should go down and understand it for yourself. Wenshan asked, "What is the treasure place? The Master replied, "It is not within your realm.
Wenshan said, "I hope the Master will show me compassion. The Master said, "Let the vast ocean change as it may; I shall never explain it for you. Wenshan was left speechless and withdrew.
All who heard this marveled at and revered him. The Emperor turned to his attendants and said, "The Zen school is indeed profound and wondrous."
The depth is such as this; even the discernment of a pure cause is rare indeed. A court official reported, "This is but the residual dregs of the Master.
Chan Master Zhe of Kaifu ascended the hall and said: "I, the mountain monk, have three seals; there is nothing added, subtracted, or left out. Facing one another..."
Presented for inspection. It can transform the ordinary into the sacred; do you all know it yet? If you do not yet know, I cannot help but annotate it layer by layer.
One seal stamps the sky: the sun, moon, and stars fall beneath its breeze. One seal stamps the mud: head and tail, thing and object, all manifest the true mechanism.
One seal stamps the water: the fish’s head is twisted around to become the dragon’s tail. The three seals are clearly manifest in their essence.
The same. At first glance, it appears neither crimson nor red; shifting between high and low, it remains unrevealed. The green mountains remain as they were amidst the white clouds.
Master Hongfu Sheng ascended the hall and said: "All of you, coming up here like this, fall into seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. Thus...
From now on, you will fall into the realm of movement, stillness, and worldly activity. If you neither go nor come, this is precisely the livelihood of a ghost cave.
How can you utter a phrase that allows for liberation? If you can speak it, I shall entrust you with this staff;
if you cannot, follow it accordingly. (He strikes the ground with the staff and descends from the seat.)
One day, a monk came to pay his respects to Chan Master Wanshou Su. The Master asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "You ought to know where I have come from, Reverend. The Master said, "A man carrying dung from Hunan; a guest harvesting grain in Jiangxi.

The monk said, "Reverend, you truly possess the divine eye. [The monk continued,] "I served as the garden head at Daguang Temple and as the library director at Donglin. The Master struck him three times.
“Strike! he roared.
Zen Master Yuan of Xiangshan ascended the hall and said: “In the wine shops and fish markets, every place is a treasure trove;
where crows cry and magpies chirp, every sound is a wondrous melody. He struck his staff and said: “Tell me, what kind of Buddha-work is this? The mess is no small matter!”
When Jǐngchún of Bǎofēng was serving as the Librarian (Zhìzàng) and attended upon Lètán, he entered the room for instruction. Lètán asked, "How much does the iron ox of Shǎnfǔ weigh?
The Master stepped forward with his hands joined and said, "But tell me, how much does it weigh? Lètán replied, "Its tail is north of the Yellow River."
With his head resting on the Yellow River, Śrīgupta has no nostrils; he continues as before to travel south in search of instruction.

As the Master hesitated, the Master of the Pond struck him. Suddenly, [the monk] attained sudden, thorough penetration. Having served as an attendant for many years, he eventually retired to live in seclusion among the forests and ravines.

He once composed a verse, saying: "Afraid of the cold, I am too lazy to shave my tangled hair; Loving the warmth, I frequently add more firewood to the hearth. My tattered *kāṣāya* robe is worn in disarray; Who could..."
Exerting great effort to arrange it.
Dharma Master Fazhen of Lushan ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to clarify that which transcends [the ordinary], you must possess the eye atop the head.

If you possess the eye atop the head, only then will you accord with the mind of one who has left the home-life. Once you have accorded with the mind of one who has left the home-life, you will constantly possess the eye atop the head. You must understand this."
Is it the eye at the crown of the head? People in the four capitals wear their clothes and eat their meals; people in the two Zhe provinces are as naturally content with warmth and nourishment.
At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, the fragrant breeze is pure; three or four peach trees in full bloom stand there.
Chan Master Yezhu Daocuan ascended the hall and said: He cited the case where one day Xuefeng ascended the seat, held up his staff, looked toward the east and said, "The one on the eastern side.
Then he looked toward the west and said, "The one on the western side. "Do you all understand? He threw down the staff and said, "Realize it right here!
The Master said: "Having looked to the east, he then gazed to the west; the staff speaks again and again."
In the cold of winter, a branch of blossoms falls away amidst the rain; there is no need for the young gentleman to lean against the balustrade.

Phonetic Explanations: *Zhù* (side-six-cut): to pound; to prick. *Lěi*: *lì kuò* cut. *Tī*: sound *zhí*. *Mào*: sound *chào*. *Shā*: *suǒ yà* cut: broken voice. *Tì*: *tā lì* cut: to leap or jump. *Cǎn*: *zǐ dàn* cut:
pouring soup over rice. *Sōu*: *sè qiú* cut: spoiled rice. *Huǎn hé*: upper character *huǎn* (shǎng huǒ wán cut): wild pig; lower character *hé* (mò gé cut): a type of wild beast.
Yī (yú yí qiè): A wave. Zhì (chǒu jué qiè): A comb. Miǎn (mí shàn qiè): A spring of water. Jí (jū dí qiè): Unfired brick. Jí (yú jí qiè): The lofty appearance of a mountain peak. Cài (qiě dài qiè):
A headband with a fringe. Huī (gǔ hú qiè): To bind objects with bamboo strips. Dàn (zè jiā qiè): To assist. Zhèn (zhī hèn qiè):
To thrust one’s right hand into another’s breast. Cuò (chū jué qiè): To point with the finger.
The Seventh Volume of the True Lineage of the Chan School:
Master Dongshan Liangjie of the Qingyuan Caodong School.
In his youth, while following his teacher, he recited the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya Sūtra*. When he reached the passage: "Without eyes, ears, nose..."
Regarding the sense bases of tongue, body, and mind, he suddenly touched his face with his hand and asked his teacher, "I possess eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and so forth;
why does the sutra say they do not exist? His teacher was startled and marveled at him, saying, "I am not your teacher.

He then pointed him toward Mount Wuxie to pay respects to Chan Master Mo and receive the tonsure. At the age of twenty-two, he went to Mount Song to receive full ordination. [Verse] First, he visited...

Nanquan was observing a vegetarian feast on the anniversary of Mazu’s death. Nanquan asked the assembly, "Tomorrow we shall offer a feast for Mazu; I wonder whether Mazu will come or not? The assembly remained silent. The Master (Xuefeng) stepped forward and replied, "He will come when he has a companion. Nanquan said, "Although this lad is a latecomer, he is quite capable of being refined. The Master said, "Master, do not suppress the noble by treating them as base. Next, he visited Guishan. He asked, "Recently I heard the story of National Teacher Zhong of Nanyang regarding 'insentient beings preaching the Dharma,' yet I have not yet fathomed its subtlety.
Guishan said, "Does the Acharya remember it? The Master replied, "I remember it.
Guishan said, "Try reciting it once for me. The Master then recounted: A monk asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? The National Teacher replied, "A wall."
“The walls and tiles,” [the Master] replied. The monk asked, “Are not walls and tiles insentient? The National Teacher said, “Yes.
The monk asked, “Do they still know how to preach the Dharma? The National Teacher said, “They preach constantly; they preach fervently, without interruption. The monk asked, “Why do I not hear it?
The National Teacher said, “It is you yourself who do not hear; it cannot be that they hinder others from hearing.”
The monk asked, "I do not yet understand who it is that can hear [this]. The National Teacher said, "All the sages can hear it.

The monk asked, "Does the Master also hear it? The National Teacher said, "I do not hear it. The monk said, "If the Master does not hear it, how do you know that insentient things are able to preach the Dharma?
The National Teacher said, "It is precisely because I do not hear it. If I were to hear it, I would be equal to the sages, and you would—"
“I do not hear me preaching the Dharma. The monk said, “If that is so, then sentient beings have no share in it. The National Teacher said, “I preach for the sake of sentient beings;
I do not preach for the sake of the various sages. The monk said, “After sentient beings have heard it, what then? The National Teacher said, “They are no longer sentient beings.
The monk said, “As for ‘insentient things preaching the Dharma,’ on what scriptural authority is this based? The National Teacher said, “It is indeed so.”
"Speech that does not accord with the scriptures is not the talk of a gentleman. Have you not seen what the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* says?

'The lands speak, sentient beings speak; all things of the three periods of time speak. After the Master had finished quoting, Muzhou said, "I have this too here, but it is simply rare to meet someone who can perceive it.
The Master said, "I do not yet understand. I beg the Master for instruction. Muzhou held up his whisk and said, "..."
"Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. He requested, "Please, Reverend, explain it to me. Muzhou said, "The mouth born of one's parents shall never be used to speak for a son.
The Master asked, "Are there others who, at the same time as you, aspire to the Way? Muzhou said, "From here, going to You County in Liling, there are stone chambers connected together.
There is a man of the Way named Yunyan. If you can brush aside the weeds and gaze upon the wind, he will surely [guide] you."
[This was] what he held in high regard. The Master asked, "I do not yet know how this man is. Guishan said, "He once asked me, 'When a student wishes to go serve his teacher, what should he do?
I replied to him, 'You must completely cut off all leakage before you will succeed.
He then asked, 'Does this not still fail to accord with the teacher's intent? I told him, 'Above all, you must never say that I am the teacher.'"
At this point, the Master took his leave of Guishan and went directly to Yunyan. Having related the preceding circumstances, he asked, "Who can hear the Dharma preached by the insentient?
Yunyan said, "The insentient can hear it. The Master asked, "Does the Master [Yunyan] hear it as well?
Yunyan said, "If I were to hear it, you would not be hearing my preaching of the Dharma. The Master asked, "Why is it that I do not [hear it]?"
Wen heard this. Yanguan held up his whisk and said, "Do you hear it yet? The Master replied, "I do not hear it.

Yanguan said, "If you cannot even hear me preaching the Dharma, how much less can you hear the insentient preaching the Dharma? The Master asked, "As for the insentient preaching the Dharma, what scriptures or teachings encompass it?"
Yan said, "Have you not seen it stated in the *Amitābha Sūtra* that the waterfowl and the forest trees all recite the Buddha’s name and recite the Dharma?
At these words, the Master attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "How wondrous! How wondrous! The insentient preaching the Dharma is inconceivable.
If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to understand; Only when hearing through the faculty of sight does one come to know. The Master then asked Yunyan:
"Venerable One, I have residual habits that are not yet exhausted. Yunyan said, "What have you been doing? The Master replied, "I do not even practice the Noble Truths.
Yunyan asked, "Have you attained joy yet? The Master replied, "Joy is not absent; it is like picking up a single bright pearl from atop a heap of refuse.
[Verse] The Master took his leave of Yunyan. Yunyan said, "After this parting, it will be difficult to meet again."
They met. The Master said, "It is difficult to find those who do not meet. [Verse] As the Master was about to depart, he asked again:

"After a hundred years, if someone should ask, 'Can you still capture the true likeness of the Master? how would you respond? Yanguan remained silent for a long while and then said, "This very one is it. The Master hesitated.
Yanguan said, "Dharma-heir Jia, in undertaking this matter, you must be extremely careful and discerning. The Master still harbored doubts. [Verse]
The Master, while crossing a stream, beheld his reflection and attained great enlightenment regarding the previous teaching. He spoke a verse, saying: "Be most careful not to seek it from another;
To do so would distance you far from me. I shall now go forth alone, And everywhere I shall encounter him. He is now precisely me, Yet I am not he.
One must understand it in this way Before one can realize Suchness. [Verse] The Master, because of making offerings to Yunyan...
Zhencian. A monk asked, "The former master said, 'It is just this. Is it not so? The Master said, "It is. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "At that time, I nearly misunderstood the former master’s intent. The monk asked, "I do not know for certain—did the former master truly know it or not?
The Master said, "If he did not know it, how could he have spoken thus? If he did know it, how could he have been willing to speak thus?"

The Way. ○ From the end of the Dazhong era of the Tang dynasty, the Master received and guided disciples at Mount Xinfeng. Subsequently, he flourished in his teachings at Dongshan in Gaoyang, Yuzhang.
He provisionally established the five ranks (*wuwei*), skillfully received those of the three capacities, extensively expounded the single sound, and broadly propagated it to the myriad species.
Transversely drawing his precious sword, he cleared away the dense forest of various views; wondrously harmonizing with profound penetration, he cut through the ten thousand ends.
...and his piercing insights. Furthermore, he attained Cao Shan’s profound realization of the ultimate meaning and his wondrous, sublime teachings.
His Way harmonized the sovereign and the minister through the interplay of the partial and the correct. Thus, the mysterious wind of the Dongshan school spread throughout the world;

consequently, the masters of all quarters unanimously honored him, calling it the Cao-Dong School. Once, when the Master was preparing a vegetarian feast for the anniversary of Yunyan’s death, a monk asked: "Master..."
"What instructions did you receive from Yunyan? The Master said, "Although I was there, I received no instructions.
[The monk] asked, "If you received no instructions, why did you prepare a vegetarian feast for him? The Master said, "How would I dare go against him?
[The monk] asked, "When you first met Nanquan, why did you instead prepare a vegetarian feast for Yunyan? The Master said, "I do not value the past."
The Master’s virtue, conduct, and Buddhist Dharma were such that [his disciples] only revered him and did not speak of his faults for him.
[A monk] asked: "When you, Preceptor, prepare a vegetarian feast for your late teacher, do you still acknowledge him? The Master said: "I half acknowledge and half do not acknowledge.

The monk asked: "Why do you not fully acknowledge him? The Master said: "If I were to fully acknowledge him, I would be failing my late teacher. [Commentary] [Verse] A monk asked: "When cold and heat arrive..."
"How do you avoid it? The Master said, "Why not go to a place where there is neither cold nor heat? He asked, "What is this place where there is neither cold nor heat?
The Master said, "When it is cold, it freezes you, O *śrāmaṇera*; when it is hot, it burns you, O *śrāmaṇera*.

Ascending the hall, he said, "Is there anyone who does not repay the four debts of gratitude or the three realms of existence? The assembly had no reply. He spoke again, "If you do not realize this meaning, how..."

The Master asked, "What is 'far away'? Sansheng said, "One must not call him a person from 'over there. The Master said, "..."
"How is it that they are not remote from one another? Sanshan said, "There is no place for discrimination. Sanshan asked the Master, "In the empty kalpa, there is no human habitation;
who dwells there? The Master said, "I do not know. Sanshan said, "Does this person still have an underlying meaning or intention?
The Master said, "Why does the Master not ask him? Sanshan said, "I am asking right now. The Master said, "What is the meaning of this? Sanshan did not respond.
"Yes. When Dongshan passed away, after the disciple had completed his funeral rites, he traveled to Daguang Moshan at Mount Daopei in Tanzhou.
There he encountered Moshan addressing the assembly, saying: "A high-minded traveler must sleep amidst sounds and forms, and sit or lie down amidst sounds and forms, only then will he attain it.
The Master stepped forward and asked: "What is the phrase that does not fall into sounds and forms? Moshan held up his whisk. The Master said: "This is..."
Dropping the phrase regarding sounds and forms, Mian put down his whisk and returned to the abbot’s quarters. Since the Master did not attain realization, he took his leave of Xiangyan.
Xiangyan said, "Why do you not stay for a while? The Master replied, "I have no affinity with you, Reverend. Xiangyan asked, "What is your reason for this?"
"Try to bring it up," the Master said. The Master then recounted the previous conversation. Yanguan said, "I have a saying. The Master asked, "What is it?
Yanguan said, "When speech issues forth, it is not sound; before form appears, there is no object. The Master said, "So there is someone here!

He then instructed Xiangyan, saying, "In the future, when you have a place to dwell, I shall come to see you," and then he departed. Later, Guishan asked Yanguan: [The text continues with Guishan's question.]
The Master asked, "Elder Aidi, who was discussing sounds and forms—is he here? Yanguan replied, "He has already departed. Muzhou said, "Did you ever mention him to him?
Yanguan said, "I did indeed respond to him. Muzhou said, "Try mentioning him to me. Yanguan repeated his previous words.
Miaoyan said, "What did he say? Yanguan replied, "He deeply approved of me. Miaoyan laughed and said, "I thought this short fellow had some real merit;
it turns out it was only in this! This boy, in the future, if he has a place where he dwells—
When near a mountain there is no firewood to burn; when near water there is no water to drink. The Master heard that Master Daomian of Daguang on Mount Fuzhou was addressing the assembly, saying:
"A phrase and no-phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree. The Master specifically entered the mountains and went to him. He encountered Daomian plastering a wall and asked:
"I have heard the Master say, 'A phrase and no-phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree. Is this so? Daomian replied:
The Master said, "If you suddenly encounter a tree that has fallen and the vines withered, where would the phrase return?
Baizhang set down his *niwan* (meditation mat), laughed heartily, and returned to the abbot's quarters. The Master said, "I traveled three thousand li and sold my bedding just for this matter."
[The Master] arrived. "How can you, Preceptor, deceive me? Guishan called to his attendant, "Bring two hundred coins and give them to this Elder.

He then instructed him, saying, "In the future, there will be 'One-Eyed Dragon' who will break through [your delusions] for you. The next day, Guishan ascended the hall for teaching. The Master came forward and asked:
"The principle of the Dharma-body is a principle beyond the profound and subtle; even not falling into the realm of right and wrong is still..."
[The Master asked,] "What is the matter concerning the Dharma-body? What is the matter that transcends the Dharma-body? Guishan held up his whisk.
The Master said, "This is still a matter concerning the Dharma-body. Guishan asked, "What is the matter that transcends the Dharma-body?

The Master snatched the whisk away, folded it, and threw it onto the ground, then returned to the assembly. Guishan said, "Dragons and snakes are easy to distinguish; a son of the Śākya is difficult to deceive."
Later, when the Master heard that Zen Master Mingzhao Qian of Wuzhou had begun his public ministry (Qian was one-eyed), he went directly to pay his respects.
Mingzhao asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Min. Mingzhao asked, "Have you ever been to Dayu? The Master replied, "I have. Mingzhao said:
"What words or phrases are there? The Master brought up the previous conversation. Zhao said, "Miaoshan may indeed be said to have his head straight and his tail straight;

Zhao said, "This will cause Guishan’s laughter to become ever more fresh. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "Guishan originally had a blade hidden within his smile.
He prostrated from afar and repented his error. [Verse] One day Zhao asked: "A tiger gives birth to seven cubs."
"Which one has no tail? The Master said, "The seventh one has no tail" (as seen in Mingzhao Qian’s *Changuan*). When the Master arrived at Jia Shan, Jia Shan ascended the hall for formal discourse.
The Master asked, "I have heard your words: 'Before one's eyes there is no dharma, yet the intent lies before one's eyes. What is this 'dharma that is not before one's eyes'?
Jia Shan replied, "The night moon sheds its radiance; the clear pool has no reflection. The Master gave a great shake of his meditation seat.
Changshi asked, "Master, what do you say? The Master said, "Before one's eyes there is no dharma;
it is utterly unobtainable. Changshi said, "The assembly, look at this warrior! [Verse] Later, the Master moved to Shushan. He ascended the hall and said:
"This sick monk, before the Xiantong era, understood the affairs of the Dharma-body (dharmakāya). After the Xiantong era, I understood that which is above the Dharma-body."
[The Master] was engaged in a task. Yunmen came out and asked, "What is the matter of the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A withered stump. [Yunmen] asked, "What is the matter above the Dharma-body?
The Master said, "Not a withered stump. [Yunmen] asked, "Do you permit me to speak of principle or not?"

The Master said, "Xu said, 'A withered stump—is this not clarifying matters on the side of the Dharma-body? The Master said, 'It is. Xu said, 'Something other than a withered stump—is this not clarifying matters above the Dharma-body?

The Master said, "If they cannot be complete, then how is it? Jingqing said, "Within this, there is no path of acceptance."
[The Master] said: "At last, this sick monk's intention is satisfied. [Verse: A monk finished constructing a stupa for his master's longevity and informed the master.
The master asked, "How much money will you give to the craftsmen? The monk replied, "Everything depends on the Master.
The master said, "Will you give three coins to the craftsmen? Or two coins? Or one coin? If you can say it, I will [grant you my seal]."
A monk came to build a stupa for his deceased master, but the monks said nothing. Later, the monk reported this to Master Xian of Daling Hermitage (who was Luoshan).
Daling asked, "Has anyone been able to say anything about this? The monk replied, "No one has been able to say anything. Daling said, "When you return, tell Shushan:
'If you give three coins to the craftsman, the Master will certainly not receive the stupa in this life; if you give [more]...'"
"Two coins for the artisan. The master and the artisan acted as one hand. "If you give him only one coin, it will cause the artisan's eyebrows and whiskers to fall out.
The monk returned and spoke according to the instructions; the Master maintained his dignified deportment.
Looking toward Mount Daling, he prostrated and sighed, saying: "I thought there was no one; yet on Mount Daling, an ancient Buddha has emitted light that reaches this very place.
Even so, it is like a lotus blooming in the depths of winter. Later, when Mount Daling heard these words, he said:
"For me to speak thus is already like a tortoise's hair growing three feet long. [Verse] A monk asked: "What is the Teacher of all Buddhas? The Master [said:]...

A monk asked, "What is the meaning of winter's arrival? The Master said, "The capital produces *dahuang* (rhubarb)."
Chan Master Qinglin Shiqian ascended the hall and said: "Within the gate of the Patriarchs, the 'Bird Path' is profound and subtle. When effort reaches its limit, all turns;
if it is not investigated, it is difficult to clarify. You people must directly investigate apart from mind, intellect, and consciousness, and study by exiting the paths of ordinary and sage."
Only then can you be entrusted with the lineage. If it is not so, you are not my son.
Chan Master Ren of Baishui at Gaoyuan once established a memorial feast for the late Master Dongshan.
A monk asked, "When we make offerings to the former master, does the former master still come? The Master said, "Offer yet another portion of the meal. [Verse] Entering the hall, the Old Monk said:
Ordinarily, I do not wish to dally with the sons and daughters of others before sounds and after forms.
Why? It is because sound is not sound, and form is not form. A monk asked, "What is meant by 'sound is not sound'?
The Master said, "Can it be called form? The monk asked, "What is meant by 'form is not form'? The Master said, "Can it be called sound? The monk bowed.
The Master said, "Tell me, shall I speak for you, or shall I answer your words? If you can understand it here, you will have a point of entry.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said, "Falling flowers follow the flowing stream; the bright moon ascends the solitary peak."
A monk asked Chan Master Baima Ru, "What is the fundamental matter of the student? The Master said, "Last night at the third watch, the moon was at its zenith.
The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A shrimp at the bottom of the well swallows the moon."
Chan Master Longya Juedun [Commentary] [Verse]: The Master asked Cuibei, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch?
Cuiwei said, “Bring me the meditation board. The Master then passed over the meditation board. Cuiwei took it and struck him.
The Master said, “I am willing enough to be struck, yet there is still no meaning of the Patriarch. He then asked Linji, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch? Linji said:
"Bring me the meditation cushion. The Master then passed the cushion over. Linji caught it and struck him. The Master said, "Strike as you will;
however, there is still no meaning of the Patriarch. Later, a monk asked, "When you were traveling on pilgrimage, you questioned two venerable elders regarding the meaning of the Patriarch.
I wonder, did those two venerable elders understand it or not? The Master said, "They understood, indeed they understood; however—"
There was no meaning of the Patriarch in it. [Verse] The Master again cited the story of Deshan’s head falling off.

Thereupon, he examined his own faults and stayed with Dongshan to participate in the communal practice and seek instruction. One day he asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Dongshan said:
"I will tell you as soon as the water in the cave flows backward. Only then did the Master realize its meaning. Ascending the hall, he said:

"Those who study the profound mystery must penetrate beyond the patriarchs and Buddhas before they can succeed. As the Venerable Xinfeng said: 'The teachings of the patriarchs and Buddhas are like having an enemy born to you;
only then does one have the capacity for true study. If you cannot penetrate them, you will be deceived by the patriarchs and Buddhas. A monk asked: "The patriarchs and Buddhas..."
"Furthermore, do you have a mind that deceives others? The Master said, "Tell me, do the rivers and lakes have a mind that obstructs people?
He replied, "Although the rivers and lakes have no mind to obstruct people, because people cannot cross them, the rivers and lakes become an obstruction to those people.
One cannot say that the rivers and lakes do not obstruct people. Likewise, although the Buddhas and Patriarchs have no mind to deceive people..."
It is something that people of this age cannot penetrate; thus, the Patriarchs and Buddhas are merely deceiving people. One must not say that the Patriarchs and Buddhas do not deceive people.

If one can penetrate beyond the Patriarchs and Buddhas, such a person has transcended them. If it is so, only then can one embody the intent of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and become equal to those of the "upward direction.
If you have not yet penetrated this, then merely studying the Buddhas and studying the Patriarchs will lead you astray for ten thousand kalpas.
[The monk] asked, "When will there be an end to this? The Master said, "How can you avoid being deceived by the patriarchs and Buddhas?
The Master said, "A practitioner must attain realization for themselves before it is possible. [Verse: Question: How should one apply effort throughout the twelve periods of the day?

The Master said, "It is like a person without hands who wishes to perform a fist; only then is it possible. [Verse] Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Wait..."
The stone tortoise understands speech and will tell you at once. [The Master] said, "The stone tortoise speaks. The Master asked, "What did it say to you? [Verse]:
One asks, "What did the ancients attain that they simply ceased [their seeking]? The Master said, "It is like a thief entering an empty house."
Question: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said: "This one question is the most bitter. (Baoci said: "This one question is the best.
When Chan Master Huijing of Huayan was serving as the *venerable* at Luopo, he once struck the gavel for a communal labor session, saying:
"Those in the upper quarters shall carry firewood; those in the lower quarters shall hoe the ground. The First Seat asked, "What is the Holy Monk doing? The Master replied: "He presides in the hall."
Do not sit improperly. Do not fall between two opposing functions. The Master asked Dongshan, "This student has no path of principle;

Dongshan said, "Then from where do you derive this emotional consciousness? The Master said, "I am asking in earnest. Dongshan said, "If that is so, then..."

"You must go directly to the place where there are ten thousand miles and not a single blade of grass. The Master asked, "Is it permitted for me to go to the place where there are ten thousand miles and not a single blade of grass?
Mount said, "You must go exactly like that. Later, Emperor Zhuangzong of the Later Tang asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master replied, "Having searched through the entire treasury of the Dragon Palace, no multitude of meanings can fully describe them."
A monk asked Chan Master Man of Jiufeng, "Everyone says they come to seek instruction; I wonder, does the Master actually provide salvation?

The Master said, "Yañña lost his head and his mind went mad. The monk said, "Is there anyone who is not mad? The Master said, "..."
[The Master] said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is it to be one who is not mad? The Master said, "Suddenly dawning awareness on the road, yet the eyes do not open.

[Verse: He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "From Min Province. The Master said, "It was no easy matter to travel so far. The monk said, "It was not difficult; with a single step, I arrived."
The Master said, "Is there anyone who does not move a single step? The monk replied, "There is. The Master asked, "How can such a person reach this place?
The monk was speechless. The Master drove him out with his staff. A monk asked, "An ancient said, 'True reality is established through delusion;

The Master said, "Arising and falling, grasping and depending. [The student] asked, "Setting aside these two paths, how can one attain the perfect and eternal?
The Master said, "If one does not revere the Goddess of Merit, who would begrudge the Woman of Darkness?"
Chan Master Beiyuan Tong ascended the hall and said: "Venerable elders, what matters are there? Come forth and discuss them!

If you possess the highest capacity, it need not be like this. But if you belong to the middle or lower capacities, you must strip away the thresholds and bases of the gates until they are bare and empty;
do not let them sink into the mud and water. Above all, you must quickly simplify your affairs; you must simply be without [delusion]."
If the mind departs, one may learn a thousand or ten thousand things, yet they will result only in intellectual understanding.
What connection does this have with the gate of the patch-robed monks? Master Cuan of Dongshan asked the former Dongshan, "What is the essential way to transcend? Dongshan replied, "The *ācārya*."
"Smoke arises beneath your feet. The Master attained immediate realization and did not travel elsewhere. Yunju further advanced his discourse, saying, "I truly dare not fail the Master;
smoke arises beneath my feet. The Mountain said, "To be profound at every step is the arrival of mastery. [Verse] A monk asked:
"When a pure practitioner does not enter Nirvana, and a precept-breaking bhikṣu does not enter hell, what then? At that time...

The Master said, "You must be thus; only then will you be able to sit securely. Daowen responded, "Yes, yes. [Verse]: Entering the hall [to teach].

[Verse] A monk asked: "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all share the single path to the gate of Nirvāṇa. I wonder—"

The Master said, "Riding alone upon a thousand-li elephant beyond all things; striking the golden bell beneath ten-thousand-year-old pines. [Additional Record] (The Master often spoke thus in response to the occasion. "Excellent!"
The Zen Master Longguang Yin (also known as Dage Heshang, "Elder Brother"), when asked by a monk, "Why does one and the same Piṇḍola attend to offerings from four worlds?
replied, "A thousand rivers share the same moon; ten thousand miles all encounter spring. He then spoke this verse: Atop the Peak of Dragon Light, ...
The Jewel Moon-Disk: it illuminates heaven and earth and pierces the dark clouds. The Venerable One does not shift from his original singular substance;
a thousand households reflect its image, ten thousand households bask in spring.
Master Jujū asked a monk, "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? The Master said, "The trees bear the color of the Canglang River."
A mountain stretches across the sky as a single stroke of blue.
Chan Master Chongyun established the Warmth Chamber (Ŏnmil-yon) and made it his constant practice to provide water and administer medicine. A monk asked, "The main road is level and open;
how should one tread upon it? The Master said, "If I were to point it out for you, you would be heading off toward the east, west, south, or north."
Chan Master Shuìlóng Zhāng ascended the hall and said: "In years past, this old monk traveled beyond the Yangtze River, through Lingnan, Jing, and Hu.
There was no monastery with a master of learning where I did not go to inquire. This was solely for the sake of meeting with you all today, each wishing to know the place of departure.
Yet, throughout the various quarters, there is ultimately no divergent teaching; it simply instructs each person to bring their wild mind to rest."
Do not seek it elsewhere; simply follow the direction and let things be as they truly are. Yet, there is no "true" state to be allowed to be.
Enjoy things according to the occasion, yet there is no "occasion" that can be employed. Even if you were to show compassion with bitter words, one cannot call day night;
even with the utmost skillfulness, one can never point east and call it west. Should one be able to do so, that would merely be a supernatural power manifesting a marvel—it has nothing to do with me.

If you belong to the class of those who merely parrot words, yet fail to examine yourselves and recognize your own errors, you are simply attempting to pluck flowers from the sky or grasp the moon in the waves.
Will you ever attain the power of realization? For now, each of you should withdraw and reflect;

if you suddenly come to accept this, you will finally know that I, the old man of Rui Long, had no choice but to lead you on such a long and winding path. Do you accept it now? At that time, a monk asked:
"What is the realm of Rui Long? The Master said, "Do you not see it? He asked, "What is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "The younger generation is to be feared."
Chan Master Baociyu asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Wolong. The Master said, "How long have you been there?
The monk said, "I have spent the winter and passed through the summer there. The Master said, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight.
Why were you there for so long? The monk said, "In a lion’s den, there are no other beasts. The Master said, "Then try to let out a lion’s roar. The monk said, "I..."
If Jia were to let out a lion’s roar, he would have no *upādhyāya*. The Master said, "Out of consideration for you as a newcomer, I grant you thirty blows.
[Verse] A monk asked: "When emotion arises, wisdom is obstructed; when conceptualization changes, the essence becomes distinct. But what is it like when emotion has not yet arisen?"
The Master said, "Separated. [The monk] asked, "Before any emotion has arisen, what is it that separates? The Master said, "This lad has not yet met the right person."
Chan Master Hanzhu was asked by a monk, "What is the Eye of the True Dharma? The Master said, "The spirit tree in front of the gate.
[The monk] asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "A poor man carries his child across [a river];
affection and love compete as they follow the current. He asked a monk, "Existence is not it; non-existence is not it; neither existence nor non-existence is not it. You..."
"What is its original name? He replied, "The student already possesses its name. The Master said, "It is not that you lack the name;
but ultimately, what is its name? He replied, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "For now, rejoice that there is no connection."
[The student] asked, "How is it that this is so? The Master said, "In the place of intimacy. [The student] asked again, "I request one more question:
the student cannot say it; I request the Master to say it. The Master said, "Come another day and I will tell you. [The student] said, "Why do you not say it right now?"
The Master said, "It is impossible to find anyone who can grasp this statement. He then asked a monk, "Zhang, Wang, Li, or Zhao—none of these are your original surname.
What is your original surname? The monk replied, "I share the same surname as the Master. The Master said, "Setting aside for a moment that you share the same surname, what is your original surname?
The monk replied, "Wait until the waters of the Han River flow backward, and then I shall tell the Master."
The Master Dao said, "Why do you not speak right now? [The monk] replied, "Has the Han River ever flowed upstream? The Master then desisted.
When Chan Master Ziling Kuangyi first arrived at Panlong, he saw a monk ask, "The green depths are as clear as a mirror;
where does Panlong reside? The Dragon replied, "Sunken sands reveal no bottom; floating waves are full of jagged peaks. The Master did not approve. The Dragon then invited him [to stay].

Regarding the Master’s Way, the Master said: "The golden dragon soars far beyond the azure heavens; how could it be detained within the depths of the pond? The mechanism of the jade wheel—the dragon is willing to abide therein.
After he took up residence there, a monk asked: "Before one has yet taken human form, what does one do? The Master replied: "The stone ox walks step by step through fire;
looking back, it need no longer chew the grass in the midday sun."
A monk asked Chan Master Wei of Tong’an, “How was it before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master said, “Meeting a divine tree by the road, everyone who sees it raises their hands in reverence. The monk asked, “And how was it after he saw him? The Master said, “In the inner room there is no spirit-bed;
the whole family does not wear mourning. One day, as the Master was touring the mountains with the assembly following behind him, he said, “The green [grass] before the steps...”
Bamboo. Yellow flowers beneath the steps. An ancient said, "True Suchness is Prajñā. Tongan, however, was not so. A monk said, "The ancients were also like you, Master.
The Master said, "One who does not crave the taste of fragrant bait may truly be called a dragon in a green abyss.

[The monk] said, "The eyes of all quarters do not find fault with Yuanming. The Master said, "Dharmācārya, you sit with eyes closed on the Mid-Autumn festival, yet you laugh at the moon for being nonexistent."
Guang said, "There are green bamboos before the steps and yellow chrysanthemums beneath the pavement. What about that? The Master said, "Annan has not yet submitted;
how could Sebei have surrendered? The monk bowed, and the Master said, "His fame is heard everywhere. He asked a monk, "At dawn and at dusk, you eat and drink."
“There is no place to hide one’s body. Do you say there is such a principle? The monk asked, “How about you, Master? The Master struck him with his whisk.
The monk said, “A servant’s hand is but a commoner; why boast of being a skilled hand? The Master said, “Holding the whip and tilting the hat—how could that be you, Reverend?
The monk asked, “In the Way of ancient and modern times, where can one hide the body? The Master said, “What do you say, Reverend? The monk respectfully...
He went out again. The Master said, "Not yet. (End of Volume 13 of the *Huìyuán*).
When Chan Master Qiǎng of Shànglán first traveled to seek instruction, he asked Xuefeng, "What is the very essence of Xuefeng?
Xuefeng struck him on the head with his staff. The Master responded, "Yes. Xuefeng laughed loudly. Later, the Master received the Dharma seal from Dongshan.
While Chan Master Tianchi Long was engaged in communal labor at Jinfeng carrying firewood, Jinfeng asked, "Has everyone carrying firewood crossed the water?
The Master replied, "There is one person who has not crossed the water. Jinfeng asked, "If he has not crossed the water, does he still carry firewood?
The Master said, "Although he does not carry firewood, he must not be disturbed."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhen of Yizhou, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Casting for a jade hare in a clear pool. The monk asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "Clapping hands and laughing at the spring breeze."
When a monk asked Chan Master Xingyin of Foshouyan, "What is the manifestation of the physical body?
the Master held up one finger (Fayan commented elsewhere: "Is there anything more?").
Chan Master Huizhong of Guiyang visited Cao’an. An asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Mount Liúmóu. An asked, "Do you see the six eyes?
The Master said, "I am not afflicted with double pupils. An approved of this. The Master subsequently returned to his former mountain.

This occurred during the reign of Emperor Wuzong of the Tang dynasty, when the Buddhist teachings were suppressed and [the Master] was required to adopt the dress of a commoner. When Emperor Xuanzong restored the religion, the Master said:
"The ancients had a saying: 'An ascendant Daoist does not receive the registers; a Buddha-to-be śrāmaṇera does not undergo full ordination. He remained merely a layman (*avadātavasana*).
He did not eat after midday and practiced meditation without fixed hours. For thirty years he did not step outside the mountains. He once addressed his disciples:
He said: "That sentient beings cannot attain liberation is due to the entanglements of their emotions. To awaken to the Way is easy; to clarify the Way is difficult.

A monk asked, "How can one attain the clarification of the Way? The Master said, "Simply shed your emotional views, and the Way will become clear of itself. Now, 'clarification' (ming) means 'to trust.
It is like a snake-handler who trusts in the power of his incantations and the efficacy of his medicines to coil and play with snakes, even tucking them into his sleeves."

Within [this state], there is no difficulty. Those who do not yet know the power of mantras and medicines are terrified and flee; however, if one simply observes the mind with clarity, emotional views are immediately shattered.
As for those who now harbor a thousand doubts and ten thousand anxieties and find no application [for this teaching], it is because they have not yet seen their own minds.
When Chan Master Tong’an Zhi was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and said: “Before the Multi-Child Stupa, the lineage son is outstanding;
before the Five Old Peaks, what is the matter? He raised this three times, but no one offered a response. Finally, the Master [Tong’an] stepped forward and said:
“Standing in formation outside the Night-Bright Curtain, ten thousand miles of songs celebrate the Great Peace. Tong’an said: “It must be this one!”
The donkey-man has finally attained it. [Verse] A monk asked: "At a place where the two capacities do not reach, how can one proclaim it?

The Master said: "Meeting nothing anywhere, not failing within the profound. [Verse] Question: "Whenever there are words and phrases, they all fall into the present moment; what about when students come forward?"
"Please, Master, point it out directly. The Master said, "It does not manifest before the eyes; one is not deluded after the phrase. [The student] asked, "What about the matter beyond this?
The Master said, "It is utterly distinct and unchanging; to deviate from this very aim is to go astray."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhimen Qin: "When two mirrors reflect each other, why is there no image between them?
The Master said, "One must even conceal oneself. The monk asked, "What about when the mirrors are broken and the stands are gone? The Master held up his fist.
Chan Master Siji of Jianfu [Verse]: A monk asked, "What is it like when there is no Buddha in the ancient hall? The Master said, "From where does the Brahma-sound come?
The monk asked, "If one does not rely on cultivation or realization, how can one achieve completion? The Master said, "Cultivation and realization constitute non-completion."
When Chan Master Dayang Jian was first entering the room at Lingquan, Lingquan asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From the monks' hall. Lingquan said, "Why did you not strike the pillar? At these words, the Master had an awakening.
[Verse] A monk asked, "What is the profound principle? The Master said, "Money hanging on the wall.
A monk asked, "What is the Sword of the Dharma King? The Master said, "Look behind your head."
A monk asked Master Wufeng Shao, “What is the primary meaning? The Master struck the meditation seat and said, “If it were not for Xiantuo, it would be thousands of miles away.”
Chan Master Guangdeyi went to visit the former Chan Master Guangde. He prostrated and asked, "What is the Master’s secret, hidden place?
Guangde said, "To hide one's body, it is not necessary to dwell in mountain crags or valleys; even amidst the bustling crowds of the marketplace, those who truly see are rare.
The Master said, "If that is so, then I shall go to offer water and flowers. Guangde said, "Suddenly, clouds and mist gather—what will you do, Dharma-heir?"
The Master said, "Gathering and drawing [water] is not in vain. Guangde joyfully remarked, "The assembly, look upon the second-generation Guangde!
The Master subsequently succeeded him as abbot, gathering disciples and expounding the Dharma. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Clad in a straw raincoat, riding a cow backward;
the grass is so deep that the horns are not revealed. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said:
The fish leap in waters that have no source; the oriole sings among flowers on withered trees. Question: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said: "When the snow is cold, one turns toward the fire; when the sun is warm, one leans against the warmth. Question: "What is the guest within the guest?

The Master said: "The wanderer has no home or plan; drifting like a tumbleweed, he does not know himself. [The questioner] asked: "What is the host within the guest? The Master said: "A thatched door."
[Huangbo] hung a pearl curtain and asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "The dragon palace is spread with grass for sitting. [Huangbo] asked, "What is the host within the host?
The Master said, "Though the Crown Prince is the legitimate heir, he does not face the august countenance of Yao.

[Someone] asked, "How was it before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A newly opened pickle jar, buzzing with flies. [The questioner] asked, "And after he saw him? The Master said, "The lid is sealed tight; no one can see inside."

"What? The Master said, "The bottom has been worn through and washed away; it is cold and still. [Verse]: A questioner asked, "An ancient said: 'The path of words is cut off; it is neither past, future, nor present.
What is the principle of this? The Master said, "How many kalpas have passed since Maitreya entered nirvana, yet Huiming has still not descended to Kapilavastu?
(Added from another collection.)
A monk asked Chan Master Guangde Zhou: "What is it like when a poor man returns home? The Master said: "Upon entering the gate, his face is not seen;

everywhere is the spring of the old garden. [Verse]: The teaching says: "Ajita, one who does not sever afflictions and does not cultivate meditative concentration—this person will undoubtedly attain Buddhahood.
How is this principle to be understood? The Master said: "The salt is exhausted, and the charcoal is spent."
Again, [a monk] asked, "What about when there is neither salt nor charcoal? The Master said, "Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful;
to speak of them to one who is sorrowful is to kill that person with grief."
Chan Master Shimen Che [Verse]: A monk asked, "What is the meaning of Yunguang acting as an ox? The Master said: "In the narrow alley, he does not ride a golden horse;
returning to the path, he puts on his tattered robe. [Verse]: Question: "How is it when the year has ended and the age is exhausted? The Master said:
"Old Wang of the eastern village burns paper money at night. Ascending the hall, he said: "The original source of all sentient beings is the Buddha."
The nature [of all things] is like the bright moon suspended in the sky;
it is only because of the obscuration of drifting clouds that it cannot manifest as light, as illumination, as the Way, as the path, as a boat, as oars, as a refuge, or as a resting place.

The fundamental Buddha-nature of all sentient beings is likewise so. At that time, Master Fenyang Shanzhao was in the assembly; he stepped forward and asked: "The bright moon is obscured by the ocean of clouds."
“Not so. Yangshan asked, “When radiant light penetrates straight through the crystal palace, what then? The Master said, “Stone walls and mountain rivers are no obstacle;
beyond the realm of Jambudvīpa, one may soar at will. Yangshan said, “If that is so, then a thousand miles away we share the same bottomless bowl, and people everywhere sing songs of peace.
The Master said, “How do you sing the song of peace? Yangshan said, “Without falling [into conceptualization].”
"The five notes have no connection with the six pitch-pipes. The Master asked, "Is there anyone who can harmonize them? Yang said, "I request that the Master not withhold his compassion.
The Master said, "May you, O Benevolent One, preserve and maintain this well for yourself."
A monk asked Zen Master Ziling Wei, "What is a person of great ferocity? The Master said, "A stone ox walks step by step through fire;
looking back, it refuses to chew the grass in the sunlight. [The monk] asked, "What is a person who commits the five heinous crimes?
The Master said, "Setting fire at night to burn the Palace of Formlessness; when dawn breaks, wearing a hat and entering Chang'an. [The monk] asked, "What is filial piety?"
To one who followed him, the Master said: "Step by step, he carries riceless rice in his hand; with palms folded before the hall, he does not raise his head.
A questioner asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said: "Vivid blue waves flow upon the flames of a red furnace."
A monk asked Master Dàlàng of Xingyuan, "Since you are the River God, why were you swept away by the water?
The Master said, "Only by following the current does one attain the wondrous; to remain on the bank, however, results in delusion."
A monk asked Chan Master Xian of Puning, "We have lived together through past kalpas; why do you not recognize me as close? The Master said, "Who?
The monk said, "Wait for me to say it. The Master said, "I thought you did not understand my words. [Another] asked, "Across a thousand mountains and ten thousand waters..."

"How does one ascend? The Master said, "The path through the blue sky has no gaps; those who reach it do not lose their functional insight. Cen Yuan-guan of Liangshan asked a monk, "When the house-thief is difficult to guard against, what then? The Master said, "If you recognize him, he cannot be an enemy. The monk asked, "After recognizing him, what then? The Master said, "Exile him to the realm of non-arising. The monk asked, "Is this not he? The Master said, "He is. The monk asked, "What about when he is not there? The Master said, "Do not look for him elsewhere. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him after he has departed? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him while he is still within the house? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is outside the house? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is neither inside nor outside the house? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is neither inside nor outside the house, yet is present everywhere? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is neither inside nor outside the house, yet is present everywhere, and one has recognized him? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is neither inside nor outside the house, yet is present everywhere, and one has recognized him, and he is gone? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is neither inside nor outside the house, yet is present everywhere, and one has recognized him, and he is gone, and one has left the house? The Master said, "He is right here before you. The Master said, "He is right here before you. The monk asked, "How can one avoid being deceived by him when he is neither inside nor outside the house, yet is present everywhere, and one has recognized him, and he is gone, and one has left the house, and he is gone forever, and one has attained liberation? [The monk asked: "Is there no place to settle the body and establish one's life? The Master said, "Dead water does not harbor dragons. [The monk] asked, "What is the dragon of living water?
The Master said, "It stirs up waves but does not create billows. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when suddenly the torrential pool overflows and the mountains topple?
The Master descended from his seat, seized him, and said, "Do not let it wet the corner of this old monk’s *kāṣāya*. [The monk] asked, "What is the student?"
The Master said, "An emperor within the realm; a general beyond the frontier. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when one proceeds in this very manner?
The Master said, "A bright moon hangs in the sky, yet one sits in darkness within the room. [Verse]: Question: What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Do not speak in such confusion.
When Chan Master Pujing Changjue first visited Guizong, he attained awakening upon hearing the Dharma.

As Guizong was about to pass into nirvana, he summoned the Master, patted him on the back, and said, "You have a karmic affinity with the Dharma; in the future, you shall save the multitudes. No one can fathom the extent of your capacity."

The Master considered that because the times were shallow and ignorant, they were unfit to bear the ultimate teachings; had he revealed them to those who were not suitable vessels, it would have caused them to incur the blame of slander and reproach.
"I would rather not strive to open the Dharma," he thought. Thus, on the third, eighth, and thirteenth days of every month, he provided bathing facilities for tens of thousands of monastics.
The Master once said to his disciples, "If only the gate of wisdom remains unobstructed, how could blessings ever be hindered? ○ Tao [the name of the official] was a Secretariat Drafter (Jigongseng).
Guo entered the monastery, paid his respects, and asked, "The Sūtras state that 'to be free from all marks is to be called a Buddha.
Yet, before our very eyes, all manner of marks are in profusion. How can one be free from them? The Master said, "Gishi, what have you seen? Tao was delighted and held him in high esteem.
From then on, although kings, dukes, and great officials repeatedly recommended him for official robes and titles, he declined and would not accept them.
Chan Master Yung-ching Te-fu [Verse]: When the Military Commissioner Cheng invited the Master to ascend the seat at the government office, a general from the musical corps came forward to prostrate.

Rising, he looked back toward the mounting platform and said, "I do not ask about 'drinking up the waters of the West River in a single gulp,' but I request the Master to swallow this mounting platform before the steps.
The Master opened both hands and sang out, "Wipe it clean and bring it here! The general...
Reflect deeply.
When Chan Master Shimen Yuan was first serving as a field overseer under Master Shitou, Shimen asked him, "What is the water-buffalo of the fields?
The Master replied, "Its horns turn and tower over heaven and earth; in every direction, spring is everywhere. Later, Shimen asked again, "The water..."
"Is the ox well? The Master said, "It has never lacked water and grass. [The monk] asked, "What about the work in the field?
