He asked, “How can it get out? The Master said, “Clouds rise on the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain. He asked about the North...

"What is the meaning of 'hiding one's body within the Dipper'? The Master said, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it enters the water. The Master returned from traveling the mountains.
The Head Seat and the assembly went out to receive him. The Head Seat said, "Master, traveling the mountains must have been difficult due to the rugged terrain.
The Master raised his staff and said, "I relied entirely on the power of this. The Head Seat then snatched the staff away. The Master threw himself down and lay prostrate. Great!
The assembly all stepped forward to support him as he rose. The Master took up his staff and drove them all away at once.
Turning back to look at his attendant, he said, "I have always said that this very power is fully possessed."
While Chan Master Xianglin Chengyuan was among the assembly, during a communal work period of weeding grass, a monk said, "Look!
A house in a lay village is on fire. The Master asked, "Where is the fire? The monk replied, "Can't you see it? The Master said, "I do not see it. The monk exclaimed, "You blind fellow!"
At that time, the entire assembly said, "The Elder Yuan has failed. Later, when Mingjiao Kuan heard of this censure, he sighed and said, "It must have been my elder brother Yuan who did it.
After [Yuan] took up residence, a monk asked, "Why does the delicious flavor of *amṛta* turn into poison?
The Master said, "The paper in Dujiang is expensive. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Treading [on the ground]."
"Who is it that walks? [Verse] Question: "What is the single bowl of lamp-light within the room? The Master said: "Three people take a tortoise and certify it as a turtle. [Verse] Question:
"What is the matter beneath the patched robe? The Master said: "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains. ○ Question:
"If all words and phrases are merely the guest, what is the host? The Master said: "Within the city of Chang'an. [The student] asked: "How does one receive this?"
[The assembly] gathered. The Master said, "A thousand households, ten thousand doors. [Commentary] / [Verse]. Question: "What is the very meaning of the coming from the West?
The Master said, "Sitting for too long leads to fatigue. [Question: "What about when one turns back immediately? The Master said, "Falling into a deep pit. [Verse]. Question:
"In a wilderness of ten thousand acres, who is the master? The Master said, "Look, look; the twelfth month is ending. [Added later]. ○ He ascended the hall and said: "It is..."
"You all have been carrying your alms-bags and traveling abroad for so long; do you yet recognize your own nature?
If you have recognized it, come forth and speak of it. If you have not recognized it, you have merely been deceived by others. Now I ask you all:
throughout your long period of study, while you were sweeping the floors, brewing tea, and wandering through the mountains to enjoy the scenery, was it you who were doing these things?"
Furthermore, it is nailed down. What do you call "self-nature"? Everyone, tell me:
that which from beginning to end is neither changing nor differing, neither high nor low, neither good nor ugly, neither arising nor ceasing—where does it ultimately return?
Do you all yet know where its final destination lies? If you can know its location here, this is the understanding of all Buddhas.
The Dharma-gate of liberation: awakening to the Way and seeing one's nature, from beginning to end, without doubt or hesitation, acting freely as one pleases;
no one can do anything with you. Every word spoken and every breath exhaled truly has its source. It is like a person buying a field: they must obtain the original deed;
if they do not have that original deed, it will ultimately remain insecure, even if they bring the matter before the authorities.
Even a judgment document is of no avail; for it is regrettable that the original contract has not been secured, and in the end, one’s property is seized by others.
You all who practice Chan and study the Way are likewise the same. Is there anyone here who has secured the original contract?
Try bringing it forth and showing it to us. For now, what do you call the "original contract"? Everyone, try!
Look at this! If you are of keen and sharp capacity, as soon as you hear such words spoken, you will know where it leads.

If you do not know where it leads, then even if you learn a thousand kinds of cleverness from the outside, memorizing and interpreting until your mouth flows like a river, you will never reach the ultimate;
it will remain worlds apart from your own self. For now, go and seek it within the very body beneath your robes and bowl.
Look! If you have a point of realization, come here and tell me; I, this old monk, will testify for you.
If you cannot find it, then simply follow the ranks of practitioners.
Chan Master Shouchu of Dongshan [Verse]: When he first visited Yunmen, Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently come from?
The Master replied, "From Chadu. Yunmen asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat? The Master replied, "At Baoci in Hunan. Yunmen asked, "When did you leave there?
The Master replied, "On the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. Yunmen said, "I grant you three blows of the staff. On the following day, the Master went up to the hall again to question him.
The Master asked, "Yesterday I was granted three blows of the staff by the Abbot; I do not know where my fault lay. Nanquan said, "You rice-bag!

You have gone off to Jiangxi and Hunan acting just like this! At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "In the future, I shall go to places where there is no human habitation.
I will not store a single grain of rice nor plant a single stalk of vegetable, yet I shall receive those who come from the ten directions."
"Come! I shall completely extract the nails and pull out the wedges for you.
I will strip away your greasy cap and cast off your stinking hemp robe, so that you may become a carefree monk in a state of ease. Is this not delightful?
The monk said, "Your body is as small as a coconut, yet you open such a wide mouth! The Master then bowed. [Verse]: Entering the hall, he said: "Words do not unfold the matter."
Words do not meet the occasion; those who rely on words perish, and those who linger in phrases are deluded. Can you still attain it?
Within the domain of you monks, when you reach this point, you must possess the eye that discerns the Dharma before you can succeed.
As for Dongshan speaking thus, he too has a fault. But tell me, where does the fault lie? [Verse] A monk asked, "What is the True Eye of the Dharma? The Master said:
A paper wick has no oil. [Commentary] [Verse] Question: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "Three catties of hemp. ○ Question:
"What is the seamless stupa? The Master said: "The stone lion at the crossroads."
Chan Master Letan Qian was asked by a monk, "What is the house style of Letan? The Master said, "How many days has it been since you arrived, Venerable? Question:
"It is said that 'so long as there is even a hair's breadth of it, it is dust.
When there is nothing at all, what then? The Master covered both his eyes with his hands. Question: "Awakening has no gate; how does one enter? The Master said, "Who told you that?"
When asked thus, Chan Master Fengxian Shen offered this verse: Master [Shen] and Master Ming arrived at the Huai River. Seeing people pulling in a net, a fish leaped through it.
The Master said, "Brother Ming, how clever! He is just like a true monk. Ming replied, "Although..."
"But even so, how could it compare to not having walked into the net in the first place? The Master said, "Brother Ming, you lack realization.
Only at midnight did Ming come to understand (Ming was the Chan Master Qingliang Zhiming of Jinling).
A monk asked Chan Master Piyun Ji, "The character 'yi' (以) is not formed; the character 'ba' (八) is not it. I wonder, what character is this?
The Master said, "Listen to an old monk’s verse: The character 'yi' is not it; 'ba' is not formed. The myriad phenomena of the universe are revealed herein.
Even if one were to skillfully explain a thousand kinds of wonders, It is neither a chant nor a scripture. [Question: How is it?
"This is one speck of dust. The Master said, "The green mountains fill the eyes" (the previous case is found in the first volume of the *Lianzhu Sònggǔ*).
Chan Master Shunfeng Shaor asked a monk: "When the True Dharma is wordless, what then? The Master said: "Words. The monk said: "I do not understand;
I beg the Master for the definitive point. The Master said: "A double case. The monk said: "Is there no expedient means? The Master said: "There is none."

Rituals are difficult to accommodate. Question: Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said: "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night.

Chan Master Rouyan Prajñā [Verse]: A monk asked, "In the Western Heaven, they use a wax figure as a test; how is it in this land? The Master said: [Verse] The moon shines upon the mountain peaks, The wind blows across the river sands. If you can understand this directly, There is no need to seek the Buddha’s face. A monk asked: "In the Western Heaven, they use a wax figure as a test; how is it in this land? The Master said: [as above].
He said: "A Korean person’s straw sandals. One day, as the assembly gathered upon hearing the sound of the wooden board, the Master presented this verse: "How wondrous!
At the three strikes of the board, all you kinsmen have come to participate. Since you are well-versed in discerning the proper timing, I shall not speak further.
Thereupon, he descended from his seat.
Chan Master Chenggu of Jianfu was of lofty and pure conduct and possessed a nature that was empty and luminous.
He visited Chan Master Jingxuan of Daguang, who remarked, "He is merely a fellow from the weeds. Thereupon, he went to visit Master Ya of Fuyan, who likewise said, "He is merely a free-spirited monk.
Consequently, he remained silent throughout the day, deeply investigating the grand regulations of the former masters. One day, while perusing...
Upon hearing Yunmen’s words, he suddenly attained enlightenment. From then on, he lived in seclusion, seeking no fame or renown.
He took up residence at the stupa of Chan Master Hongjue at Yunju, where scholars from all directions flocked to him; thus, he was known as "The Ancient Stupa Master.

In the fourth year of the Jingyou era, Fan Gong Zhongyan, while serving as the governor of Poyang, heard of the Master’s virtue and character and invited him to reside at Jianfu Temple to propagate the school.
Feng. [Verse] A monk asked, "Great Good Knowledge, with what do you accord with people? The Master said, "Do not. The monk said, "In that case, there is questioning and answering.
The Master said, "Do not" (slightly different in the *Lianzhu*). Question: "One shout distinguishes guest and host; illumination and function proceed simultaneously.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Dry firewood and damp reeds. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "Blazing red flames."

Heaven. ○ Ascending the hall: Now, those who have left the household life do so for the sake of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*). Within the unconditioned dharma, there is neither benefit nor merit.
Lately, those who have left the household life have become greedily attached to blessings and wisdom, which is entirely contrary to the Way.

If you seek blessings and wisdom, you must first clarify the mind; yet if you wish to realize the Way, there is no place for you to apply the mind. Therefore, I constantly exhort everyone: do not study [in this manner].
As for the Buddha-dharma, simply let the mind rest. Those of sharp faculties attain liberation at that very moment;
those of dull faculties may take three or five years, but at the farthest, no more than ten. If you do not awaken, I, this old monk, shall send you to the Hell of the Plucked Tongue. *Chan*.
A monk asked Chan Master Qīn of Shuangfeng, "What is the realm of Shuangfeng? The Master said, "At night, listen to the water flowing behind the hermitage;
by day, watch the clouds rising from the mountain before you. [Another] asked, "What is the phrase for the Master’s way of benefiting others?"
The Master said: "It is like using the wind to fan the fire. Ascending the hall, he said: "To take one step forward is to lose sight of principle;
to retreat one step is to lose sight of phenomena. Even if you remain entirely motionless, you are still the same as the insentient. A monk asked: "How can one avoid being the same as the insentient?
The Master said: "In movement and stillness, in all your actions. The monk asked: "How can one avoid losing sight of principle and losing sight of phenomena? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"Step forward! Step back! The monk bowed. The Master said, "In the past, there were those who understood it in this way;
I did not approve of them. The monk asked, "I beg the Master to point directly to it. The Master then struck him out. A monk asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye?"

The Master said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [Question: "What is the Sword of the Dharma King? The Master said: "A tempered blade is but a vain display; it is not equal to the Dragon Spring (Longquan) sword.
[Question: "How is it when it is used? The Master said: "Even concealing its point is not permitted;

how much less can one endure its edge being bared? [Verse: Question: Does Piṇḍola, who partakes in offerings throughout the four worlds, succeed in reaching them all? The Master said: It is like the moon.
He entered the water. The questioner asked, "How is it that one acts without becoming entangled? The Master said, "Before the Hall of the Bright Moon, jade dew hangs down;
within the Palace of Crystal, true pearls gleam."

A monk asked Zen Master Zifu Chuan: "When meeting face-to-face, how can one look into the mirror and utter 'Heh'? We beg the Master to bestow half a verse, so as to spare future generations from doubt. The Master said: "A single phrase before the blade transcends the Tamer of Men; if you attempt to ask 'How is it?', you will be at odds for kalpas. The monk said: "If that is so, then people throughout the East and West Hills already know this. But what of the courtyard of Zifu? The Master said: "The courtyard of Zifu is vast and boundless; the ten directions are all within it. The monk bowed. The Master said: "Do not let others see you. The monk departed. [The Master] said, "Whose wind and moon is this? The teacher replied, "For now, take up the previous discourse.
Chan Master Huangyun Yuan ascended the hall and said: "An ancient said: 'In every sight before the eyes, there is never nothing. When facing a critical moment, why do you not speak?"
I, this mountain monk, am not like that. There is never a moment when it is not present before one’s eyes. When the critical moment arrives, what will you say? Take care!
Master Lun of Longjing ascended the seat for his inaugural sermon. Raising his whisk, he said, “Do you understand? If you do, you are adding a head atop your head.
If you do not, you must sever your head to find life. A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “Diligence.”
[The Master] was plowing a field. [A monk] said, "The student does not understand. The Master said, "Harvest the grain early.
Chan Master Dayong Yin was asked by a monk, "Since you are Dayong, why did you drive the monk out?
The Master said, "The great ocean does not admit dust; a small stream is full of weeds. [Another monk] asked, "What is the single path of the ancient Buddhas? The Master pointed.
Deshan said, "I am not asking about this. Deshan replied, "Go! Once, Deshan was scheduled to travel elsewhere with an elderly master, but due to certain circumstances, he did not go.
The master said, "The Buddha’s word is never double. Deshan replied, "The Dharma has no single direction."
A monk asked Zen Master Huayan Hui: "I have heard it said of old: 'Where the deluded mind has no place, that is bodhi.
At the very moment of delusion, is there still bodhi or not? The Master said: "The sound of your coming has already been illumined. The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said:
"'Where the deluded mind has no place, that is bodhi.'"
A monk asked Chan Master Huangbo Faji, “What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, “To serve as a model for all people under heaven.
A monk asked Chan Master Gushan Feng, “Whose song does the Master sing? Whose ancestral wind do you succeed? The Master said, “Snow.”
The plum blossoms on the ridge have bloomed; the old monk in the cloud-cave is startled.
Chan Master Qingbing of Dongshan went to visit Yunmen. Yunmen asked, "Where did you depart from today? He replied, "Huilin.
Yunmen raised his staff and said, "When the Great Master Huilin departs like this, do you see him? He replied, "I deeply understand this question. Yunmen—
He looked left and right with a smile and that was all. From this point on, the Master entered the inner chamber and received the seal of enlightenment.

The Ruler of Jinling invited him to reside at Guangmu; not long after, he was commanded to enter the Chengxin Hall to compile the essential sayings of various regions. After ten years, he was welcomed to take up residence at Dongshan.
Master Beichan Ji ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said:

"The Buddhas of the past, future, and present, and the myriads of Bodhisattvas, all at once turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the tip of this staff. They pass entirely through the nostrils of everyone here.
Do you see them? If you see them, bring them forth for me. If you do not see them, it is very much like standing [in place]."
Dishi Han said after a long silence, "The wind is calm and the waves are still;
it would be better to return to the hall. Master Jingyuan Zhen ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all True Suchness.

Dharma assembly, if you attain True Suchness, then mountains, rivers, and the great earth will be hidden away. If you do not attain it, then you contradict the ultimate words of the ancients. The assembly [was silent].
"Those who have attained the Middle Way, come forth and speak! If you cannot speak, it is better that each of you return to your hall. Take care!
Master Dàfàn Yuán, upon seeing the Holy Monk (Śākyamuni), asked a monk, "How old is this Holy Monk?
The monk replied, "He is exactly the same age as the Master. The Master shouted, "This fellow is quite clever; he has spoken well!"
Cen Master Yuan Guang of Yaoshan asked a newly arrived monk, "Have you come from the south or the north? The monk replied, "From the north.
The Master said, "Without falling into verbal explanations, speak quickly, speak quickly! The monk said, "I am a man of the Way from Fujian; I am well-versed in our local dialect. The Master said:
The assembly departed. A monk said, "It is certainly so. The Master said, "Jump even higher! and struck him.
Chan Master Fenggohai was asked by a monk: "The verdant bamboo stalks are all True Suchness (Tathatā). What is True Suchness?"
The Master said, "A guest who can turn iron into gold hears the name but does not see the form. [The student] said, "If that is so, then I shall take my leave with gratitude.
The Master said, "The delusions of the past persist even to this day."
A monk asked Zen Master Yunmen Qiu, “What is the color-changing mani jewel? The Master said, “The colors are not non-existent;
but what is the jewel? The monk said, “I do not understand; I have come specifically to request your instruction. The Master said, “The clouds have the power to emerge from the mountains;
the water has no sound as it enters the ravine.”
A monk asked Chan Master Foyuan, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Copper head and iron brow. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Stirring up dust and raising clouds of soil."
Chan Master Ciyun Shen was asked by a monk, "What is it like when the precious mirror faces the courtyard? The Master said, "Heaven and earth both lose their color.
A monk asked, "What is the one phrase of the special transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, "I fear knocking on my teeth might startle them."
Chan Master Huchengjian ascended the hall and said: "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all share one path to the gate of Nirvāṇa.
All you practitioners of Chan, how is it that this is the gate of Nirvāṇa? Is it because we have gathered here for a short while that this constitutes the gate of Nirvāṇa?
Do not misunderstand! All you practitioners of Chan, if you do not understand it in this way, is there some other meaning to be discussed?"
"Liangdimu, here at my place, it is already a matter of necessity that I speak to you all in this way; I have already been neglectful of you.
What further benefit would there be in attempting to step forward? O Zen practitioners, simply remain free from affairs, and you will naturally find peace and joy.
Let things proceed spontaneously according to their true nature, acting with ease as conditions arise. Do not go wandering at others' doors."
Household. Seeking understanding and interpretation, one memorizes them in the heart; yet, bound by them, one attains no freedom. Thus, one is constrained by birth and death—when will one emerge?
A pity that time passes; in the blink of an eye, it is already the next life.
You must strive with all your might. At that time, a monk asked: "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The Master said: "The firewood crackles, the bamboo rings."

This was startling to the ears of those present. The monk said, "I, a student of the Way, do not understand. I pray that the Master will point it out directly. The Master said, "The house dog’s barking is fierce and does not cease at night.
A monk asked, "What is the pivotal bolt of the higher realm? The Master said, "Drawing the sword and stirring the Dragon Gate."

Master Huguo ascended the hall for the discourse. "In the ground of ultimate reality, not a single speck of dust is received; within the gate of Buddha-activity, not a single dharma is abandoned. He further said:
"If there were even one dharma, Vairocana would fall into the rank of ordinary beings; if there were not even ten thousand dharmas, Samantabhadra would lose his realm.
All you venerable elders, how can you engage in such intellectual theorizing? Morning and evening you come here in this manner, yet toward all..."
"What did the Elder say that would suffice? If he spoke of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, there are already the presiding masters and the Vinaya masters for those.
If he spoke of worldly truths and causes and conditions, these are not matters for the Sangha to deliberate upon.
If he discussed the Buddha-dharma, how much of the ancestral lineage’s Dharma could possibly be weighed against it? It is none of these; one must know that each case stands on its own."
This is a matter concerning each person’s own portion. What, then, is the matter concerning the portions of you venerable elders? Do you know it?
Reveal something of your realization before this assembly to express the journey of your entire life and your study under spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).

To possess the *śakrāloka* eye and not be deceived by others—would that not be most wonderful? Is there anyone present? After a long silence, he said: "If no one comes forward, I shall go about buying and selling."

Master Chan Master Qin of Xichan was asked by a monk, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth?
The Master said, "All the stars in the heavens bow toward the North. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams? The Master said, "The great earth is level and smooth."
[A monk] asked, "What is the phrase of 'following the waves and riding the currents'? The Master said, "In spring they sprout; in summer they grow.
Juehua Chan Master was asked by a monk, "What is true suchness and nirvana? The Master said, "The sound of the autumn wind rustles;
the sound of the mountain stream flows with a murmur."
A monk asked Master Yanchang Shan: "Where have the ancient sages of old gone? The Master said: "They were not in the mountains;
they dwelt beneath the trees. The monk asked: "I wonder what they accomplished? The Master said: "Do you know where they ended up?
The monk was speechless. The Master then struck him.
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Zu, "What is the master’s pivot? The Master said, "Few people can step upon it.
The monk asked, "What happens when one suddenly steps upon it? The Master said, "Try stepping forward and see. The monk then gave a shout.
The Master then struck him.
Upāda Yunmen Lang had studied at lecture halls since his youth. He heard a monk ask Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?
Yunmen replied, "Hide your body within the Big Dipper. The Master could not fathom its subtle meaning, so he went to visit Yunmen. Yunmen—
As soon as he saw [the Master], he seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master hesitated; the Gatekeeper pushed the door open and recited this verse:
"Yunmen towers high, the white clouds hang low; The current is swift, the fish dare not dwell. Entering the gate, one already knows—yet has not yet seen.
Why labor to tread again upon the mud? Thereupon, the Master attained great enlightenment. A monk asked, "What is liberation? The Master...
He said: "Wearing boots while walking on water.
When Chan Master Zuanzishan asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? the Master said: "In the morning, look toward the southeast."
In the evening, he looked toward the northwest.
When Dali Heshang first visited Baiyun, Baiyun raised his fist and said, "Lately, I have not been like this.
The Master grasped the meaning and prostrated; from then on, he entered the inner quarters. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the West? The Master replied, "Torn straw."
Shoes. ○ Question: "What is the unconditioned (wuwei)? The Master then waved his hand. ○ Question: "When a donor makes an offering, how do you repay them?
The Master pinched his mustache with his hand and said, "If there is a mustache, one pinches it. What if there were no mustache?
The Master replied, "That is not within your realm."
When Master Baohua saw a monk passing down the steps from the Dharma Hall, he tapped his meditation seat.
The monk said, "If it is this, there is no need to bring it out. The Master was pleased; he descended from the platform to question him, but the monk remained silent. The Master then struck him.
When Chan Master Yuehua of Mount Yue first visited Baiyun, Baiyun asked, "What is your profession? He replied, "The *Peacock Sūtra*.
Baiyun said, "A fine young man from a good family, yet you follow after birds and insects. Upon hearing these words, the Master was struck with wonder and took him as his mentor.

After a long time, he attained realization of the fundamental principle. Subsequently, he resided at Mount Yuehua. There was once an elderly monk who ascended the Dharma Hall and paced back and forth from east to west.
Looking around, he said, "What a fine Dharma Hall! Yet, alas, it has no master. When Master [Shishuang] heard this, he summoned him and said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea.
Xiu asked, "If even the most ultimate within the profound is but the hair of a tortoise or the horns of a hare, and one does not cultivate within the two truths, how can there be secret application?
The Master said, "Settle yourself. Xiu said, "In that case, I shall break my staff and cut my straw sandals."
The Master said, "Examine this closely.
Leying Kuang asked a monk, "If you obtain the root, do not worry about the branches. What is the root? The Master said, "Do not ask others.
The monk asked, "What are the branches? The Master then held up his finger. Once, while they were working together on a communal task of repairing a fence, a monk...
Question: "The ancients opened various gates of expedient means; why, Master, do you instead block them off? The Master said: "Drive the stake in securely. Later, a monk asked Master Baiyun:
"The ancient zither has lost its sublime resonance; I beg the Master to play it for us. The Master said: "Though Boya was exquisite..."
[The Master] clapped his hands. At that time, those listening were few. [A monk] said, "If so, then we have met another Ziqi. The Master said, "Laughter breaks out and the startled strings snap;

Chan Master Wenshu Zhen [Verse]: A monk asked, “The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? The Master said, “The Yellow River has nine bends.
[Added by Chongshou] He was also asked, “What is the meaning of the ancients clapping their hands? The Master said, “A house with no minor servants cannot produce a gentleman.”
Chan Master Qín of Nántái [Verse]: A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "An inch of tortoise hair weighs seven catties."
Chan Master Deshan Yan was asked by a monk, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "The waters of Taoyuan encircle the White Cloud Pavilion. [He] ascended the hall and said: "When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth is fully contained within it.
Upon the tip of a single hair, the lion manifests its full body. Now tell me: when a single speck of dust arises and the entire earth is fully contained, how much does Mount Sumeru weigh? One...
The entire body of the Lion King atop the fur; how many drops are there in the waters of the great ocean?

If someone can say it, I will give you my staff and you may roam freely throughout the world. If you cannot say it, Mount Sumeru shall cover your head and the waters of the great ocean shall drown your body.
A monk asked Chan Master Qianming Pu: "The ancients did not permit the simultaneous cultivation of all practices. Is that which does not fall within the realm of merit and achievement permitted?
The Master said, "One. The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I beg the Master to point it out again. The Master said, "Thirty years hence."
A monk asked Chan Master Zhongliang Chong: "When the fishing line hangs a thousand feet down, with its intent fixed upon the deep pool, what then? The Master said:
"A red-scaled fish leaps upon the palm."
A monk asked Zen Master Huanglong Yuan, "Who is worthy to don Kāśyapa’s robe of supreme practice?
The Master said, "A patch of ground scorched by fire; when spring arrives, it meets with green once more."

Chan Master Puan Dao’s Verses on the Three Phrases: **Encompassing Heaven and Earth:** Heaven and earth, along with the myriad phenomena, The hells and the heavens— In every single thing there is true seeing;

It is also westward. Crimson clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun circles Mount Sumeru.

From the eastern hermitage, I constantly see the snow upon the western one; from the lower stream flows the water of the upper stream.
After the white clouds have dispersed at midnight, a single bright moon arrives before my bed.
A monk asked the Fifth Patriarch, Zen Master Jie, "What is the color-changing mani jewel? The Master said, "It follows. The monk asked, "And what happens after it has followed?
The Master said, "An old woman with two goiters. [Verse] Zhimen asked: "I do not ask about the passing of summer and the coming of winter;
what is the matter when we meet beneath the forest trees? The Master said, "Listen to the jade flute before the Five Phoenix Pavilion."
Lòu asked, "What can be done about the Main Peak being high and the Foreground Peak being low? The Master said, "Striking a golden bell atop the summit of Mount Sumeru.

The monk said, "I do not understand; what is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Looking at the mountains in the daytime.

Turtle hair grows an inch at every joint. If you wish to study Bodhi, Just look at these appearances. After a long silence, he said: "Do you know where this falls?"
There is none. If you do not know where it falls, look! Look! Bodhi has entered the Sangha hall. Long time standing. Ascending the hall: The spring cold is freezing;
last night there was fine snow. Do you see it? The great earth is covered in vast snow; the spring wind remains as cold as ever.
To speak of Chan or speak of the Way is easy; to become a Buddha or a Patriarch is difficult. Be careful. Showing [the assembly] due to an incident.
The Assembly: When the weather clears, we thatch the roofs; when the sky is dry, we reap the grain.

Linji’s 'shout upon entering the gate' could not avoid pressing the eyes until flowers appeared. Apart from these two paths, I wonder how Dongshan would have acted for people?"
The Master said: "It has been a long time since the weather cleared and it rained; recently, clouds have begun to rise. [The student] asked:

"If someone were to ask you about the fundamental principle of Dongshan's teaching in the future, how would you explain it to them? The Master said: "The vegetables in the garden are withered and parched; I am carrying water to sprinkle on the spinach."
Chan Master Shishuang Cheng asked a monk about an ancient saying: "Rolling up the curtain to face the bright day; shifting the chair to face the green mountains.
The monk asked, "What is 'rolling up the curtain to face the bright day'? The Master said, "Bring me the water pitcher. The monk asked, "What is 'shifting the chair to face the green mountains'?
The Master said, "Put it back in its original place. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Outside the mind there are no dharmas; outside dharmas there is no mind."
The mind follows conditions, vast and unconfined; do not hesitate any further. You all, as soon as you step onto the stairs, should turn back immediately.
What is the point of waiting for a second dose of foul water to be splashed upon you?
A monk asked Chan Master Ledu Tangcheng, "The one who sees is form; the one who hears is sound. Apart from these two paths, please, Master, speak otherwise.
The Master said, "An ancient temple with a new plaque on its eaves. One day, seeing a monk wearing his patched robe, the Master said:
[The monk] said, "I have such fine needlework. The Master said, "You only want it to be secure. The Master said, "Why do you 'beat the grass to startle the snake'?
[The monk] said, "When a guest arrives, one must see to them. The Master said, "There is only this; is there anything else? [The monk] said, "Clouds arise upon the mountain peaks.
The Master said, "Not yet. Speak further. [The monk] said, "Water drips before the cliff."
A monk asked Chan Master Yungai Yong, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The inscriptions on ancient temples are difficult to read.
The monk asked, "What is the intent of this? The Master said, "Those who read them all knit their brows."
Chan Master Shangfang Yue ascended the hall and said: "Gathering the yellow leaves, swirling the blue smoke; on the bamboo mat, one sleeps through the night in one's robes.
After the congee, the session is dismissed with three strikes of the drum—who could speak further of the Patriarch’s Chan? He then descended from his seat.

The Master said, "Before the Prajñā Terrace. [He] ascended the hall and said: "The thousand flowers vying to bloom and the hundred birds singing in spring—this is the phrase that points upward.
The Buddhas appearing in the world and the spiritual friends arising in compassion—this is the phrase that points downward. What, then, is [the phrase that points directly]?"
"A phrase that does not enter either of two paths. If you recognize it, the breath issues from the crown of your head; if you do not recognize it, it is like a clay ox plowing a stony field.
[The Master] struck the meditation seat and descended from his position.
A monk asked Master Xincan of Jinshan, “The Buddha said, ‘I have a great affliction: it is because I have this body. Before my parents were born, I do not know where this body was.
The Master said, “Throughout vast kalpas, it has had no location; if one discusses birth and extinction, it becomes entirely non-existent.
The monk said, “If that is so, then the mind that pervades the ten directions does not reside in any place. The Master said, “Mud... [The text here is incomplete].
Shaking the Stake from Within. ○ Ascending the Hall: That which is prized in the world is the Beryl of Huai-zhi and the Pearl of Lord Sui;
Jinshan calls these "donkey dung and horse manure. That which is prized beyond the world is True Suchness, Liberation, Bodhi, and Nirvana;
Jinshan calls these "boiling pork and clanging bowls. But tell me, speaking in such a manner—where does it land?
Therefore, this is not a mind of acceptance and rejection, nor is it a heavy reliance on heterodox and deluded views. Do all people know?
A fierce tiger pays no heed to meat upon a table; how could a roaring furnace cast a needle from within a bag?

Chan Master Xuedou Chongxian Mingjue took up the sutras at the lecture hall, investigating principles and exhausting the profound mysteries. His interrogations were as swift as charging blades, and his eloquence was peerless;
all recognized him as a vessel of the Dharma, and everyone pointed him toward a journey to the South. He first visited Zhimen, where he immediately posed this question:

He did not give rise to a single thought. "How could there be any fault? Master Men summoned the teacher to come forward. As soon as the teacher drew near, Men struck him over the mouth with his whisk.
When the teacher was about to open his mouth, Men struck him again. The teacher attained sudden enlightenment and subsequently went to reside at Cuifeng.
Later, he moved to Xuedou. On the day he ascended the hall, a monk asked, "The great Dharma conch is blown and the great Dharma drum is struck;
with the imperial ministers present at the assembly, what is this? The Master said, "The pure breeze has not ceased its coming. The monk said, "In that case, I have met the Master.
The Master said, "Once a word has been spoken, even four horses cannot overtake it. The monk bowed, and the Master said, "I let you off by one move."
He then surveyed the great assembly and said: "The humans and devas are gathered here in such numbers; what matter should we together clarify?

How can one take the transmission of the school (zongcheng) to consist merely of alternating roles of guest and host, or the mere pursuit of questions and answers? The vast style of our tradition possesses sovereign majesty and power."
Its brilliance transcends both past and present; it holds fast to heaven and earth. The thousand sages have said only that it must be known by oneself; the five vehicles are unable to establish it.

Thus, though one may awaken before sound, the ultimate meaning remains obscure at the moment of looking into a mirror; though one may know the source beneath words, one still lacks clarity regarding what lies beyond the realm of consciousness and emotion.
If you all wish to know the true manifestation, simply let there be no grasping or yearning above, and cut off the self below.
In person, the natural, eternal radiance manifests before you; each and every one stands solitary like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.

Can you discern this clearly or not? If you have not yet discerned it, discern it! If you have not yet clarified it, clarify it! Once you have discerned and clarified it, you will be able to cut off the stream of birth and death and occupy the same seat as the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
This moment of wondrous, perfect, and transcendent awakening is precisely when you can repay the unrepayable debt of gratitude and assist in the Unconditioned Way.
Transformation. Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is Vimalakīrti’s single silence? The Master said, "Hanshan visits Shiqi.
[The monk] said, "In that case, one enters the gate of non-duality. The Master sighed once. He then added, "Where has the Great Being Vimalakīrti gone?
For a thousand ages, he leaves people gazing on him without end. Do not ask further about the gate of non-duality; last night there was a bright moon."
Ascending to the solitary peak. ○ Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure.

Within this vast and silent world of heaven and earth, standing alone, what can one gaze upon to the end? He then descended from his seat and looked back at his attendant, saying: "Just now, was there anyone looking at the abbot’s quarters?
The attendant replied: "There was. The Master said: "The heart of a thief is always fearful. ○ Ascending the hall, he addressed the assembly: "This single expanse..."
"The fields have been assigned to you for a long time now, yet you all still do not recognize their four boundaries.
If you want the tree in the center, I do not begrudge it. [Verse] A monk asked, "What is the source of all Buddhas?
The Master said, "The cold colors of a thousand peaks. The monk asked, "I do not know for certain: is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "Raindrops on mountain flowers."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The ten directions have no walls, and the four sides have no gates. Where did the ancients go to see their guests?
If you can utter a 'hand-taking' phrase, I grant you dominion over all under heaven. [Verse] Addressing the assembly, he said:

"A sword from Longquan and an axe share the same substance, yet their sharpness and dullness differ vastly. A common hack and a thoroughbred gallop on the same path, yet their speed and slowness are distinct."
[Added to the Collection]. [Verse] A monk asked: "The mountain flowers bloom like brocade; the stream water is as deep blue as indigo.
Why is it that within the student's own sphere, one does not understand? The Master said: "Staring with eyes wide open inside a withered tree. The monk said:

"In that case, one discerns the field from the sprouts, and recognizes the person through their words. The Master said: "Thirty blows! Wait for another time. [Added to the Collection]. [Verse] A monk asked: "How is it..."
The Master of this Buddha said: "Surrounded on four sides by mountains.
[Added by Zeng] Chan Master Yungai Peng first visited Chan Master Shuangquan Ya. Shuangquan appointed him as his attendant and presented him with the koan of the *bājiāo* (plantain) staff.
For a long time, he failed to gain realization. One day, while Shuangquan was tending the fire, the Master stood in attendance beside him. Shuangquan—

Suddenly he asked, "Try bringing up the story of the *zhuzhangzi* (the staff). Let us deliberate upon it together. As the Master was about to bring it up, Baofu Quanshu picked up his fire tongs and shook them.
At that moment, the Master attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He ascended the hall and said: "Height is not found at the summit; wealth is not found at Fuyan."
"Happiness does not reside in heaven; suffering does not reside in hell. After a long silence, he said: "Friends fill the world, but how many can truly know one's heart?
Chan Master Zhangfasi was asked by a monk, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied, "How many people have groped for it?"
Suo Bu-zhu said, "If you suddenly reach it, what then? The Master said, "What could be done with that?

Chan Master Bei-chen Xian [Verse]: A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "It cannot be lifted by a spoon. [Verse]: On the night of the year’s end, he gave a small *chan* (sermon), saying:
"The year is exhausted and the age is spent; there is nothing with which to share the year-end with you all. This old monk shall roast one..."
In an open space, there is a white ox. They cook millet rice, boil wild vegetable soup, and burn firewood. After everyone has eaten, they perform the Village Music (Murata Raku).
Why? To avoid leaning on others’ doorways or huddling by others’ walls; otherwise, one would inevitably be called a "lord" by the people of the age.
Having said this, he descended from his seat and returned to the Abbot’s quarters. When night had deepened, the Rector entered the quarters to pay his respects and said, “The District Magistrate...”
A public official was inside. When he arrived, the Master said, "What are you doing? He replied, "I heard that the Master slaughters oxen but does not accept their hides and horns.
The Master then took his hat, threw it to the ground, and the man picked it up.
The Master leaped down from his meditation seat, grabbed him by the chest, and shouted, "Thief! Thief! The man then placed the hat over the Master's head and said, "Heaven!"
"Han, you may go back," the Master said, laughing heartily. He then went out. At that time, Fachang was serving as attendant.
The Master looked at Chang and asked, "How do you resolve this koan? Chang replied, "Paper is expensive in Tanzhou; one statement covers it all."
The monk asked, "Venerable Ribang, what is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth? The Master held up his staff. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams?
The Master held the staff horizontally across him. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current?
The Master threw the staff down. The monk said, "Beyond these three phrases, I beg the Master to speak. The Master then rose.
Go! The Master praised the portrait of Kaifu Zhen, saying: "His pure demeanor is slender; it may be gazed upon and admired, yet though one admires it, it is not the person himself.

His marvelous brushwork has depicted him; it may be compared to and imitated, yet though one images him, it is not the true reality. Neither the person nor the true reality—like the full autumn moon in its perfect orb."

Some say there is no flavor; others say the past is as if present before one’s eyes. Seeking it, seeking it—manifestation and concealment strike at the opportune moment, a hair’s breadth of discrepancy.
When the golden sun is at its zenith, the swift wind and thunderbolt crash down.
Chan Master Kaixian Xian was pure and austere in his conduct. Having traveled extensively among the seats of various masters, he made enlightenment his sole ambition.

He went to visit Deshan, who, while presiding over the assembly from the high seat, looked out at the crowd and said, "The lion yawns; the elephant king turns back to look. Suddenly, the Master attained realization.
Entering the room, he presented his understanding. Deshan asked, "How do you understand this? The Master turned around and said, "The back garden."
The donkey ate the grass; the mountain burned it. Later, he arrived at Xuedou. Xuedou spoke with him and was delighted by his transcendent brilliance.
He dubbed him "The Monk Xian Who Roams Freely Across the Sea" and subsequently appointed him to share the teaching seat, whereupon eminent monks from the four quarters came to revere him.
On another day, Xuedou proposed that the Master take up residence at Jinge. Upon hearing this, the Master secretly wrote two verses on the wall and departed, saying: "It is not that there is no..."

In spirit, he continues the ancestral lamp; in his realization, he feels ashamed that he has not yet attained the level of Neng of Lingnan. Beneath the moon at the third watch, he departs from the mountain cave;
full of lingering affection, he remains silent as he gazes upon the azure peaks. For over twenty years amidst the four seas, he has never ceased seeking masters and choosing friends.

This morning, having reached the ground of no-mind, he was instead driven out of the mountains by that very state of no-mind. In his later years, the requests from the assembly became increasingly frequent, whereupon he...
Opening the Dharma first to satisfy the aspirations of both monastics and laypeople.

Chan Master Qin of Zisheng Monastery in Xiuzhou ascended the hall and said: "Awakening through many lifetimes is not the work of the patched robe; that single point of clarity does not depend on a lamp.
He held up his staff and said: "The Patriarch is upon the tip of this staff; Maitreya is beneath the feet of the lantern. You must...
I do not ask about the waist-drum of Mount Mi; how is it that you are a distinct point?
If you can speak, then boundless lands and realms are all upon your eyebrows. If you cannot speak, how will you cross the Rakshasa Bridge?
After a long silence, he said: "The waters flow in a thousand streams, the moon; the mountains lock in a single valley cloud. He then struck his staff.
Descend from the seat.
Chan Master Gui of Lüyuan in Tanzhou ascends the hall and says: "Whenever there is a causal occasion, one must understand its fundamental principle (*zong*).

If one understands its fundamental principle, there is neither 'is' nor 'is not. In its functioning, it surges like billowing waves and boils like a seething sea, operating entirely through the movement of the true essence. As for that essence..."
The mirror is clear; as water sinks and rises, it accords with conditions and returns to stillness. Now tell me: how many people are there in the Tuṣita Heaven palace? How many are seated?
If you can distinguish the black from the white here, I grant you all your freedom to go east, west, south, and north, like clouds or cranes.
If you do not understand this, you will never reach the end of your days trudging in straw sandals. *Chan*.
Chan Master Yunju Xiaoshun (styled Laofu): In his youth, he was coarse and impetuous, but suddenly awakened to the nature of floating illusions.

He entered the monastic life under a teacher and cultivated minute details of conduct. [Verse] He went to visit Dongshan. One day, while begging for alms in Wuchang, he first visited the home of Layman Liu Gong.
The Layman was held in high esteem by the public for his noble conduct; whatever he intended to grant or take away, none failed to comply with him. At that time, the Master’s age was...
[The Master] was young and, not knowing [the monk’s] extensive training, treated him with some levity. The scholar said, "Old man, I have a question.

If our minds accord, you shall open the commentary; if they do not accord, I ask that you return to the mountain. He then asked, "How is it when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master replied:
"Black as lacquer. [The scholar] asked, "What is it like after being polished? The Master said, "It illuminates heaven and earth.

The scholar gave a long bow and said, "Please return to your mountain, Venerable Sir," then he brushed his sleeves and entered his residence. The Master was crestfallen and immediately returned to Dongshan.

Dongshan asked him the reason for this. The Master recounted the incident in detail. Dongshan said, "If you had asked me, I would have told you. The Master posed the previous question again. Dongshan said, "This..."
Not far from Hanyang, Master Jin spoke these words later. The Master said, "Before the Yellow Crane Tower, at the Yingwu Isle.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment; his sharp spiritual edge was unassailable. He ascended the hall and, citing Jia Shan, said: "At the gate of the bustling marketplace..."

"Recognize the celestial son! Grasp the old monk at the tip of every blade of grass! Yunju did not do so; rather, the wife rocked the loom with a *zha-zha* sound, while the child made "guo-guo" noises with his mouth.

Ascending the hall, he said: "In other places, there are those who play with the heads of snakes, stroke the tails of tigers, leap across the great ocean, or hide their bodies within the edge of a sword.
Here at Yunju, we wash our feet with hot water on a cold day, and take off our clothes at night."
He would put on his socks and go to sleep. At dawn, while he was putting on his travel trousers, the wind blew down the fence. He called for laborers to split bamboo and tie it back up.
Chan Master Qisong of Furi Temple in Hangzhou received the Dharma from Dongshan.

Every night, the Master would wear an image of Avalokiteśvara upon his head and recite her name until he had completed one hundred thousand times before retiring to bed; this became his constant practice. From that time on, regarding worldly scriptures and books...

Without formal study, he was able to compose the *Yuanjiao lun* (Treatise on the Origin of the Teachings) in over one hundred thousand words, clarifying that the Way of Confucianism and Buddhism is a single, unified thread, thereby refuting the arguments of those who followed the traditions of Cheng, Zhu, Han, and others who sought to exclude Buddhism. Those who read it were awed and submissive. Later, he resided at the Yong’an Aranya.

He composed the *Diagram of the Patriarchs of the Chan Gate*, the *Record of the Orthodox Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma*, and the *Supplementary Collection of Teachings*, which he presented to Emperor Renzong.

Upon reading them, the Emperor sighed with admiration and ordered the Bureau of the Propagation of the Law (*Chuandefa Yuan*) to compile them for inclusion in the Tripitaka. An imperial edict was issued to honor him, bestowing upon him the title "Enlightened Teaching" (*Mingjiao*).
Both the Chancellor Han Qi and the Grand Councilor Ouyang Xiu received him with courtesy and treated him with great respect. Subsequently, he returned to the East.
On the fourth day of the sixth month in the fourth year of the Xīníng era, he rose at dawn and wrote a verse, saying: "The moon is bright in the late night; today I joyfully walk alone.
I shall not follow the old man of Dàméi, greedily chasing the cries of the flying squirrel. He passed away at midnight. Among his remains after cremation, five items remained indestructible:
the crown of his head, his ears, his tongue, his *kumārabhūta* (youthful) body, and his prayer beads. From the bone of his crown, light emerged.
The śarīra were crimson-white and crystalline pure; both monastics and laypeople joined together to preserve them from decay and interred them to the left of his former residence at Yong’an.
Later, while residing at Beijian of Jingci Monastery, Ju Jian composed a "Praise of the Five Kinds of Unchanging [Śarīra].
The Master’s collected works comprise twenty fascicles, titled *Xinjin*, which circulated widely throughout the world.
Xu Shi, the Governor of Hongzhou, visited Dongshan and attained the Eye of the True Dharma. One day, while sitting with Letan Cheng and Shanglan Pu, Cheng asked:
"I have heard the Langzhong say: 'Sitting through the night upon the Cloud-Linked Rock; planting pines in the rain during spring.'"
"What did you say to Dongshan at that time? The Master said, "The office has been dismissed early today.
Tanzu asked, "I heard you replied, 'The Great Sage of Sizhou appears in Yangzhou'—is this true? The Master said, "Serve another cup of tea. Tanzu said, "His reputation is not in vain.
The Master said, "When will you return to the mountain, Monk? Tanzu said, "Today I was seen through by Shanglan."
Lan then shouted. Dan said, "It must be you who can do it. Gong replied, "I cannot help the boat; I shall break the scoop.
Chan Master Liang of Yuyuan left home at the age of seven and received the tonsure at nine. He was devoted to the study of the Way, never neglecting his practice even while sleeping or eating.
One day, while washing his face, he splashed water on the ground and experienced a slight awakening. Immediately, he yearned for a teacher to seek out, traveling far to visit Le... (Lengshui).
He attended the Dharma seat of Master Tan, serving him for over ten years until he received the seal of approval (*inka*) upon realizing the pivotal point of the teaching.

He then traveled to Mount Lu, where he served as the *jishi* (record-keeper) under Chan Master Netu of Yuan Tong. During the Huangyou era, Emperor Renzong issued an imperial decree appointing him to head Jingyin Chan Monastery.

He was summoned to the Huacheng Hall for an audience, where the Emperor questioned him on the general meaning of the Buddha-dharma. His responses pleased the Emperor, who bestowed upon him the title Chan Master Da Jue.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The great sun rises in the east, piercing through the darkness of the great chiliocosm.

If you all stand within the light, you are still merely shadows and echoes chasing one another. If you stand within the darkness, you are likewise a fellow who hides his head while exposing his shadow.
At this point, how can one express it? After a long silence, he said: "When meeting people, speak only three parts; do not yet cast yourself entirely out."
A single mind. *Chen*. ○ Ascending the hall: Within the worldly dharmas, how many people have been deluded? Within the Buddha-dharma, how many people have been intoxicated?
As for being neither deluded nor intoxicated—of what kind of person is this the affair? ○ Ascending the hall:

As soon as the tip of the verbal spear is raised, the ocean of meaning becomes profoundly deep. If you would take the direct shortcut, each of you please return to your quarters. ○ Ascending the hall.
In the Hall, [the Master] manifested his form in response to conditions like the moon in water. He then picked up his staff and said, "This is not an object;
it manifests its form right now. He asked, "Tell me, where is the moon? After a long silence, he said, "The open sky has a path that must be penetrated;
the bottom of the pond leaves no trace, so there is no need to seek it. He struck the incense altar and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Shengtian Jian ascended the hall and said: "The realm of Vairocana is the profound gateway of myriad wonders;

it is inexhaustible when explained by those with knowledge, and its depths cannot be fathomed even as Sudhana draws from them. Manjushri embodies it in silent stillness, while Samantabhadra realizes it in manifold layers.
If one follows its true nature, it is like clouds vanishing from the azure sky—originally there was never a single thing."
Things, if they follow their own intellectual functioning, are like flowers blooming in a spring valley—their application is boundless.

Though it is said that [the Buddhas] pervade as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, they all equally follow this One Way. Now I ask you all: what is this One Way? After a long silence, he said:
"Where the white clouds break, one sees the bright moon; when the yellow leaves fall, one hears the sound of pounding clothes. Study!
Chan Master Jiufeng Shao ascended the hall and said: "When I speak of Chan, it is like a cricket spitting oil;
it comes out as soon as one squeezes it. If one does not squeeze it, there is not a single drop. Why is this?

It is simply because you have never studied the causes and conditions of the ancients or prepared yourself in advance with superior insights and knowledge, so that upon ascending the hall, you merely grind your lips and stroke your beak, [like crickets] waiting for the dawn."
The smell of the rice steamed all those present. Every question and answer was truly unavoidable; how could it be otherwise?

It is not as if I alone am like the Tathāgata Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū, who sat in silence for ten kalpas without opening his mouth, only beginning to speak after being repeatedly entreated by the devas, the Brahma kings, and the sixteen princes. It is certainly not that I am begrudging or withholding anything.
It is simply because I dare not let you all go to waste. Since I, this mountain monk, do not let you go to waste, you must not say that I understand ascending the seat for formal discourse.
When Chan Master Shu of Xita entered the hall:
"On the platform of Huangmei, those present were as numerous as hemp seeds; within their phrases, they presented their vital functions. This matter is indeed [worthy of consideration].
"Alas! Truly, there has been nothing from the very beginning. 'The blue sky and bright day are obscured by clouds'—this is the koan.
Master Yiyu Yi ascended the hall and said: "As soon as Mazu entered the hall, Xiongpeng immediately rolled up his mat.
A gust of spring wind arrives, and flowers lie scattered across the ground. He then descended from the seat.

He sent the head seat Tao to study for a long time under Letan. Letan asked him, "The Patriarch came from the West to transmit the mind alone and point directly at the human mind, so that one may see one's nature and become a Buddha.
How do you understand this? The Master said, "I do not understand. Letan said:
"Before you left home to become a monk, what were you doing? the Master said, "I was herding oxen. Duan asked, "How did you herd them?
The Master replied, "In the early morning I rode them out; in the evening I rode them back. Duan said, "You truly do not understand well.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and immediately composed a verse, saying: "I cast off the ox-ropes and left the home-life; I shaved my beard and hair and donned the robes."
Kāṣāya. Someone asked me about the meaning of my coming from the West; I held my staff across my shoulder and sang "La-li-la.
Chan Master Chenghao of Yuyuan visited Beita, where he realized the essential point of the mind and attained the samādhi of great mastery.
He fashioned a loincloth and inscribed upon it the names of the patriarchs of successive generations, saying: "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are but a trifle compared to this. Furthermore—

He wrote [the characters] upon his sash; thus, the monastic communities referred to him as "Hao the White Linen Pants. During the Yuanfeng era, while presiding over the assembly at Guyin, a monk from his hometown also attempted to imitate this.
Upon seeing him, the Master rebuked him, saying: "What principles do you possess that you dare to treat this as a mere joke?
It will lead to nothing but vomiting blood—nothing can be done about it. Shortly thereafter, at Lumen, the monk passed away exactly as the Master had predicted. [Verse] Shown on the Winter Solstice.
The assembly said: "As the course of the sun shifts and passes, my coarse cloth trousers are bright red. Do not wonder why they are unwashed; there has been no one to come and change them.
Self-praise: "When the rice gruel is thin, I sit; when the bed is narrow, I lie down first. My ears are deaf, so I love loud voices; my eyes are dim, so large characters are suitable for me."
Chan Master Yunju Qing was asked by a monk, "What is the phrase that encompasses heaven and earth?

The Master said, "It fits. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that follows the waves and drifts with the current? The Master said, "Broad. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that cuts off all streams?

The Master said, "Narrow. [He] ascended the hall for formal instruction: "The Way is fundamentally non-action; phenomena are neither extended nor compressed. A single thought-moment is ten thousand years; ten thousand ages exist within it."
The moon is white and the wind is calm; the mountains are green and the waters are blue. Every dharma manifests before us; every thing is complete.

The meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings are neither straight nor crooked. To truly know the price of rice in Luling, one must realize that the wheat has ripened before the mountain.
