An eighty-year-old widow does not speak of remarriage.
Dharma Cloud Weibai Fuguo Chan Master ascended the hall and said: "The past is already past; as for the future, do not calculate it."
It concerns the very events of the present moment. This morning, on the fifteenth day of the first month, the bright moon is perfectly full. Let us beat the drum and invite everyone to look.
"Great assembly, there is no doubt that you can look, but what do you call this when it has finished? Do not seek it in the heavens; do not search for it in the water.
The Master’s *Continued Lamp Record* (Xu deng lu) consists of thirty fascicles and was included in the Imperial Canon.
A monk asked Master Xianyan Chun, "Deshan had the staff; Linji had the shout. How do you, Reverend, apply them?
The Master said, "I am tired today. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "It is actually you who are alert."
Chan Master Ciji Cong ascended the hall and said: "Throughout the day, we are diligent and strive for one another, much like trying to lead an ox up a wall.
Great assembly, why is this so? We greedily pursue life, busily hurrying from day to day; when called back, we do not turn our heads—what can be done?"
Chan Master Baimiao Gui ascended the hall and said: "Fortunately we have met this auspicious occasion; you must gather rare insights.
Since you have encountered this mountain of jewels, do not leave empty-handed. Do not wait for some other time or day to speak grand words behind the door or in the corner of the wall."
It pervades heaven and earth and spans all time and antiquity; it is simply the one self-nature of each person within this very midst, wherein there is nothing else whatsoever.
All of you, every day when walking, walk upon it; when lying down, lie upon it; when sitting, sit upon it;

when responding in speech, speak with your full mouth upon it; even up to raising an eyebrow, winking an eye, feeling anger or joy, love or hate, or remaining in silent stillness—you move through it all.
Playfulness has never ceased from the very beginning. For what reason do you refuse to accept this and instead seek rest within yourself?

It is simply because, since immeasurable kalpas past, the weight of your passionate desires has been heavy and the path of birth and death has been long; you have turned your back on awakening and joined with the dust of the world, giving rise to doubts within yourself.
It is like a bird flying in the sky, unaware that the sky is its home, or a fish swimming in the water, forgetting that water is its very life.
How can you suppress yourself and instead ask others? This is much like holding a bowl of rice and claiming hunger, or standing by a river and crying out for thirst.
If you all wish to attain rest, each of you must stand firm on this very spot and settle your spirit. With a single thought, turn the light back within; suddenly, you will illuminate yourself.
How is this different from the red sun in the sky, moving alone without partiality, or the bright pearl in a dish, turning of itself without being nudged? Thus it is.
Although it is thus, this is only for those of initial capacity; they have never yet stepped upon the mechanism that lies above.
But tell me, what is this mechanism that lies above? After a long silence, he said: "Looking up at the sky, one does not see the sky."
Chan Master Fuyan Chuan ascended the hall and said: "The characteristic of nature is a single expanse of clear sky; the nature of characteristics is a thousand waves rising in competition.
If you penetrate the source, the clear stream flows without obstruction. Thus, by raising a single thought, the dharma-gates as numerous as motes of dust and grains of sand are suddenly revealed;
by picking up a single hair, the realms of boundless lands are simultaneously manifested. Now tell me, where are Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra?"
"What place is it where one does not run downhill? A swift opportunity is hard to encounter. Having said this, he descended from his seat.
Master Deshan Renhui addressed the assembly: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination. Simply do not harbor hatred or attachment, and all will be transparently clear.
I, however, am not like this: the Ultimate Way is most difficult; it requires discrimination. If there were no hatred..."
Affection. Strive to see it clearly.
Chan Master Xiangji Min ascended the hall and said: "The wooden horse breaks through the path of a thousand riders; the iron ox penetrates ten thousand layers of barriers.
Where are the wooden horse and the iron ox? After a long pause, he said: "Startling the wild geese on the sands at twilight in the sky. The sea...
Two or three paces from the gate, Chan Master Laixiang ascended the hall.
Looking over the assembly, he said: "As a patriarch of our school, one must take up the guiding thread wherever one is.

In responding to questions and providing answers, one must wield the power of killing and giving life according to the moment; the mind’s eye must be sharp and clear, leaving no room for demons. If you seek [enlightenment] through the staff..."
To certify [this] by shouting "Ho! and then taking it upon oneself is to bury the ancestral style. To feel shame for what others have already done is to turn away from the single path.
There is no room for hesitation; when a single breath does not return, one is still but a dead man. O Great Assembly, even if you reach such a state, it is still merely words buried in concealment;
you have not yet found the path of total penetration. I dare ask you all: what is this path of penetration?
"Is there anyone who can speak of this path? If not, I, this mountain monk, cannot help but explain it for you. After a long silence, he said:
"The jade leaves Jingchu, its cold light stirring; the sword emerges from Fengcheng, its purple qi sweeping across."
Chan Master Zhikong ascended the hall. "The mirror of the mind is bright; its reflection is unimpeded.
He then picked up his staff and said, "To call this 'staff' is an obstruction; not to call it 'staff' is also an obstruction. Apart from these two..."
Ultimately, how is it? Do you wish to understand? Is there obstruction or not? Who is there to oppose it? The great earth, mountains, and rivers are utterly pulverized.
Zen Master Huayan Zhiming ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, in the heavens, the myriad phenomena are arrayed in equal alignment."
Manifesting in the earth, it brings forth the four seasons; in humans, it appears and disappears, contracting and expanding, such that the six sense-faculties function interchangeably.
But tell me, how does it manifest upon the tip of this mountain monk’s staff? After a long silence, he struck once and said:
Whether high or low, it reaches everywhere.

Chan Master Yongtai Hang ascended the hall and said: "The dragon soars through the azure heavens, its transformations beyond measure; the phoenix flies through the blue sky—whom can its traces be known?
When it may go, it goes, never departing from the hundreds of thousands of samādhis; when it may stop, it stops, how could it ever forget the myriad [dharmas]?"
The elephant encompasses the myriad phenomena. Therefore it is said: "It cannot be grasped; it cannot be relinquished; within that which is unobtainable, one simply attains it.
But tell me, what is it that is attained? After a long silence, he said: "Do not engage in false conceptualization."
A monk asked Chan Master Shousheng Bang, "Setting aside both the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings, how can one quickly attain Buddhahood?
The Master said, "That which is 'accomplished' is ultimately not so; that which is 'Buddha' is likewise not real. As the monk hesitated, the Master rebuked him, saying: "Ha!"
"What is the meaning of the head-phrase?

Chan Master Ze of Changlu addressed the assembly in the Dharma hall: "Beyond the tower, the colors of Purple Gold Mountain are exquisite; before the gate, the sound of the Dew of Immortality water is cold.
Beneath the shade of the ancient locust tree, amidst the clear breeze—let me point this out once more for you all. He held up his staff and said, "Do you see?"
"Do you see? He struck the incense table and said, "Do you hear? He leaned his staff against it and said, "If the eyes and ears are unobstructed, one is sufficient wherever one is;
the sounds of water and the colors of mountains flow on of their own accord."
Chan Master Linji of Jia Shan ascended the hall. After a long silence, he drew a perfect circle and said, "The five thousand-plus scrolls cannot fully explain it;
the Buddhas of the three periods have not praised it enough. This makes one recall the oil-selling old man.
He hurriedly stepped down from the rope-platform and stood there. "Investigate!"
Chan Master Yuanfeng Man ascended the hall and said: "This is a matter of the sword’s edge; it requires one who is a man of the sword’s edge to accomplish it.

There are certain seekers of fame and profit who act as teachers for gods and humans, hanging up the head of a sheep while selling dog meat, thereby corrupting those who have recently entered the path."
"The Great Canon of the former sages has been extinguished! You people, hearing such news—does it not make your hearts tremble with cold?
Thus, by misleading sentient beings, you shall fall into the Avīci Hell. Alas, alas! To seek a moment’s pleasure, you incur ten thousand kalpas of lingering calamity.
What desperate urgency drives you to become a disciple of the Śākya? He shouted, "Deaf people merely strain their ears! and then descended from his seat.
Chan Master Shansheng ascended the hall. To raise the sound is to seek to stop the echo, yet one does not realize that sound is the root of the echo.

To play with the shadow to escape the form, yet one does not realize that the form is the source of the shadow. To inquire about the Dharma by means of the Dharma, yet one does not realize that the Dharma is fundamentally not-Dharma.

To transmit the mind by means of the mind, yet one does not realize that the mind is fundamentally no-mind. When the mind is fundamentally no-mind, one knows the mind is like an illusion; when one realizes the Dharma is non-Dharma, one knows [the truth].
Dharmas are like dreams; the mental phenomena are not real. Do not pursue them in vain. They are like dreams, illusions, and empty flowers—what need is there to grasp at them?

When you reach this point, the Buddhas of the three periods, the entire Great Canon, the words of the patriarchs, and the "entanglements" spread by the old monks throughout the land—all these will fail to apply.
Why? Because "peace itself was brought about by the generals, yet we do not permit the generals [to enjoy it]."
Seeing Great Peace.

Chan Master Zhan of Zhao-ti (a native of Jiahe) in the Western Capital ascended the hall and said: "Neither biased nor unbiased, neither correct nor incorrect—this matter has from of old been difficult to compare.
With wind and rain filling the heavens, one’s very bones and hair stand cold. What need is there to further enter the nāga-samādhi? He struck the meditation staff.

[The Master] lowered his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "The six sense-objects are not evil; they are identical to perfect enlightenment. On horseback, who is this fair-faced youth?
Piercing through flowers and breaking willows, the corner of his kerchief hangs down. Last night, he was drunk at the Bright Moon Tower; calling for dice, he lost his golden mansion.
Whether he returns with falcon on arm and hound in hand, or whether the lady with the arched brows and white teeth is too powerless to be angry—can this mind truly [be grasped]?"
"How many people know? Yellow heads and blue eyes are not acquaintances. *Lara-lari!*" (He claps his hands once and descends from the seat.
Chan Master Chuming of Jingci ascended the hall for discourse: "When you go out the door, you see mountains and rivers; when you enter the gate, you see the Buddha hall.
The numinous light penetrates everywhere—why do you all fail to realize this? If you do not realize it, Jingci will have no recourse today. [End of section] *Shang* (Ascending).
The Hall. If one discusses this matter, it is like spreading out precious gems and piling up jade and gold in disarray. Those who obscure their own nature willingly endure poverty and distress;
those with eyes, however, simply pick them up as they come to hand. Thus it is said: "In Jambudvīpa there is a great treasure, yet those who see it are few, and those who obtain it are even rarer.
If someone were to offer it to me, I would become a Buddha in a single moment. Then, picking up his staff, he said: "Now, all at once—"
Presented for your consideration. Summoning the assembly, he said, "Keep your eyes wide open! He then threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Xuefeng Sihui addressed the assembly in the Dharma hall: "The Great Way is right before your eyes, yet it is difficult to behold even there."
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, this very morning on the fifteenth day of the third month, do not trouble yourself by standing for long. [Ascending the hall:
All dharmas are without difference. Yunmen’s “moldy steamed buns” and Zhaozhou’s “tea. Blowing a jade flute from atop the Yellow Crane Tower—“In the fifth month, plum blossoms fall in the river city.
I am ashamed before Elder Fu of Taiyuan, who heard the drums and horns at the fifth watch and played [his lute] as dawn broke.

Lute. (He lets out a shout. Ascending the hall: All you friends who have traveled south in search of the Way, you have worn through your straw sandals. You claim to have transcended study and dwell in non-action, sitting idly away the days and months.
Yet ordinary emotions are easy to cast off, while saintly understandings are difficult to forget. If there is even the slightest trace remaining, it all becomes a leakage.

One may practice the Way within this very state. It is like the earth supporting a mountain; responding to things by manifesting forms is like a donkey looking down a well—altogether free from calculation.
The path has already been established, yet if one discusses "correspondence," it becomes further removed from the actual encounter. I urge you, worthy ones: do not apply your minds in error.
Each person returned to their hall; what further matter was there to seek?
Master Ming of Zifu ascended the hall and said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like cutting down a tree by reaching its root, or treating an illness by finding the correct acupuncture point.
If one has reached the root, why labor over hacking away at a thousand branches? If one has found the point, there is no need for six partial treatments."
He struck the ground with his staff once and said, "This is the root; which one is the hole? He threw down the staff and said, "This is the hole;
what then do you call the root? He shouted, "Tsk! What kind of talk is this?"
Chan Master Yunfeng Xuan ascended the hall and said: "Rest! Cease! A single thought for ten thousand years!
Cold ashes and withered wood! An incense burner in an ancient temple! A single length of white silk! "Great assembly, the insight of the ancients was like the sun shining across the sky;
they did not cling to the two extremes, so how could they fall into the realms of darkness? Alas, the descendants of later generations mostly dwell on the side of 'one color'."
I understand. But I, this mountain monk, am not like that. I do not cease; I do not rest. My karmic consciousness wanders aimlessly;
I stumble and fall in all directions. I sit and sleep amidst clamor at the crossroads, in the midst of sounds and forms; I dwell in the villages of three families.

The streets are overflowing and the roads are blocked; they go about playing amidst thorns and brambles. On mountains of knives and trees of swords, their bellies are split open and their hearts gouged out;
in boiling cauldrons and glowing furnaces, their skin is pierced through and their bones are rotted away. To sing such a song is very much like a three-year-old child rolling a brocade ball.
Ascending the hall: Lean bamboos and tall pines drip with emerald fragrance; Gentle breezes and sparse moonlight pass through the heat and cold.
I know not who dwells in the temple west of the plain; Each day, the sound of the bell escorts the setting sun. Ascending the hall: A monk asked, “What is the meaning of the West?
The Master said, “It strikes the forehead; it bumps the nose. The monk asked, “What is the intent behind this? The Master said, “A donkey carrying a load.”
Lücai asked, "Is there anything further above this? The Master said, "Arriving in the Western Heaven in the morning, returning to the Eastern Land in the evening.

Lücai said, "I thank the Master for his response. The Master said, "The Great Vehicle is being worn out by you, Langdang. The monk withdrew. The Master then said, "When a monk asks about the meaning of the Westward Journey, he strikes his forehead and bumps his nose.
What is the underlying intent? It is like a donkey carrying [the load] and Lücai riding the horse. Arriving in the morning..."
"Reaching the Western Heaven at dusk, returning to Tang at dawn; the Mahāyāna is just like a polished, clumsy thing. Why?

Because a person of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words. Thereupon, he clapped his hands, laughed loudly, and descended from the seat. A monk asked, "Dana burned the wooden Buddha."
The head monk asked, "Why did your eyebrows and beard fall out? The Master said, "One person spreads a falsehood; ten thousand people spread a truth.
The monk said, "If that is so, then they do not fall out. The Master said, "A double case. The monk said, "I do not yet understand; I have come specifically to request your instruction.
The Master said, "Jung, Yuan, Qian, and Ji—[the monks of these regions] stick brushes in their hair."
Chan Master Fuxian of Yanqing ascended the hall and said: "When a Hu comes, a Hu appears; when a Han comes, a Han appears. But what is it like when both Hu and Han come at once?
He remained silent for a long while and then said: "The setting clouds fly alongside the solitary wild goose; the autumn waters share the same hue as the vast sky. (Examine this.)

Chan Master Yàn of Dàochǎng ascended the hall and said: "The World-Honored One pressed his finger, and the Sea-Seal manifested its radiance. He held up his staff and said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization," and then descended from the seat.
The Dharma Master Congjian of Tianzhu possessed vast knowledge and insight; his reputation resounded throughout the lecture halls, and he had attained a profound realization of *śamatha-vipaśyanā*.
He frequently associated with Chan practitioners and once sought instruction from Datong through the power of the Way. One day, Datong composed a letter and sent it to him.
When the Master opened the seal and beheld the two circular marks, black and white, he attained enlightenment. He replied with a verse:
"The black mark and the white mark—carrying a yoke, one passes through the trial. Whether understood or not, it is like waves rising without wind. If you ask what the ultimate matter is:
Mount Dongting stands upon Lake Tai."
Chan Master Pujizhun ascended the hall and said: "The mountains are green after the rain; the moon is white as the clouds part. The cold pines bear snow;
the courtyard cypresses sway in the wind. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there still the meaning of the Patriarchs?
If you have not yet realized this, listen for a moment: Look! Look!"
Chan Master Nifaha Hai first studied under Master Fayun Xiu. Later, he received the transmission of the Dharma from Master Fazhen.

Although several renowned scholars repeatedly urged him to appear in the world for the benefit of others, he resolutely refused. On the day of his passing, he spoke this verse: "In the frosty sky, clouds and mist gather."
The mountain moon coldly reflects its radiance; at night he received news from his hometown. At dawn, the traveler did not know where he was. When morning came, he sat and passed away.
After being exhorted by Lord Qingxian, the layman Prime Minister Fu Bi never ceased his efforts day or night to advance in this Way.
Hearing that Chan Master Yongning presided over the Dharma seat at Touzi, his reputation preeminent throughout the Huaidian region, Fu went there to resolve his doubts. He met Yongning...

When he went up to the seat for the assembly, he saw that the Master looked back at him with the dignified turn of an elephant king. Gong felt he had attained something; he therefore assumed the etiquette of a disciple and hurried to the master’s quarters.
The Master ordered an attendant to invite him to enter the inner room. Upon seeing him, the Master said, "The Minister has already come in; Fu Bi is still outside.
Hearing this, Gong broke into a sweat that soaked his back, and he attained great enlightenment immediately. He subsequently sent a verse to Yuan.
Zhao Ben said: "Upon seeing Master Yong once, his realization was profound; through successive conditions, he inherited the mind of the Master.

Though the mountains and rivers of the southeast are said to be far away, he faces the Holy Light and the Sublime Sound face-to-face. Later, he submitted a memorial to bestow upon Master Yong the title of "Certified Realization."
Chan Master Niben Zhao ascended the hall. "The spiritual source is unmoving; upon what does the wondrous essence rely? This vivid, solitary luminosity—whose radiance is it?
To say it is the True Suchness or the Ultimate Reality is much like cutting a sore on healthy flesh.

To further deliberate upon it as the "Patriarchal Meaning" is precisely to lose one's head while recognizing its reflection. Let us set aside for now the Old Barbarian’s forty-nine years of preaching dreams. [In the] Sangha Hall...
The Venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra asked, "Do you still remember what was raised for your sake by me?
After a long silence, he said, "Take care of your eyebrows.
Master Wanyan You preached in the hall: "Where the previous sages did not reach, the common folk have arrived. Since the common folk..."
Whether one has arrived or not, whether one knows or does not know—set all of this aside at one side. Consider, for instance, when a monk asked Qianfeng:
"The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all enter the single path to Nirvāṇa; I wonder where the head of that path lies?
Qianfeng took his staff, drew a line, and said, "It is right here. Now tell me: how does this old man compare with those former sages?
How far apart are the ordinary flow [of beings] and [the enlightened state]? A tiger from the South Mountain bites a stone sheep; one must recognize birth and death within this.
Chan Master Huishen of Hailin and Cishou of Cishou relied upon Jingzhao at Zisheng in Jiahe.

Jingzhao cited the karmic conditions of Liangsu meeting Magu and asked: "What is the place where Liangsu knows? The Master immediately attained profound clarity and subsequently went forth to reside there.

At Zifu Monastery, shoes were piled up outside the door. When Chan Master Fojian Qin of Jiangshan arrived while on a tour of propagation, the Master (Zifu) led him on a tour of the quarters after the tea ceremony.
Upon reaching the quarters for the "thousand-man" community, Fojian asked, "Since this is the quarters for a thousand people, why is there only one person here?
The Master replied, "Better one reality than many falsehoods. Fojian said, "Is that so? The Master was abashed. It happened to be the morning...
The court established Zifu as the Shenxiao Palace. Consequently, [Zhaozhou] departed for Jiangshan, leaving Xian’an Chen to request further instruction.
Chen said, "At Zifu, you should have known that such matters are simply this and left it at that. Zhaozhou replied, "I am truly not yet settled; I hope the Master will not reject me."
Jian took up the story of the "Soul Departure of the Beautiful Woman" and examined it from every angle until his doubts were completely dispelled. He presented a verse, saying:
"It is merely the place where one has always walked; To mention it casually is already a source of confusion.
Last night a sudden gale arose, Blowing down how many peach blossoms, who knows? Jian struck the table and said, "Is this not the living meaning of the Patriarchs?"
Ascending the hall: "Where does the cloud arise from? From which ravine does the wind spring? What a fine place for entry!

Yet few travel the official road. Ascending the hall: It is not the environment, nor is it the mind. To call it "Buddha" is already to sink into obscurity. Within this, there is fundamentally no hierarchy;
one must strictly avoid seeking within that which has no hierarchy. If you do not seek at all, the error is even deeper. Break it open!
"Cloud Gate, you rice-bag! Only now do you know that red earth is gold!
*Pfft!* Whenever Chan Master Wanshou Gui saw a monk, he would invariably ask, "How have you been lately?
If the monk hesitated, he would pat him on the back and say, "Inconceivable. When he was about to pass away, the assembly gathered. He spoke once more, "Inconceivable," and then joined his palms.
He passed away.
When Zen Master Cheonui Jeol was asked about the saying, "Regye constantly calls out, 'The Host! the Master replied with a verse:
"Regye constantly calls out, 'The Host! It soars forth from the highest peak of Mount Sumeru. When the great earth is overturned, there is nothing left behind."
Seeking a place: A single melody of flute and song within the painted tower.
Zen Master Zhizhe Shouchuan ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to strike the profound pivot, you must possess integrity and be utterly resolute.
Only one who can cut through nails and sever iron—a person of stark and unyielding resolve—will succeed. As for those who hide behind blades and evade arrows, who are merely mediocre..."
For those of this sort, there is a share [of the Dharma] upon seeing it. With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat and descended.
Master Chanran Baoen ascended the hall and said: "Students who engage in empty talk without substance must seek wondrous enlightenment.
To abandon wondrous enlightenment for empty talk is like chasing after a foul odor. Although this is so, rare are those who encounter a guest with pierced ears; many instead meet—
The man who marked the boat one day said to the assembly, "Worldly conditions are easily defiled, while the path of practice is difficult to discern. You all must exert yourselves.
Having finished speaking, he passed away.
Chan Master Xuefeng Yan ascended the hall and said: "To cast off delusion in search of enlightenment, one does not realize that delusion is the very hammer of enlightenment.

To cherish the holy and loathe the ordinary, one does not realize that the ordinary is the very forge of the holy. But when both the holy and the ordinary have vanished together, and both delusion and enlightenment are forgotten—how do you speak this single phrase?
At midnight, colored clouds enshroud the jade elephant; at daybreak, five-colored clouds crown the mountain peak."
Zhe. Wang Dafu of Wei Prefecture visited Paramārtha (Yuanfeng) and realized his return [to the source] upon hearing a few words.

Thereafter, he returned to the southern slope of Mount Tan and lived in a thatched hut for three years. Once, he sang this verse: "Within the Tan mountains, how long is the day? On the ridges of green pines, the white..."
In the Cloud Village, where singing birds and crying monkeys form the site of practice, he lets his hair flow loose and sings and laughs while gathering *wei* roots;
let people call him a madman, for he is a wild man.
Master Zhen of Mount Lin ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said: 'At the end of autumn and the beginning of summer, there ought to be thirty instances of reprimanding one's feelings.'"
A blow! Yue-lin does not think so. At the assembly on Vulture Peak, when the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled—at that very moment, he should have been given thirty blows.
Why is this so? Because in times of peace, one needlessly raises the sword.
He teaches others to blow the great Dharma conch and beat the great Dharma drum. When he takes a step, golden lotuses bloom beneath his feet;
when he sits upright, a precious throne rises majestically. Brahmā leads him from the front, surrounded by swirling incense and flowers, while Śakra follows behind him.
Dragons and elephants stand side by side, causing descendants of later generations to emulate one another; in groups of threes and twos, they all claim to possess extraordinary character and bearing.

From kalpa to kalpa, through endless toil, they refuse to return home and sit in peace. Their flapping lips and wagging tongues are like the chiming of bells and stone chimes or the blowing of pipes and reeds;
their brandishing arms and pointing at their chests exceed the number of rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds. They further display their fondness for wandering mountains and playing in waters.
"Parting the grass to catch the wind," he says before people, "the stone nods its head; flowers fly down from heaven, covering the ground. Even so, he deserves thirty blows.

But tell me, how should one reward him for his labors during the summer retreat? After a long silence, he said: "When the myriad treasures have achieved their work, what thickness or thinness is there?
When the price of a thousand-jin weight is set, it naturally rises or falls on its own."
A monk asked Master Guanyin of Xiuzhou, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A tortoise walking through fire at midnight.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Space has no front or back. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.
Chan Master Xiang of Jingci ascended the hall. An ancient said, "When a single film obscures the eye, empty flowers fall in confusion.
Holding up his staff, he said, "Jingci raises this staff—is this not 'a single film obscuring the eye'?
Within it, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas all manifest bodies sixteen feet tall, of purple-gold hue, riding upon their lands and traveling through the ten directions."
To now speak of "all dharmas" and "delivering all sentient beings"—is this not like empty flowers falling in disarray?
Right now, can anyone cut it off while the staff has not yet been raised? Come forth and meet with Jingci! If there is no one, [I shall strike].

"Be careful not to fall into the trap of thinking that flowers are fundamentally non-existent in the sky; the eye is fundamentally free of cataracts. Having said this, he threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Chan Master Huichun of Lingyin ascended the hall and said: "My mind is like the autumn moon, clear and bright in the azure pool.
He then gave a shout and said: "Hanshan has fallen into error! O Zen practitioners, being clear and bright and free of dust—how could this be the moon of the Mid-Autumn Festival?"

It may be compared [to the moon]: empty and luminous, beyond all dependence; it cannot be equaled by the pearl that illuminates the world. It stands alone, revealing heaven and earth; its light swallows the myriad phenomena.
Pervading the heavens and covering the earth, it shines through antiquity and soars through the present. But tell me, what is this? After a long silence, he said:
"On this night, the single orb is full; where is its pure light not present?"
Chan Master Dachtang Daochang of Jingci Monastery ascended the hall and said: "If you have not yet penetrated the Patriarch’s Barrier, there are a thousand difficulties and ten thousand hardships.

Once you have penetrated the Patriarch’s Barrier, there are still a thousand difficulties and ten thousand hardships. Setting aside for a moment the difficulties when you have not yet penetrated it—now that you have penetrated it, why are they still difficult?
Though one may obtain the price by putting down the colander, to move the ladle is groundless."
Chan Master Liaotang of Mount Jingshan ascended the hall and said:

"Those practitioners who investigate the mystery of the Way and yet cannot achieve immediate penetration and liberation when encountering circumstances and conditions do so because their karmic consciousness is deep and heavy, their delusive emotions are stubbornly fixed, the six sense-gates have not ceased, and not a single point is unobstructed.
This state of absolute purity is difficult for sentient beings to reach; one must enter the forest without moving a blade of grass and enter the water..."

Chan Master Baoben Yuan addressed the assembly from the high seat. A monk asked, "The Dharma taught by all Buddhas is entirely of various expedient means;
is this so? The Master said, "Yes. The monk asked, "Why then is it said that the mark of the cessation of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words? The Master said:
"Do not misunderstand this. The monk drew a line with his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). The Master shouted, "The mark of the quiescence of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words.
Now, when students see that the Way cannot be proclaimed in words, they immediately attempt to cease their thoughts and forget external conditions, blocking off their sight and hearing.
With such a view, they do not yet possess a share of mastery. Do you all understand 'quiescence'?"
"Look! Upon leaving the gate, not a single hair's breadth is seen; the eyes are filled with white clouds and green ridges.
Chan Master Longqing Qian went to visit Huanglong at Huangbo. Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Bazhang.
Huanglong asked, "When did you leave there? The Master replied, "The thirteenth day of the first month. Huanglong said, "Your heels must ache terribly; give me three..."
"Ten blows," the Master said. "Not only thirty blows. Long shouted, "After traveling as a mendicant for so long, you have not a breath of spirit left!

The Master said, "Even the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are likewise thus. Long asked, "When you came here like this, how could there ever have been even a hair’s breadth that reached the realm of the Buddhas?
The Master said, "The Buddhas have likely never reached the realm of Qingxian. Long asked, "What about..."
"What is the place where you were born? The Master said, "In the morning I ate white congee; now I feel hungry again. "What is your hand like? Is it like a Buddha’s hand?
The Master said, "Playing the lute under the moon. "What are your feet like? Are they like a donkey’s feet?
The Master said, "A heron standing in the snow is not the same color [as the snow]. Long sighed in admiration and looked at him, saying, "You have shaved off your hair and beard; you ought to..."
"For what purpose? The Master said, "I simply want there to be no affairs. The monk said, "In that case, 'A few sounds of the clear chime are beyond right and wrong;
one idle man dwells within heaven and earth. The Master said, "What words are these? The monk said, "O sharp-witted patch-robed monk!
The Master said, "That too is unnecessary. Long said, "There is an Elder Bian here; you must exert your full attention. The Master said, [To Bian: "..."
"What excellence does he possess? [Nanquan] asked. [Longtan] said, "He patted you on the back once. "How was that? the Master asked. [Longtan] said, "What did he do?
[Longtan] said, "He spread out both hands. The Master said, "Where did you learn this hypocrisy? Longtan laughed loudly.
The Master then spread out both hands himself, and Longtan shouted at him.
Chan Master Sanzong ascended the hall and said: "Brilliantly shining, lively and agile—the entire ten-direction world is but a single hair-tip.
Thrown before you, do you know it or not? Do not pick it up on the level of the conceptual mind. He gave a single clap.
Chan Master Letan Ying visited the *Huayan Shiming Lun* (The Ten Clarifications of the Avatamsaka Sutra), through which he realized the essential tenets of the school.
He then went to the seat of Chan Master Nan of Huangbo. Huangbo conversed with him until dawn and said, "The responsibility for carrying the Great Dharma rests entirely upon your person;

take great care of yourself. Wherever he went, his discussions eclipsed those of his peers. Later, while traveling through the Western Mountains, he stayed with the Head Seat Sheng at Shuangling. Subsequently, he opened [a monastery].
He presided at Fashi Gate. After some time, he moved to Letan. Ascending the hall, he looked over the assembly and said: "The crags of Shimen are treacherous and the iron gates are secure;
looking up, they rise in layers ten thousand fathoms high. Only the hornless iron ox can break through them, creating waves within the sea of Vairocana.
Now tell me, how do you speak that single phrase which does not involve the waves? After a long silence, he said: "One."
Wuzhuo did not have time to inquire about the meaning of the phrase; even to this day, he remains a "wild-platter monk.

Because the administrative officials were quarreling and could not be stopped, the Master said to the assembly, "That you do not maintain discipline as a community is precisely because I lack virtue. I feel ashamed before Huanglong."

In recording the beginning and end of his travels, he said: "After my passing, I shall be cremated; my remains shall be enshrined in a collective stupa (pútóngtǎ) to demonstrate that life and death are not separate from the pure assembly.
Having finished speaking, he passed away.

Chan Master Baoning Yuanji ascended the hall and said: "Extensively seeking the meaning of texts is like seeking a form in a mirror; stilling thoughts to contemplate emptiness is like grasping at the moon in water.
To speak of the single transmission of the mind-seal is already an extraordinary complication. Deshan and Linji have labored in vain."

Shigong and Zihu turned it into something quite extraordinary. If it were Baoning, he would not act in such a way at all; he would simply follow conditions in eating and drinking, remaining entirely ordinary.
Deeply reclusive amidst the white clouds, he was content to be one who has transcended learning. I dare ask you all: how would you handle this?
Baoning finally asked, "With what shall one repay the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence? After a long silence, he said:
"Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful; to speak of them to a sorrowful person is to kill them with grief."
When Chan Master Yunfeng Daoyuan was staying with Jicui, they were seated together at the end of the formal session. At that time, two monks were discussing the "Wild Fox" kōan.
One said, "Even 'not being ignorant of cause and effect' has not yet allowed one to shed the wild fox body. The other said, "'Not falling into cause and effect' [is what sheds it]."

"And when have you ever fallen as a wild fox? Hearing this, the Master was struck with awe. He then went to Jicui Hermitage, and while crossing a mountain stream, he experienced a sudden, profound realization.
He composed a verse, saying: "Neither falling nor being obscured; for monks and laypeople alike, there is no taboo. A man of true stature has the bearing of a king."
Vying for bags, robes, and coverlets; with a single staff, they roam wherever they please. A wild fox leaps into the ranks of the golden cats; Cuijian expresses his joy on their behalf.
Chan Master Hongyan of the Fourth Patriarch asked a monk:
"What is the characteristic of the mind? The Master said: "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked again: [How is it? The Master said: [It is... (The text ends here).
"What is the essence of mind? The Master said, "What do you call mountains, rivers, and the great earth?
Chan Master Qingyin Qian’an Yuan ascended the hall and said: "In the beginning, my late master served Xiexian Zhi and Letan Cheng for twenty years.

There was nothing—whether the wondrous and profound mysteries of the Chan school or the subtle essentials of the sutras and treatises—that he did not penetrate. It was through Yunfeng’s pointing that..."
Upon meeting Ciming, [Furong] realized that not a single word was of use. He consequently established three "gateless barriers" to test his students;
yet the students were like Prince Gong’s painted dragon—they were terrified as soon as the dragon appeared.
Master Chan Master Lianquan Tanshou was asked by a monk, "What is the place where the student turns? The Master said, "Sweeping the floor and watering the flowers.
The monk asked, "What is the place where the student is intimately present? The Master said, "Highly propping up the pillow on the head.
The monk asked, "How is it when it is not like this at all? The Master said, "The oriole sings atop the ridge; the flowers bloom before the crags."

Chan Master Lingjiu Huijue ascended the hall and addressed the assembly: "Great assembly, the hundreds of thousands of samādhis and immeasurable wondrous meanings are all beneath the feet of each of you.
Please, each of you, turn back and take them up for yourselves. Do you understand?
Whether you turn back or do not turn back, recognize the path home. Let wisdom serve as the bridge and gentleness as your refuge. When dwelling in safety, anticipate danger. In...
One who delights [in pleasure] must know it to be suffering. Have you not seen Master Pang? He cast away gold as if it were mere filth.
Father and son sat together in a circle, speaking words of the unborn. Take these words of the unborn well to heart: in the nine months of summer, snowflakes fly;
in the three months of winter, sweat falls like rain.
The Master Jicui Yong addressed the assembly: "Since this mountain monk has resided in this hermitage, there is no Chan to be preached and no Dharma to be transmitted.

Furthermore, I possess no rare treasures or extraordinary jewels; I have only secured a single ember from a continuing firebrand to leave for future generations, so that their smoke and flames shall never cease and their fiery light shall remain forever bright.
He then cast down his whisk. At that moment, a monk picked it up from the ground.
He rose and blew out [the lamp] with a single puff. The Master then shouted, "Who would have known that the remaining embers of the firebrand would vanish and the flames go out from this fellow?
Thereupon, he shook his sleeves and returned to his hermitage. The monk stuck out his tongue and departed.
The Master of the Hermitage at Guizong, Zhixian, relied upon Huanglong and thereby attained his profound intent. He composed a verse that said: "If you have not yet arrived, you must arrive;
once arrived, it makes people laugh. Eyebrows are originally of no use; who possesses such cleverness? Not long after, Huanglong withdrew from his post.

Zhishi was submerged among the crowd. One day, after the communal labor (puching) had concluded, he wrote a verse: "The tea buds, rustling, have just left the roasting kiln; The bamboo shoots, in haste, are again emerging from the mud.
In this mountain cottage, the spring tasks of the year are complete; Who cares for leisure when the board at the head of the bed is low?
Because of this, the monastic disciples (nazzi) flocked to him. The Master was displeased and built a hermitage on a peak, composing a verse: "Atop the thousand peaks..."

"Sharing one roof; the old monk has half a room for himself and half for the clouds. Last night the clouds followed the wind and rain away; in the end, they are not as idle as the old monk. When Chan Master Wuxin Wuxin of Huanglong went to visit Huaitang, Tang held up his fist and asked, "What do you call this? "A fist," [Wuxin] replied. Tang said, "If you call it a fist, you will fall into hell like a shooting star. Wuxin was greatly enlightened. He then composed a verse: "A fist is not a fist; The fist is not a fist. If you call it a fist, You will fall into hell like a shooting star. Tang said, "You have attained my marrow. He then had him serve as the head of the assembly. Later, when Wuxin was about to depart, Tang asked, "Where are you going? Wuxin replied, "To the place where there is no Buddha or patriarch. Tang said, "Even if you go to the place where there is no Buddha or patriarch, you must still pass through the gate of the local official. Wuxin said, "I am already passing through. Tang said, "The local official has just now gone out. Wuxin said, "He has returned. Tang said, "How can you say he has returned? Wuxin said, "He has returned. Tang said, "You have attained my marrow. Wuxin then took his leave. As he was crossing the bridge, he suddenly leaped into mid-air and shouted, "Ah! Tang called out from within the hall, "Wuxin! Wuxin turned his head and looked back. Tang said, "Do you understand? Wuxin said, "I understand. Tang said, "If you say you understand, you will fall into hell like a shooting star. Wuxin bowed and departed. That very day, he ascended the Dharma hall and addressed the assembly: "The first phrase is like a sword-edge; The second phrase is like a precipice.
