In the hall, he looked at the assembly and said, "An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball. He then descended from his seat.

The Master [Dongshan] joyfully stepped out from among the assembly and said, "Venerable Monk, please try rolling one yourself. The Patriarch made a gesture with his hands as if beating a war drum and, in the Shu dialect, sang a folk song from Mianzhou:
"On Mount Douzi, they beat the earthen drums; On Mount Yangping, they scatter white rain. The white rain falls, take it..."
A dragon girl wove a bolt of silk measuring twenty-five *zhang* in length; half belonged to Luo Jiang and half to Wu Xu. Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He covered the Patriarch’s mouth and said, “It need only have been sung as far as this point. The Patriarch laughed heartily and returned. [Later,] he ascended the hall to preach.

This one great cause and condition has, since the World-Honored One held up the flower and Kāśyapa smiled, been entrusted by the World-Honored One as the Treasury of the True Dharma-Eye to Mahākāśyapa.
Thereafter, it has been transmitted from lamp to lamp and passed down from patriarch to patriarch until the present day, continuing in an unbroken succession.
It has truly reached the point where flowers bloom everywhere on the ground; therefore, it is called Nirvāṇa.
"Wondrous Mind. It is also called the Original Mind; it is also called the Original Nature; it is also called the Original Face;
it is also called the Ultimate Truth (Paramārthasatya); it is also called the Akṣobhya Eye; it is also called the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
In a man, it is called 'man'; in a woman, it is called 'woman. You all, simply awaken to it yourselves! All such things are merely idle words. Thereupon, he took up [the whisk].
Master Qifu said: "To realize it is called Chan; before awakening, it is truly difficult, difficult, difficult. Before one's eyes stands Mount Sumeru.
Once awakened, it is easy, easy, easy; whatever comes from the mouth is not otherwise."

Among the five patriarchs, Master Zizhen was the one who relied upon the Patriarch for the longest time without yet having attained realization. At that time, Yuanwu served as the Seat-Holder (Zuoyuan).
The Master went to seek his instruction, and Yuanwu said, "Brother, try telling me where your doubt lies. The Master then cited the passage from Deshan’s informal sermon:

"I do not answer those who come to talk; those who ask questions receive thirty blows of the staff. Yuanwu said, "Prostrate yourself! I can act as your teacher. [The Master] then raised the case once more.
"No. After the master had finished bowing, Wuzu told him to repeat his previous statement. The master said, "Deshan’s informal discourse says he does not answer questions.
Wuzu covered his mouth and said, "Just look at it like this. The master went out and cried out loudly, "A grievance! A grievance!
How can there be a public case that merely instructs people to look at a single phrase? A monk said to the master, "Brother, you should not speak like this."
The Master said, "The Head Seat must have skillful means. Because he sat in meditation to investigate this for ten days, his doubts were suddenly resolved.

He went to pay his respects to Wuzhuo, who said, "Brother, you have finally realized that I did not deceive you. He then went to the Abbot’s quarters; the Patriarch (Dongshan) greeted him with a smile.

From that time on, his understanding of the profound and mysterious became daily deeper. The Master posted a notice at the door of the Attendant’s quarters, saying: "Dongshan has three phrases. If anyone can speak them, [I shall grant them the position]."

He was immediately enrolled as a resident monk, and the other practitioners were all disheartened. One day, a monk carrying his sitting mat went directly to the master’s quarters and said to him, "I cannot explain the Way;
I simply wish to be enrolled as a resident. The Master was greatly pleased and called for the *vinaya-dhara* (Vina) to arrange a place for him beneath a bright window.
Chan Master Jiuding Su went to visit the Fifth Patriarch. Upon hearing the words of Shoushan regarding the meaning of the Westward Journey, he suddenly attained realization.
He composed a verse, saying: "Topsy-turvy, topsy-turvy! Topsy-turvy, topsy-turvy! The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. Just so!"
How utterly groundless! Turning his head, he unconsciously realized his cloth robe was on. When the Patriarch saw this, he asked, "As for Baizhang’s story of the wild fox, what do you say?
The Master replied, "Those who come to speak of right and wrong are themselves the people of right and wrong. The Patriarch was greatly pleased.

When the Head Seat Yuanli first visited Master Yan at Baiyun, every time he entered the room for instruction, Yan would invariably say to him, "Monks of the robe-lineage must clearly distinguish between black and white.
The Master harbored this doubt without ceasing. One day, as Yan ascended the hall, he cited the saying of Shoushan:
"The bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. He then said, "Do you all understand? Do not ask about the bride or the mother-in-law."
"Enough of this bother. On the road at Pāṭaliputra, when I encountered rice, I ate rice; when I encountered tea, I drank tea. Those who enter and exit the same gate are enemies from past lives.
At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened and said, "Today, the distinction between the monastic and the lay has been made clear."
Puyong Zhizang [Verse]: Upon reaching the occasion of entering the room of the Fifth Patriarch, the Patriarch raised the story of the "Two Women and the Separated Souls" and questioned him.

Puyong presented his realization with a verse, which said: "The two women merge into one daughter-in-law; The turning wheel is severed, difficult to turn back. From of old, coming and going leave no trace;
Travelers need not ask the path by which they came. (Note: According to the tenth volume of the *Lianzhu songgu*, there is an account of the Fifth Patriarch Yan asking...)

The monk asked, "In the story of the 'Soul-Separation of the Borrowed Maiden,' which one was the real? He then provided this commentary: "Wang Zhou wished to marry the maiden Qian as his wife, but her parents would not permit it. Consequently, Qian fell ill and remained at home. When Wang Zhou was about to travel far away, he saw Qian coming toward him under the moon;

they boarded the same boat and departed. Three years later, she gave birth to a son. Qian then returned to her parents' house. As soon as she reached the gate, another maiden emerged from the house; upon meeting, the two merged into a single body."
Chan Master Xian of Chengtian ascended the hall and said: "The waning moon falls as the fifth watch ends and the sky dawns; white clouds drift—this is a matter clearly before one's eyes.
It is not a function of the present moment. Since it is a matter before one's eyes, why is it not a function of the present moment?"
After a long silence, he said: "What I wish to say cannot be fully expressed; let us deliberate instead beneath the forest trees. Yudao Po of Jinling [Verse]:
She made her living selling sesame cakes and was a constant companion to the assembly as they visited Langya.
Langya showed her the story of Linji’s "True Person Without Rank. One day, she heard a beggar singing the *Lianhua Yue* (Lotus Music), which said: "Not..."
Because Liu Yi had sent a letter, she wondered how it could have reached Lake Dongting. Suddenly, she attained great enlightenment; she threw her rice-cake tray to the ground.
Her husband looked on askance and said, "Are you mad? His wife slapped him and said, "This is not within your realm.
She went to see Langya, who, upon observing her, knew the depth of her realization. He asked, "Who is that person of no rank? The nun replied instantly, "There is one."
The person of no station has six arms and three heads, exerting effort in wrath. With one strike, Mount Hua was split into two paths; the flowing waters of Wanyan know nothing of spring.
Because of this, her reputation became widely renowned. Whenever a monk arrived, she would say, "Child, child!
If the monk hesitated, she would immediately close the door. Chan Master Fodeng Xun went there to test her. When the old woman saw him, she questioned him as before. Xun said:
"Where is my father? The old woman turned around and bowed to a pillar. Xun immediately kicked it over and said, "I thought there was something particularly extraordinary here.
He then went out. The old woman scrambled up and said, "Child, child, come back! I cherish you! But Xun paid her no mind at all.
When An Shouzuo arrived, the old woman asked, "Where have you come from? An replied, "From Deshan. The woman said, "Deshan Tai was indeed a son of an old woman.
An asked, "And whose son are you, old woman? The woman said, "Having been questioned by you, Senior, I am compelled to stand right here and urinate."
When Chan Master Dahui Zonggao of Jingshan was seventeen years old, he shaved his head and received full ordination in the Vinaya.

While casually reading the records of the ancient Yunmen, he felt as though he were encountering something familiar from his past training. He then went to rely upon Chan Master Cheng of Guangjiao, but soon left to travel through the four quarters, following various elder masters of the Caodong school.
Having mastered their teachings, he departed for Baofeng to visit Chan Master Zhantang Zun. Upon seeing him, Zhantang...

Yantou regarded this with suspicion and had him serve as his attendant, hoping to guide him toward the shortcut for entering the Way. However, the Master (Dongshan) was so unconstrained in his responses that Yantou could find no fault in him;
instead, he rebuked him, saying, "You have not yet attained realization. Your illness lies in your reliance on intellectual understanding, which constitutes the obstacle of knowledge (*jñeyāvaraṇa*).

When Yantou was near death, he instructed the Master, saying, "After I am gone, you must see Chuan Qin (Qin being Yuanwu). He will surely be able to exhaustively bring forth these functions of your potential. Yantou passed away. The Master...
He hurried to visit Master Wujin to request an inscription for his hall and stupa. Wujin’s gate was high and he rarely granted approval;
however, finding that the Master’s words were in accord with his own, he offered him lodging and extended an invitation. He named the Master’s hermitage Miaoxi (Wondrous Joy).

Later, when the Master visited again, Wujin further instructed him to go see Yuanwu. [Verse] The Master arrived at Tianning Monastery. One day, he heard Yuanwu ascend the hall and cite a monk’s question to Yunmen: [text continues].
"What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? The Gatekeeper replied, "On the mountain to the east, one walks upon the water.
If it were Tianning, he would not have said so. Had someone asked him, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?

he would have simply told them: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. Upon hearing these words, the Master’s past and future suddenly severed. Although this was so...
The characteristic of movement does not arise; one simply sits back in the state of pure nakedness. Wuzu said to him, "It is no easy matter for you to reach this stage.
It is a pity that though you have died, you cannot yet live. Not doubting the words and phrases is a great illness.
Have you not heard it said: 'Let go at the edge of the precipice; if you are willing to accept it yourself, you will revive after death—this cannot deceive the Master. You must believe this."
"There is this principle," [Wuzhuo] said, and he consequently appointed [Zhaozhou] to reside in the Zhemu Hall as an attendant who did not manage administrative affairs.

Every day, he entered the room for private instruction together with the high officials (Zhemu was the place where court officials rested). Whenever Wuzhuo raised the question, "There is a phrase, there is no phrase;
it is like a vine leaning against a tree," and questioned him, Zhaozhou would say, as soon as his mouth opened, "Not so, not so. After half a year had passed, he finally asked Wuzhuo:
"I heard that when you were with the Fifth Patriarch, you once asked this same question. I do not know what the Fifth Patriarch said.
Wuzu smiled but did not answer. The Master said, "You must have asked this before the assembly at that time; why would it not be permissible to speak of it now?"
Dongshan was compelled to acknowledge this. He said, "I asked about the 'phrase with' and the 'phrase without,' like a vine leaning against a tree—what is the underlying meaning?
The Patriarch replied, "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted. Dongshan asked again, "What is it like when the tree falls and the vine withers?
The Patriarch replied, "It has followed along. At that moment, Dongshan was suddenly relieved and said, "I understand! Thereupon, Dongshan recounted several... [instances].
When he questioned him on the causes and conditions [of the teachings], the Master responded without hesitation. Yuanwu said, "Now I know that I did not deceive you.

He then composed the *Record of the True Lineage of Linji* and entrusted it to him, appointing him to oversee the secretariat. Before long, he was ordered to share the seat [with the Master] in the teaching hall.
There, he wielded a bamboo staff to test his students, and the monastic community came to revere him profoundly. His fame resounded throughout the capital. Minister of the Right Lü Shun...
The Emperor granted him purple robes and the title "Buddha-Sun" (Furi). During the Jurchen uprising, their chieftain intended to take several dozen Chan monks as captives;
the Master was among those selected but managed to escape. He went to Huqiu Mountain in Wu to spend the summer retreat, where he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

Upon reaching the passage on the Bodhisattva ascending to the seventh stage and realizing the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), he thoroughly understood what he had previously questioned of Zhan Tang regarding Yaśoda.
The story of Luo carrying his bowl to the house of a woman in childbirth. At that time, Yuanwu was summoned to reside at Yunju. The Master went there to pay his respects;
on the second day of his arrival at the mountain, he was immediately invited to serve as the First Seat (Dìyīzuò).

At that time, there were many "dragons and elephants" among the assembly who, because Yuanwu had long left the seat vacant while waiting for the Master’s arrival, harbored feelings of resentment. When it came to the winter solstice, [Yuanwu] held the whisk (to preach). Zha...
Chan Master Jueyuan stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What is it like when a sword hangs between the eyebrows? The Master replied, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven.
Yuanwu, while seated below, made a gesture with his hand, saying, "Stop, stop! That question was excellent; the answer is even more extraordinary."
Yuan then returned to the assembly, and from this point on, the monastic community underwent a transformation. Ascending the hall for the formal address:

On the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the first month, at Shuangjing, mallets strike the gongs and drums resound. If you wish to understand the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, look to the village songs and communal dances. Ascending the hall for the formal address.
Chan Master Yuan Tongxiu addressed the assembly, saying: "At Shaolin, for nine years he sat in cold meditation, yet was ultimately seen through by Shen Guang.
Now, jade and stone are difficult to distinguish; one can only wrap it in hemp and paper.
This one, that one, and yet another—if one has clear eyes, why need there be further explanation? Today at Jingshan, I cannot help but add my own dog-tail to the end."
A continuation of the "fox-tail" [mimicking the noble]. There is indeed some substance here. The Old Barbarian’s discourse fell into ruin nine years ago;
it is a pity he let it pass at that time, which led to those followers of silent illumination sitting in meditation for years within a ghost cave—one of them, another of them, yet another.
Although his bitter words were earnest and repeated, they were like the wind passing over the treetops. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mud ox beneath the water chews raw."
Iron. Kōnbatsu-ti bit his tongue; the Sea God grew angry and took up a coral whip; Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, suffered pain that pierced to the marrow. Ascending the hall, he said:
"It was just the Mid-Autumn Festival of the eighth month, and now it is already the fifteenth of the ninth month.

He struck the meditation staff on the floor and said, "Only this does not migrate. Throwing down the staff, he said, "The entire assembly has heard it with their ears and seen it with their eyes. —Wenyuan.
On the anniversary of the Chan Master’s passing, the Master held up the incense and said: "This venerable one was in his lifetime stubborn and upright, his spirit overwhelming all quarters.
He displayed an overweening, coarse indifference and employed a blunt, unconventional style. He claimed, 'I shall exchange my wooden *muhan* beads for the eyes of all people under heaven.
Little did he know that his unfilial son would pierce his nostrils with a broken cord."
Since the head of the rope is already in the hands of Jingshan, whether he causes it to live or whether he causes it to die depends entirely on Jingshan.
Tell me, by what means is this verified? He then burned incense and said, "This is the verification.
A monk asked, "Does a person of great cultivation still fall within the realm of cause and effect? Baizhang of the past replied, "He does not fall within cause and effect."
"Why did he fall into the body of a wild fox? The Master said, "Whenever you meet someone, simply present it thus.

[The monk] asked, "As for what Baizhang later said, 'He was not deluded regarding cause and effect,' why did he shed his wild fox body? The Master said, "Whenever you meet someone, simply present it thus.
[The monk] asked, "If someone were to ask Jingshan, 'Does a person of great cultivation still fall under the sway of cause and effect? before—"
Shen asked, "What did the Master say to him? The Master replied, "I told him: 'Whenever you meet someone, simply speak of it in this way.
A questioner asked, "When the past mind cannot be apprehended, the present mind cannot be apprehended, and the future mind cannot be apprehended—what then?
The Master said, "The words of the master come from the mouth of the master. The questioner asked, "How should one receive and uphold this? The Master said, "Simply act in this way."
If you uphold this, you will certainly not be deceived. [Verse: When both mind and Buddha are forgotten, what then? The Master said:
"The old woman selling fans shields her eyes with her hand. A monk requested instruction on the story of Jia Shan’s realm. Before the monk had finished speaking, the Master gave a shout.
The monk was left bewildered. The Master asked, "What were you asking? As the monk prepared to speak, the Master struck him repeatedly and shouted him out. As soon as the Master saw...
The monk entered. The Master immediately said, "It is not so; go out. The monk went out. The Master said, "A man of immeasurable capacity has been turned around by the flow of words.
[Verse] In the room, he held up a bamboo stick and asked a monk, "To call it a 'bamboo stick' is to commit an offense (*chu*).
Not to call it a 'bamboo stick' is to turn one's back (*bei*). You may not utter a word, nor may you remain silent. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk said, "Please..."
The Master said, "Monk, put down your bamboo staff. The monk replied, "Master, you put down your bamboo staff. The monk then brushed out his sleeves and departed.
The Master said, "Attendant, recognize this monk! (In the early Chunxi era, the complete record of eighty fascicles was bestowed upon him and circulated alongside the Tripitaka.)
Chan Master Shao Long of Huqiu went to visit Chan Master Xìn of Changlu and attained a general understanding of his teachings.

When someone brought a transmission of Yuanwu’s words to him, the Master read them and sighed, saying, "It is as if one were imagining the taste of vinegar; though it has not yet drenched my intestines or moistened my stomach."
This was enough to bring people great joy; my only regret was that I had not yet heard his voice.

He then proceeded from Baofeng to rely upon Zantang, stayed as a guest at Huanglong, and called upon Chan Master Sishin. Next, he visited Yuanwu. One day, while entering the inner room for instruction, Yuanwu asked:
"When seeing the very act of seeing, that seeing is not [the] seeing. Seeing is already detached from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. He then raised his fist and said, "Do you see?"

Wuzhuo asked, "Do you see it? Yunmen replied, "I see. Wuzhuo said, "That is adding a head on top of a head. Upon hearing this, Yunmen attained a sudden realization. Wuzhuo rebuked him, saying, "What have you seen?
Yunmen replied, "Dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing water from passing through. Wuzhuo approved of him and subsequently appointed him to oversee the library.
Someone asked Wugu, "Master Long is so gentle and easygoing; how can he accomplish anything? Wugu replied, "He is merely a dozing tiger. Ascending the hall, he said:
"There is no dharma before one's eyes, yet the myriad phenomena stand in dense array. The meaning lies right before one's eyes, yet it suddenly emerges, difficult to discern."
It is not a dharma of the present moment; wherever one encounters it, it is there. It is not something that reaches the ears or eyes, yet it is never apart from seeing, hearing, sensing, or knowing.
Even so, you must still step upon its supreme pivot before you can succeed. Therefore it is said: "The net cannot hold it;
though called, it does not turn its head. Buddhas and patriarchs have made no arrangements for it, and to this day it has no fixed location."
In this way, there is no need for the laborious effort of concentrating the mind. The gates of the pavilion open; without moving a single step, one reaches all hundred cities.
[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff and draws a line, saying: "When you encounter a dead snake on the road, do not strike it; carry it home in a bottomless basket. [Verse:
When he first visited Sīxīn, Sīxīn asked, "What kind of monk are you? The Master replied, "A wandering monk. Sīxīn said:
"Where do you come from? What kind of donkey's tracks and horse's tracks are you making? The Master said, "What does a barbarian from Guangnan say?
Yunmen asked, "Why not say it in a loud voice? Yunmen replied, "That has some of the air of a true monk. He then invited him to stay for the summer retreat. [Added from later collections]
Chan Master Duanyu of Yuyang first relied upon Chan Master Yi of Jingci. Not long after, he happened to hear a monk strike a pillar and say, "Why do you not speak of Chan?
At that moment, the Master suddenly attained a slight realization. He subsequently went to visit Chan Master Yuan of Longmen, Chan Master Zhuo of Gantang, and Chan Master Xiang of Letan;
all of them commended him for his exceptional brilliance and progress. Later, he met Yuanwu at Zhongfu Mountain. One day, Yuanwu—
Question: "Who knows that the Eye of the True Dharma was extinguished at the side of this blind donkey?

Is it extinguished right now, or not? Dongshan said: "Please, Master, keep your mouth shut. Wuzu said: "This is still within the realm of ordinary sentiment. As the Master (Dongshan) was about to respond, Wuzu struck him.
Dongshan’s lingering attachments were instantly cast off. Ascending the hall, he said: "When walking, there is no trace of walking; when speaking, there is no speaking."
If one’s conduct and speech reach their destination, then one will encounter the target and draw the arrow; if one’s conduct and speech are not yet clear, then the divine blade will cut them off.

Even if one’s speech is without leakage and one’s conduct does not lose its way, one still remains stuck within the shell and leakages. If one were a great garuḍa with golden wings, [one would fly away].
The Ten-Shadow Divine Steed, capable of traversing hundreds of thousands of *yojanas* in an instant, gallops across the four quarters and the eight directions.
It does not pause to graze, nor does it stop to bury its body; it relies on nothing at all. Is there still a portion for one to tread upon?

Every moment and every speck of dust is the essential passageway. Ascending the hall, he said: "When Deshan entered the gate, he struck him with his staff. Most people look for this within their own skin-bags."
Burying one's traces: when Linji entered the gate, he immediately shouted. This was entirely a matter of appearing and disappearing within the sensory field of sound.
If you are a truly heroic monk, you must have the wind rise beneath your feet, transcending the paths and tracks of past and present.

[The Master] picks up his staff, strikes once, and shouts, saying: "This very thing—how is it? If you call it a blow or a shout, you are still drowsing and have not yet awakened; if you do not call it...
He delivered shouts and blows. Not yet having recognized the ultimate nature of Deshan and Linji, [the Master] struck once more and said, "Do not move at all!
Whenever the Master presided over the assembly, his countenance was invariably stern. He never ate or slept apart from the community, and he never grew weary in proclaiming the Way.
In the tenth month of the Gengwu year of the Xiangxi era, he manifested a slight illness. The Head Seat, Faquan, requested his final instructions. The Master said, "Exhaust this mind and intention;
support one another with the Way. Having spoken these words, he passed away.
A monk asked Chan Master Daomiao Foxing Fatai: "Principle conforms to phenomena, encompassing all existence as a single, tranquil void;
phenomena follow along with principle, equalizing all differences as they return to the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). What is the Dharma-realm of Principle?"
The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of phenomena? The Master said, "The myriad phenomena in their dense array.

[The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between principle and phenomena? The Master said, "East, west, south, and north. [The student] asked, "What is the dharma-realm of the non-obstruction between phenomena and phenomena?
The Master said, "Above, below, and the four intermediate directions. [One day] he ascended the hall and said: "If one pushes toward the ultimate truth, that truth has no form."
Exhausting delusion: delusion has no form; both truth and delusion are non-existent. The eyes are revealed in vast openness.
Once the eyes are revealed, what do you see? The morning sun melts the snow upon the crags; the north wind blows open the wax-plum blossoms.
Ascending the hall: To realize the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena is not yet to be called the ancestral style of the Buddhas.

To embody total function and total illumination is likewise not the essential subtlety of a patch-robed monk. You must directly break through the sturdy barrier and recognize that single aperture above.
What is this single aperture above? The spring chill is piercing; it freezes the youth to death. Ascending the hall: If you wish to know the Buddha...
"As for the place where it goes, it is simply this sound of speech itself. "Tsk! Master Fu does not recognize good from evil;

by teaching that there is a 'brightly shining and spiritually alert' self, he corrupts the men and women of people's families. Master Zhigong gave him a shout and said, "Master Fu, do not speak in such a manner!"
"Speak further. The Great Being spoke again: "Empty-handed, one grasps a hoe; walking, one rides a water buffalo.
A person passes over the bridge; the bridge flows, but the water does not flow. Master Zhigong laughed heartily and said:
"The beginning was still somewhat bearable, but the end is even more distressing for people."
Chan Master Jingyuan Huguo of this hermitage studied the Tiantai teachings for three years before leaving them to visit Yuanwu at Zhongfu.
There, he heard a monk reciting the words from Sijian’s *xiaocan*: "Since one is deluded, one must attain awakening;

since one has awakened, one must recognize delusion within awakening and awakening within delusion. When both delusion and awakening are forgotten, all dharmas are established from the state where there is neither delusion nor awakening."

Upon hearing this, the Master was filled with doubt. He immediately hurried to the Buddha Hall and, pushing open the door panels with his hands, attained a sudden and great enlightenment (*sudden awakening*).

Thereafter, he served as an attendant; his wit and eloquence burst forth with extraordinary brilliance. Yuanwu dubbed him "The Stubborn Yuan," and the attendant subsequently inscribed his own portrait with this title.
He entrusted [the work] with these words: "Throughout my life, I have spoken only of 'stubborn' Chan. When one encounters such stubbornness, it is like hitting an iron wall;
one must cast off the cage and sever the feet. Tracing it back to the Great Earth, it is pitch black.

In my later years, I have become even more blunt and direct, wielding the Vajra mallet to shatter the nests of delusion. If you wish to recognize the face of Yuanwu in the future, I shall present it all to you at once."
When Chan Master Yunbian of Nanfeng went to visit Yuanwu, as soon as he stepped through the door for his private interview, Yuanwu said, "Look under your feet.
The Master struck a pillar once. Yuanwu said, "Why do you not speak a single word that hits the mark?
The Master said, "If the teacher shakes his head, the disciple wags his tail. Yuanwu said, "Try wagging your tail for me. The Master performed a somersault and left. Yuanwu—
He laughed heartily. From this, his reputation became known. One day, while entering the city walking with monastics and laypeople, he arrived at Shilaro Lane.
Someone asked, "The lane is here; where is Shilaro? The Master raised his arm and said, "Follow me."
When Yuanwu returned to lead Zhaojue, Master Huiyuan of Lingyin went to visit him and heard Yuanwu’s general discourse (*pushe*).
Yuanwu raised the karmic cause-and-condition concerning Layman Pang’s question to Mazu: "Not being a companion to the myriad dharmas.

At that moment, Master Huiyuan attained sudden enlightenment and collapsed among the assembly. The assembly helped him up, whereupon the Master said, "I have awakened from my dream. That night, during the small *chan* (sermon), the Master came forward.

A questioner asked, "I am nakedly pure and empty, possessing not a single thing; I am as poor as a skeleton with not a single coin. My door is broken and my house is ruined. I beg the Master for relief.
Wu said, "The seven treasures and eight jewels are all seized at once. The Master said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent household.
Wu said, "If the faculty does not leave its station, one falls into a sea of poison. As soon as these words were spoken, the Master let out a shout. Wu struck him with his staff.
Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he asked, "Have you finished eating the blow? The Master shouted again. Wuzhuo shouted twice in response. The Master then bowed.
From that time on, his spiritual acumen became sharp and piercing, meeting no resistance or contradiction. Ascending the hall, he said: "How pleasant it is that mid-spring is gradually warming!
How could one bear the Cold Food Festival and Qingming? Ten thousand layers of cloud-covered mountains rise in emerald green; the wind and moon under the vast sky are noble neighbors."
Amidst flowers and willows, red and green; on the lake and sky, the waves are steady and the wind is calm.
The mountain birds on the branches chirp repeatedly and insistently, their instructions earnest and their exhortations urgent. But tell me, what exactly were they instructing and exhorting?
[The Master] strikes the meditation staff and says: "Remember this for next year’s day; it shall still be the Cold Food Festival and Qingming."
Master Wen of Hongfu ascended the hall and said: "How do you understand 'neither obscured nor falling'? Even if you understand it, you will still fall as before into the state of a wild fox.
One night, a cool wind arises from the painted horn; the bright moon fills the boat as it drifts upon the rivers and lakes."

When Chan Master Huazangmin first lectured on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* in Chengdu, he became a refuge for those studying the doctrinal teachings (*yixue*). At that time, Yuanwu resided at Zhaojue Temple;
the Master was friends with Chan Master Sheng and visited him there, where he heard Yuanwu’s informal discourse (*xiaocan*).

Yuanwu cited the karmic occasion of the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant, to which Zhaozhou commented: "It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters do not take shape..."

"The patterns and colors have already been revealed. Where, then, is the place where the patterns and colors have been revealed? Master Xi harbored doubts about this and went to enter the room of Master Xiang.

Upon entering, he asked, "What sutra does the Preceptor lecture on? Master Xi replied, "The Śūraṅgama Sūtra. Master Xiang said, "In the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, there are the 'Seven Places for Examining the Mind' and the 'Eight Reversions to Discern the Vision.
Ultimately, where does the mind reside? Master Xi presented many of his scholarly interpretations, but Master Xiang did not accept any of them.
The Master again requested further instruction. Wuzhuo told him that in all circumstances, one must manifest the "manifestation of literary patterns" (*wencai yichang*).

Later, while Huì was incidentally requesting instruction on the *Ten Mysterious Gates* (*Shixuantan*), he raised the question: "What is the appearance of the Mind-Seal (*xin-yin*)? Wuzhuo replied with a stern voice, "The manifestation of literary patterns has already appeared.

Upon hearing this, the Master attained realization and subsequently sought formal certification. Wuzhuo applied the hammer and tongs of his true style, but the Master was at a loss for what to do. One.

Ri said to Wuguo, “Master, stop citing these stories. Wait until I speak of them. Wuguo consented. The Master said, “When you habitually brandish the mallet or raise the whisk, is this not what is taught in the sutras:
‘All phenomena in all worlds, every mark that exists, are themselves the wondrously luminous true mind of bodhi’?
Wuguo laughed and said, “So you have been making your living right here all along! The Master spoke again.
When [Zhaozhou] shouted "Lower! and struck the meditation seat, was this not "returning the hearing to hear one's own nature," whereby that nature achieves the Unsurpassed Way?
Wuzu said, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras: 'The wondrous nature is perfectly luminous, transcending all names and forms'?

At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened. Wuzu left Sichuan and stayed at Jia Shan; the Master ceased his lectures and attended him there. One night, while presiding over an assembly for the monks, Wuzu raised the ancient example of the sail.

The matter had not yet been resolved. When Master [Zhaozhou] heard this but did not yet understand it, he went to seek a definitive answer. Huairang said, "Ask me. Zhaozhou repeated the previous conversation.
Huairang said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. At that moment, Zhaozhou attained complete clarity. He said to Huairang, "The ancients said it was like a single drop falling into a vast ravine;
they did not realize that the great ocean can fall into a single drop. Huairang laughed and said, "What can be done about this fellow?"
Later, he went to pay his respects to Fojian at Jiangshan. Fojian asked, "Foguo has a phrase that he never casually spoke to others;
has he ever spoken it to you? The Master said, "Shut your dog’s mouth! Fojian raised his voice and said, "This is not the principle.
The Master said, "No one is snatching away your salt and tea bag; why are you shouting? Fojian said, "If Foguo had not..."
"I shall speak for you; I shall speak for you. The Master said, "When the Abbot was in doubt, he left the monastery to seek instruction elsewhere.
Jue laughed heartily.
Zen Master Daoyuan of Zhaojue went to visit Zen Master Daowu of Dabie, whereupon he contemplated the words, "Vast emptiness—no sage."
Suddenly, he burst into laughter and said, "Dharma has been here all along. Daoyu then went to visit Foguan, who recognized his potential.
Later, he stayed with Yuanwu at Jingshan and reported his insights to him, but Yuanwu did not approve.

When Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Yunju, the Master followed him; yet although he had attained a degree of conviction, there remained a stubborn obstruction in his chest that he could not remove.
He was filled with doubt. Later, when Huìwù questioned his assembly of disciples, he asked, "When the time of birth and death arrives, what then?

A monk said, "The incense altar laughs at the Master. He then asked the Master, "What about you? The Master replied, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated. Huìwù said, "If someone asks you this, how will you respond?
As the Master was about to answer, Huìwù overawed him by saying, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated. At that moment, the Master attained thorough realization. Yuan.
Wu struck him with his fist. The Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Wu said, "What did you see that you act like this?
The Master replied, "The poisonous fist has not yet been repaid; I shall never forget it for kalpas."

Chan Master Ren of Rantang in Zhongzhu frequently visited the Tripitaka Translation Bureau to thoroughly investigate the sutras and treatises; however, he remained particularly unconvinced by the School of the Patriarchs (Chanzong).
At that time, Yuanwu was residing at Tianning Monastery. One morning, the Master went to pay him a visit while Yuanwu was conducting the "entering the room" (入室) session for the assembly.

Upon seeing him, the Master felt deep reverence and submission, yet he stepped forward with sudden resolve. Yuanwu said, "To rely on the scriptures to explain their meaning is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages."

"To depart from a single word of the Sūtras is to speak like a demon. "Quickly say it! Quickly say it! When the Master prepared to respond, Wuzhu struck him across the mouth with his fist, causing him to lose a tooth.
Thereupon, he attained great enlightenment. [Later,] he ascended the hall and said: "More than half of the spring's ninety days has passed; the weather for nurturing flowers is truly harmonious.
On the branches of the rhododendron, the song of the oriole is fine—do those of the current age perceive this? Even so..."
Thus it is. For now, as for the phrase "penetrating sound and penetrating form," how do you speak of it? "The golden bit makes the horse neigh upon the fragrant grass;
the person in the jade tower is drunk beneath the apricot blossoms on this spring day. Ascending the hall, he raised the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature, saying:
"A beauty of sixteen years embroiders slowly; beneath the purple *zhijing* flowers, the yellow oriole warbles. How pitiable, this boundless sentiment of spring’s end!"

It is all contained within the moment of halting the needle and remaining silent. On the eighth day of the fourth month in the Jia-wu year of the Chunxi era, Emperor Xiaozong issued an imperial decree for [Dahui] to enter the palace.

He was granted a seat and requested to preach the Dharma. The Emperor cited the karmic cause and condition regarding "not being a companion to the myriad dharmas" and commanded him to provide an exegesis.
The Master finished his presentation and spoke this verse: Pressing a scale-weight to extract oil—enough with idle talk and long-winded words.
With a hundred thousand strings of cash girded at the waist, one rides a crane up to Yangzhou.
Chan Master Xiang’er Yuanjue left Sichuan and traveled extensively to visit venerable masters who possessed the Way. Later, he went to Daopei to rely upon Foxing.

After some time, he entered the inner quarters to present his insights. Foxing said, “You are still far from it,” yet recognizing that he was a vessel for the Dharma, he appointed him as an attendant to oversee guests.
Whenever the Master attended upon Foxing, Foxing would invariably cite the *Lotus Sūtra*’s passage on opening, showing, awakening, and...
He entered the four characters and was commanded to speak. [The Master] said again, "Only when I nod my head vertically shall you be correct. By chance, he was dismissed for failing in his duties.
Having no one to rely upon during his period of confinement, he stayed in the home of a layman. One day, while reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:

"Furthermore, they do not know what is fire and what is the house," whereupon he attained sudden enlightenment. When his period of confinement ended and he returned to visit his teacher, Xingjian was the first to see him.
He agreed. Yuanwu subsequently received imperial permission to reside at Yunju. When the Master arrived there, he presented what he had attained to Yuanwu.
Yuanwu scolded him, saying, "This is originally a pure ground; why are you defecating here? At that moment, the Master’s doubts were suddenly resolved.
He once said to a guest: "Sudō said, 'I carry this rock back home; within my sleeves lies the Eastern Sea. Huang Valley said, 'Huichong’s misty rain, reeds, and wild geese.'"
"Sitting by me on the Xiao and Xiang rivers and Lake Dongting, wishing to call for my small boat to return home—those who see this say it is a painting;
this is the very marrow of Chan.
Master Zu Jue of Huayan at Zhongyan relied upon Yuanwu at Zhongfu. One day, he entered the room [for instruction], and Yuanwu raised [a koan]:
When Layman Daoyan was speaking, he "sat upon the tiger’s head and grasped its tail"; beneath the first phrase, he clarified the fundamental principle.
When he was silent, his sharp wit was laid bare like a flash of lightning sweeping across the sky. "How do you understand this? he asked. The Master was unable to respond;

he spent day and night investigating it until, suddenly, he attained realization. He presented a verse of his awakening, saying: "My home is atop a solitary peak; For many years it has been half-shut."

[The Master] entered the hall and lamented, "My body has already grown old; my livelihood is now entrusted to my children and grandchildren. Upon realizing this, he was granted permission [to leave]. The following day, he entered the room [of Zen Master Wuzu].
Wuzu asked again, "How did you resolve yesterday’s *kōan*? As the Master was about to respond, Wuzu shouted, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of such logic!
The Master remained for another five years, becoming increasingly bewildered and distressed. Later, while at Xixian on Mount Lu, he read...
Chan Master Fushan Yuan’s *Eliminating Dogmatic Discourse* states: "If one says that there is intimacy or distance in awakening, how could there be stinking weeds growing within a sandalwood forest?
Having attained sudden and thorough realization, he sent a verse to Yuanwu, saying: "Leaving the forest, I have returned to the weeds;
The celestial net is vast and cannot be evaded. Who would believe that karmic conditions offer no place of escape? I return home with no fear."
His voice was loud; Wù was greatly delighted. He held it up to show the assembly, saying, "I have thoroughly realized the *Avataṃsaka*.
Ascending the hall, he cited the case concerning the passing of Master Shishuang, when the assembly requested the Head Seat to succeed him as abbot, and the dialogue between him and Attendant Qián.
The Master said, "Where a true teacher acts, it is like fire melting ice; having passed through the barrier of right and wrong, the entire faculty is forgotten."

In the funeral rites, the Head Seat exhausted the Way, yet remained stuck in a single color; the Attendant’s insight surpassed his master, yet he could be said to have realized the subtle essence while losing the fundamental source, utterly confused about what to face and what to turn away from.
He did not realize that the Head Seat was like a heron standing in the snow—his species distinct, yet not in harmony with the surroundings;
the Attendant was like a phoenix soaring through the crimson heavens, unentangled by golden nets. One person stood atop a high mountain peak; the other [remained] deep...
Wandering at the bottom of the deep sea, each coming from their respective directions, they have gathered together within the ninefold city. Do you wish now to recognize these two?
(He raises the whisk. The dragon lies in the azure pool; the wind is piercingly cold. (He lowers the whisk.
The crane returns to the void; its back brushes the heavens.
Master Mingyin Tanwan ascended the hall and said: "You have a pair of eyes; I also have a pair of eyes.
If you try to deceive me, you are deceiving yourself. If you become a Buddha or an Ancestor, I, this old monk, shall have no share of that.
If you become an ass or a horse, I, this old monk, will not be able to save you. When various donors entered the mountain and requested him to ascend the hall, he spoke this verse:
He said: "I have no special attainment; it is called a hollow departure. I thank you for your earnestness in coming all this way.
Since there is no Dharma to be entrusted, I have merely opened the mountain gate for you."
Chan Master Xueting Yuanjing of Huqiu ascended the hall and said: "To speak, one must see;
to see, one must also be able to speak. If you can see but cannot speak, you fall into the realm of shadows and your understanding becomes biased and withered.
If you can speak but cannot see, you fall into the constraints of timing and descend into a sea of poison. As for those under my gate, even if they can both speak and see—excellent!"
"Thirty blows! Even if one cannot speak of it or perceive it, thirty blows are still appropriate.
Even if Cuiyun speaks thus, thirty blows are also appropriate. He then called out loudly to the assembly, "Danger!"
Master Tansou Fansi of Tianning delivered this discourse from the high seat: "Those who know there is something also eat porridge and rice;
those who do not know there is something also eat porridge and rice. How can one directly verify whether they have it or not, whether it is right or wrong, and whether it is deviant or correct?
If you cannot verify this, the matter of studying the Way remains far off. He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
[He] took his seat. ○ Ascending the hall, the Mountain Monk said: "I am the fourth-generation descendant of Yangqi.
This old fellow has a 'Three-legged Donkey Treading with its Hooves' kōan. Although everyone can recite it, they simply do not know where it lands.
The Mountain Monk, without sparing a hair of his eyebrows, shall provide a footnote for you all. He then said: "An octagonal millstone runs through the void."
Master Jue of Mount Jun ascended the hall and cited an ancient saying: "The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems; the more one drills into it, the harder it becomes.
Looking for it, it is right in front; suddenly, it is behind. Do you all recognize this? If you do not, I shall explain it for you:

"The more one looks up at it, the higher it seems"—not separated by so much as a hair’s breadth. The critical ford is held fast; even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot escape it. "The more one drills into it..."
Firm and solid; the true essence is spontaneous. The birds sing and the flowers bloom before the green cliffs. Looking for it as if it were in front, it is neither correct nor biased.
It cuts off the ten directions and its majesty subdues the great chiliocosm. Suddenly it is behind—what a leakage!
How laughable that Yunmen hides his body in the Big Dipper. *Duḥ!* (A shout of realization)
Master Baohua Xian ascended the hall and said: "Do not investigate Chan; cease studying the Way. Rest the mind and let go of contrivance, for it is ever vast and open.
The ready-made case is already a cumbersome entanglement; even this very 'no-mind' is already a fabrication.
Even if you could sit and cut off all existence prior to birth, it would still be difficult to penetrate my 'Wrong! Wrong! Wrong!'"

Chan Master Jue of Dongshan ascended the hall and said: "In the past, the butcher Guang'e went to where the Buddha was, cast down his butcher's knife, and declared, 'I am counted among the thousand Buddhas.
The World-Honored One said, 'So it is, so it is.

Today, those in the monastic communities assume that Guang'e was actually one Buddha who manifested as a butcher by means of expedient means. To see Guang'e in such a way would indeed be cause for joy."
"No connection. Again he said: "Guang'e is precisely a man who does not blink when killing people; yet he cast down his butcher's blade and became a Buddha on the spot.
For now, let us say there is no connection. He further said: "Guang'e cast down his butcher's blade and said, 'I am counted among the thousand Buddhas.
How distinct this one Buddha is! For now, let us say there is no connection. If you wish to know Guang..."
"E-ma! After wind and rain have passed over the peach blossoms along the road, where can a horse’s hoof avoid the lingering petals?
Xu Fu, the Grand Councilor and known as the Layman of East Lake, served as a Minister of the Interior at the beginning of the Jingkang era.
Together with like-minded court officials, he hung his alms bowl in Zemo Hall at Tianning Temple and applied himself diligently to the study under Yuanwu. Yuanwu, for his part, was also pleased."
His realization was transcendent. One day, he went to the office of the Secretary (Shuji) and pointed to Wuzhu’s crown, saying, “This old fellow’s heels have not yet touched the ground.
Wuzhu turned his face away and said, “How could a turtle ever escape from inside a jar?
The official replied, “I am glad that this old fellow’s heels have finally touched the ground. Wuzhu said, “Do not slander him. The official then withdrew.
The Prince of Jun, Zhao Lingjin, was styled the Layman Chaoran.

In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Shaoxing era, the Duke, along with Grand Secretary Wang Zao, Vice President of the Council Li Bing, and Minister of Rites Zeng Kai, visited Mount Jing to pay their respects to Dahui.

Upon hearing of their arrival, Dahui ordered the drum to be beaten for a private interview. The Duke joyfully approached him, incense in his sleeve. Dahui said: "Regarding the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl..."
The scholar asked, "How do you understand this? Huangbo said, "What bowl are you looking for? and brushed his sleeves, about to leave.
Huairang rose and grabbed him, saying, "The ancients attained enlightenment right here; why do you not attain it?
As the scholar was about to respond, Huairang struck him and said, "What bowl are you looking for? The scholar said, "Only then can I be this old man."
The Vice Minister Li Mīxùn was styled the Layman Pǔxiàn. Serving as a Secretariat Drafter, he frequently entered the room of Yuánwù.
One day, returning from the morning court audience, his horse leaped as he reached Tiānjīn Bridge, and he suddenly attained realization; sweat poured from his entire body.

He went straight to Tiānníng Monastery, where it happened that Yuánwù was stepping out the gate. Seeing him from afar, Yuánwù called out, "Layman, rejoice! You have completed the Great Matter. The official [responded].

He spoke in a stern voice, saying, "What is this, Master, that you are causing your eyes to dazzle? Wuzhuo then gave a shout, and the official also shouted. Thus, their spiritual sparks met with swift and sharp agility.
There was a lady named Lady Fan of Chengdu who had lived as a widow for many years; she sat constantly and did not lie down. Having heard that Yuanwu was residing at Zhaojue...

Jue went to pay his respects and requested instruction on the causes and conditions for entering the Way. Wuzhuo told him to contemplate: "It is not the mind, it is not the Buddha, it is not an object—what is this?
For a long time, Jue could find no point of realization. Fan wept and said to Wuzhuo, "Master, what expedient means do you have that might allow me to understand more easily?
Wuzhuo replied, "I do indeed have an expedient means. He then instructed him to simply continue contemplating: "What is this?"
Later, there was a verse of realization that said: "I have finally realized how near it all has been!
Chan Master Wenshu Xindao went to Chengdu to study *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (The Treatise on Consciousness-Only), believing he had reached the ultimate understanding.

A fellow student challenged him, saying: "The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only. Yet now, before our eyes, the myriad phenomena are vividly manifest. Where, then, is this 'mind' or 'consciousness'?"
The Master was utterly bewildered and did not know how to respond. He subsequently left the pass and wandered through the Jianghuai region.

Upon arriving at Taiping in Shu, he heard Chan Master Fojian’s night discourse, in which he raised the story of Zhaozhou’s “Cypress Tree” and cited Jue Tiezui, who said, “The former master did not say such words;
do not slander the former master. This caused him to fall into great doubt. After a long period of sustained inquiry, one night he attained sudden enlightenment. Immediately—
He hurried to the Master’s quarters, intending to recount his realization. As soon as Huayan Jue saw him approaching, he closed the door. The Master said, "Master, do not deceive me.
Jue replied, "The ten directions have no walls; why do you not enter through the door? The Master then punched a hole in the window paper.
Jian immediately opened the door, grabbed him, and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master struck Jian on the head with both hands, spat at him, and departed.
He then presented this verse: "Zhaozhou has a story about the cypress tree; Zen practitioners have transmitted it throughout the world.
Most pick at the leaves and search for the branches, Unable to understand it directly at its very source. Master Jue says there is no such word."
This is precisely reviling with evil words in one’s face. If a Chan practitioner possesses the eye that penetrates all quarters, they should skillfully discern the true from the false within this.
Jiandeng agreed with this. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The lion yawns; the elephant king roars.
Yunmen hides his body within the Big Dipper. Why did Baiyun call it 'a hand'? The Buddhas of the three periods do not know its existence. The wildcat..."
The ox, however, knows that there is. But tell me, what is this matter of his knowing that there is? Rain beats upon the pear blossoms as butterflies fly;
the wind blows the willow catkins as they roll away like balls of wool.
Chan Master Nanhua Bing ascended the hall and said: "This matter is most extraordinary; it is not obstructed by direct speech.

The old farmer next door has, according to custom, obtained a piece of it. It not only penetrates sound and form, but also accords with the seasons. If you ask what school this belongs to, the eight characters do not apply to anyone.
He struck the meditation seat and descended. Ascending the hall again, he said: "Delusion does not delude itself; it is in response to..."

Awakening establishes delusion. Awakening does not awaken itself; it is because of delusion that awakening is spoken of. Thus, awakening is the substance of delusion, and delusion is the function of awakening.
Both delusion and awakening have no origin; within this, there is neither distinction nor commonality. Without distinction or commonality, it cannot be moved by a brushstroke.
The Patriarch did not bring it here; its nostrils weigh a thousand catties.
Master Longya Cai had served diligently at the Dharma seat of Fojian from an early age, never shying away from administrative duties;
his reputation was already renowned throughout the monastic community. As he traveled on pilgrimage toward evening, he arrived at Huanglong, where it happened that Sisi was at the main gate.
When asked where he had come from, he gave his name, and it was immediately recognized that he was Master Cai, the steward of Taiping in Shuzhou. The following day—
[The Master] entered the room. Sīxìn asked, "If you understand the first phrase, you understand the final phrase;
if you understand the final phrase, you understand the first phrase. Setting aside both the first and the final, how do you understand the story of Baizhang’s wild fox?
The Master said, "I already knew his understanding upon entering the door; why must one tread further in the mud? Sīxìn [nodded].
Xin Changlao said, "Death is in the hands of the Senior Elder. The Master said, "Though the words differ, the ultimate principle is without discrepancy.
Xin Changlao asked, "What is this matter that is without discrepancy? The Master replied, "If one does not strike the horn of Huanglong, how can one know the pearl beneath its chin?
Xin Changlao then struck him. Ascending the hall, he cited the small assembly talk of Master Sixin, which said: "If one were to discuss..."
This matter is like a man who has three sons. The first son is intelligent and wise; he filially supports his parents, receives guests and visitors, and manages the family estate.
The second son is fierce, stubborn, and crafty; he is greedy for lust and addicted to wine, lying drunk in the streets and alleys, and ruining the family estate.
The third son is blind, deaf, and mute; he cannot distinguish between beans and wheat, and is incapable of such tasks. In this regard—
"Yes. I can only eat my meals. Among these three people, Huanglong wished to select one for use. Furthermore, there are four phrases:
"life within death," "death within life," "constant death within death," and "constant life within life. He used these four phrases to test the monks of the world.
The Master said, "What do you call these 'four phrases'? What are the surnames and given names of these three people? If [you can answer]..."
If you recognize this, you will walk hand-in-hand with Huanglong, without the slightest gap between you.
If this is not yet the case, I cannot help but offer this "water and flowers. The three persons share one body; their function is no function. The four lines share one sound;
they are both empty and not empty. If you wish to know these three persons and the four lines: when the golden bird first rises, it is a mass of red.
Chan Master Penglai Qing ascended the hall and said: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. Let the various quarters nod their heads as they will.
But when the tree falls and the vine withers, there is no plan to pierce the heavens above, nor any stratagem to enter the earth below.
O sharp-witted ones, if you can fix a single eye here, you will see it extending freely in all directions. He raised his whisk and said, "Look!"
Look! One song, two songs—no one understands them. After the rain, the autumn waters in the night pond are deep.

Chan Master Fodeng Xun studied under Chan Master Guangjian Ying without attaining realization. He then went to Taiping Monastery to join the assembly and seek instruction, yet he made no progress whatsoever.
Thereupon, he sealed his bedding and vowed: "If I do not attain thorough penetration in this life, I swear never to unfold these."
Thereupon, he sat by day and stood by night as if mourning the loss of his parents.

After more than seven weeks had passed, Master Fojiàn suddenly ascended the hall and said, "The myriad phenomena, including the entire universe, are all sealed by a single Dharma. Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
He went to see Fojiàn, who said, "What a pity that this bright pearl was picked up by such a madman! He then questioned him, saying, "Lingyun said..."
"From the moment he first saw the peach blossoms until now, he has not doubted further. What is it that he does not doubt?
The Master said, "Do not say that Lingyun no longer doubts; even now, if you try to find a place of doubt, it is utterly unobtainable. Jueyan said:
Xuansha said, "It is truly so, it is most truly so; yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate. Where was it that he had not yet reached the ultimate?
The Master said, "I deeply understand how the Venerable One’s compassionate heart is so earnest. Xuansha acknowledged this. As the Master rose from his prostrations, he presented a verse, saying:
"All day long I gaze at the sky without lifting my head; Only when the peach blossoms are in full bloom do I raise my eyes. Even if you were to have more than this..."
"The Celestial Net. Once you have penetrated the secure barrier, you may then rest. [The Master] instructed Yuanjing to protect and uphold [the teaching].
That evening, he spoke to the assembly in a stern voice, saying, "This time, Upāsaka Xun shall sleep soundly. When Yuanwu heard this, he suspected it was not yet so and said:
"I must first examine him before I can accept him. He then sent someone to summon him. While they were wandering the mountains together, they happened upon a mountain pond.
Huineng pushed the Master into the water and suddenly asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou saw the Fourth Patriarch?

The Master replied, "The pool is deep, so the fish gather. Huineng asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master replied, "The tree is tall, so it draws in the wind. Huineng asked, "As for seeing and not seeing..."
"How is it at the moment of seeing? The Master said, "The extended foot is within the tucked-in foot. Wuda praised this.
Ascending the hall, he raised the story of the old woman burning the hermitage. The Master said, "In general, to support the school and establish the teaching, one must be such a person.
Look at that old woman; though she was but a woman, she possessed the strategic insight of a great man. For twenty years she strained oil and wasted sauce."
This is indeed understandable. One day, at the top of a hundred-foot pole, one must make a leap into the void, exhausting all the strength of one’s lifelong efforts.
Unless one is a man of the world who understands the opportune moment, this will not happen until skill is exhausted and the clumsy emerges.
Even so, do you wish to understand? Only after the snowfall does one know the steadfast nature of the pine and cypress; only when faced with difficulty does one see the true man.
Mind. Chan Master Létán Míng ascended the hall and, citing the karmic conditions of Zhaozhou’s visit to Zhunü to "probe the water," the Master said:
"Old Zhao, as the clouds gather, the mountains and peaks are revealed; after the rain at Zhunü, the wind through the bamboo is clear. In whose private villa, within the pond, [does this occur]?"
Unable to finish painting a pair of mandarin ducks, he again brought up the story of Deshan’s alms-bowl. The Master said:

"From of old, when a family is wealthy, the children are spoiled; they head toward the Jiangnan region to dangle their painted oars. This draws the old lord to his loss of self-control, coming aboard the boat to join in the singing."
Chan Master Baozang ascended the hall and said: "More than ten days have passed since Qingming; the rain of flowers has ceased, and the depths of one's heart are profound.
Spring colors vex the mind, making sleep impossible; a yellow oriole flies past the green willow shade. He then laughed loudly and descended from his seat.

When Chan Master Hai Xiangyu first met Fojian, Fojian asked, "If the Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed up in a single mouth, where else could there be sentient beings to be taught?
What is the principle of this? As the Master was about to offer a reply, Fojian shouted at him.
The Master suddenly attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "The reality-limit has never received any dust; Within it, there is neither old nor new."
"The green mountains are, moreover, the property of my own house; there is no need to seek out another home or ask for the ford.
Jian said, "Put it down. The Master bowed and departed.
Chan Master Jingzhong Can ascended the hall: "On the ninth day of the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh; a single phrase is luminously pervasive from antiquity."
Now, Yang Guang’s camel is nowhere to be found; last night its tracks were seen beneath the pines.
(End of Volume 19 of the *Huìyuán*).
Chan Master Zhūān Shìguī of Lóngxiáng first relied upon Dàcí Zōngyǎ; his mind was intoxicated by the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* for over five years.
In the autumn, he traveled south to visit various venerable masters. Upon first ascending Longmen, he reported his usual realizations to Foyan.
Foyan said, "Your understanding of the mind is already ultimate; you simply lack the effort required to open your eyes. He was subsequently appointed to the office of the Hall Superintendent.
One day, while standing in attendance, Foyan asked, "What is it like when all dualities are transcended? Foyan replied, "It is like the announcement made in your Sangha hall."
Zhui was at a loss for words. Later that evening, when Yan arrived at the Hall Office, the Master brought up their previous conversation. Yan said, "Idle talk.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. During the Shaoxing era, he received an imperial decree to open the mountain monastery of Nengren on Mount Yanwang.
At that time, Zhenxie was residing at Jiangxin. Upon hearing that the Master had arrived, he feared that the conditions for his Dharma affinity were not yet ripe;

thus, he personally crossed the river to welcome him back to the Abbot’s quarters and performed nine full prostrations to entice the people of Wenzhou. Consequently, they all turned toward him with great enthusiasm and reverence.

Before the Master had even assumed office, his disciples, fearing the strict enforcement of monastic regulations, set fire to the monastery in the dead of night, reducing it to a heap of bricks and rubble. The Master, however, ultimately settled under trees and constructed a dwelling from them.
Ascending the seat, he addressed the assembly, saying: "I have grown weary of leisure and shall no longer beat the drum of Gushan; in my old age, I have come to see Mount Yandang.
The magnificent pavilions and lofty towers are entirely gone; by the stream stand but two or three thatched huts. He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
The patrons who had heard the Dharma joined their efforts in the construction, and before long, it was restored as a magnificent monastery.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Luminously clear, there is no awakening; where there is a dharma, there is delusion.
You people cannot stand here; you people cannot dwell here. If you stand, you are precarious; if you dwell, you are blind.

You must simply ensure that the mind does not rest in the mysterious, the phrase does not rest in the mind, and function does not rest in the trigger. Once these three are clarified, there is no need to manage anything anywhere."
It manifests spontaneously; there is no need for deliberate attention, for it is naturally clear.
Even so, one must further know that there is a matter beyond this. Long rain, no clearing. *Pfft!* Ascending the hall: When seeing is seen, that seeing is not seeing.
Even seeing is already detached from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. The fallen flower has the intention to follow the flowing water, yet the flowing water is without sentiment for the fallen flower.
All things that can be returned are naturally not you. That which does not return to you—what else could it be?
"Long have I lamented that spring departs with no place to be found; I did not know it had turned and entered into this very midst. With a shout, he said: "Thirty years hence!"
Do not say that the teachings of the Benevolent One (Śākyamuni) ruin people's families.
Chan Master Wuguang of Yunju possessed innate wisdom; upon hearing Chan Master Chong cite the anecdote of Emperor Wu’s question to Bodhidharma, he felt as if he had recovered a long-lost object.
He immediately said, "Since I am already vast and empty, what 'saint' could there be? Chong was struck by his words.
"Exert yourself in your southern pilgrimage. He received a prediction of enlightenment at Longmen. One day, a monk had his foot bitten by a snake.
Foyan asked, "Since this is Longmen, why was he bitten by a snake? The Master replied, "Indeed, the marks of a great man have appeared.
Foyan further esteemed him for this. Later, when these words reached Zhaojue, Yuanwu said, "Longmen has..."
Is this not a monk? The Dharma path of Dongshan has not yet become desolate.
Chan Master Zhong of Huanglong Muan studied the Tiantai teachings and attained realization of the principle of the three contemplations within one mind.

Unable to remain hidden from view, he traveled extensively to consult renowned masters. Upon reaching Longmen, he observed a water mill turning and thereby clarified the essential point of the mind, subsequently composing a verse.
[Guishan] said, "Turning the Great Dharma Wheel—enveloped right before one's eyes. [Yangshan] asked further, "How is it? [Guishan] replied, "Water pushes a stone mill; presenting the Buddha-eye.
Yangshan asked, "What is the matter within it? The Master said, "The water flows long in the mountain stream.
Yangshan said, "I have a final phrase; I shall entrust it to you. The Master immediately covered his ears and departed. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "Do not seek it outside. [The student] asked, "What is the mind? The Master said, "Do not search for it outside. [The student] asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "Do not look for it outside. [The student] asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "Do not transmit it outside.
[The student] asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Svāhā in a place of stillness."
Chan Master Xuedang Xing of Wugu ascended the hall and said: "If you understand, then you understand; the jade is naturally without flaw.
If you say you do not understand, the pestle’s tip has sprouted flowers. Let me ask: how does nine years of facing the wall compare to the Great Assembly’s picking up of the flower?
Nanming, to deliberate in such a manner is merely to scatter sand with the wind. *Cen* (Examine)! Arriving at Guoqing, the assembly requested him to ascend the hall. He said: "A phrase..."

Sweep away! The meaning is also swept away. At the point where a hair’s breadth or a cowhair’s tip is severed, it is like a mountain, like a peak. The phrase has arrived; the meaning has also arrived.

At the point like a mountain, like a peak, where a hair’s breadth or a cowhair’s tip is severed, suddenly, as if a single thread were forced open, both meaning and phrase arrive and yet neither arrives;
both are swept away and yet neither is swept away. One reaches the state where there is no entanglement beyond the three phrases, and no target to be aimed at beyond the six phrases.
At this very moment, how do you express it in a single phrase? "Though we meet under the same canopy, our paths diverge; together we shall take each other’s hands and ascend the high terrace.
Entering the hall, he raised the example of Zhaozhou addressing the assembly: "The old monk has nothing to do except for the two meals of rice gruel and porridge;
these are the only occasions where my mind is distracted. The Master said: "Today is the first day of the sixth month. The attendant strikes the drum; the Elder ascends the seat."

The Hall Master said: "All of you are here together, applying your minds in a confused manner. Chan Master Baiyang Shun, who had relied upon Foyan, heard a general discourse (pusuo) in which Foyan cited the *Mind-King Inscription* by Dashi Fu: "The mind-king is originally bright; It does not wait for conditions to arise. If one seeks it through the six senses, It is like looking for a thief in an empty house.

If one can see the thief within the empty house, Then the thief will naturally vanish on its own. If one seeks it through the six senses, It is like looking for a thief in an empty house. If one can see the thief within the empty house, Then the thief will naturally vanish on its own."
"The flavor of salt in water; the indigo in the lacquer. It is certainly there, yet its form is not seen. Upon these words, the Master attained realization.
Later, while observing the rapid turning of the jewel-treasury, he suddenly clarified the Great Dharma. He hurried to the master’s chamber, prostrated himself, and presented this verse:
Clouds drift slowly over the unique peaks at the summit; streams flow coolly from the source without branching.
Though one wanders the mountains, failing to reach their very end, in the end the green mountains will obstruct the eyes. The eyes smile and grant approval. Ascending the hall for instruction:
Good things arrive in piles upon piles; there is no need for fabrication or arrangement. Yellow leaves falling in the forest are swept away by the water; white clouds crossing the valley...
Clouds and wind swirl back; with a single cry from a cold wild goose, all sentiment and thought are severed. As soon as the frost-bell strikes, my mountain crumbles.
Yet the white poplar tree has a quality that surpasses others: throughout the night, it stirs the dead embers in its cold hearth. Suddenly, a monk comes forth and says:
The old man is fond of showing off his wares; he has ended up with such a state of utter poverty. I simply told him, "Yet you have hit upon it. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"What is my hand like? It is like the Buddha’s hand. The Southern Star and the Northern Dipper are in the heavens.
What are my feet like? They are like a donkey’s feet. All past affairs have been forgotten. Every person has their own karmic origins; each one is complete with square feet and a rounded head."
Perfect. Standing on the banks of the Dayu Rapids, the solitary moon’s reflection falls upon the deep cove. It cannot be grasped; it is difficult even to see.
A single strain of a fisherman’s song passes over the distant shoals. Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind blows through the thatched roof, leaking within;

the rain beats upon the *kalyāṇamitra*’s eyes, making them moist. Thus clearly evident, yet one does not know it; one comes here to stand with bowed head. (At that time, the monk Shao Deng heard this.)
As for Master Shou of Yunju, he disciplined himself with austere purity. Whether entering or leaving, he traveled alone, relying only on his staff and straw raincoat.
Having studied under various masters of the various schools throughout Zhejiang, he eventually arrived at Longmen. There, he reported to Foyan what he had realized during his daily practice.
Foyan said, "These are all merely intellectual understandings; they are not the ultimate matter. If you wish to resolve the question of birth and death, you must seek [the true teacher]."

Miaowu was struck with awe and believed it with deep sincerity. One day, the Master ordered him to take charge of the Xiangji (Fragrant Accumulation) Hall; Miaowu firmly declined on the grounds that his spiritual practice was not yet complete.
Foyan urged him, saying, "Go ahead and take up the post for now; there are many within it who will preach the Dharma for you.
